Published Project Description: Jonesborough Locally Grown (JLG) is a 501(c)(3) non-profit that connects farmers, food, and the community to grow a vibrant local food system. JLG operates two markets: Boone Street Market (BSM), a year-round local foods store, and Jonesborough Farmers Market (JFM), a tailgate farmers market. Both are producer-only that source primarily within 100 miles of Jonesborough, TN. JLG keeps fees low to benefit the vendor and supports over 100 vendors, many of whom are small or beginning farmers. JLG markets operate with significant volunteer support, donations and fundraisers – somewhat unreliable labor and funding sources, as the COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated. For the long-term financial stability of BSM and JFM and viability of JLG vendors, sales must increase to avoid radically changing the low vendor fee structure JLG currently employs. JLG was awarded a FMPP grant in 2018, allowing the start of an intensive marketing campaign. The previous grant was successful despite challenges presented by the pandemic, but rising inflation and overhead costs have increased the sales threshold required to sustain JLG markets. This project builds on the sampling and advertising elements of the previous project – and adds an important consumer demand: online ordering. With FMPP funds to support these initiatives, sales at BSM and JFM are projected to increase 15% by the end of the project period. Increasing sales in addition to foot traffic and retaining vendors are key to the long-term financial stability of BSM and JFM – and, therefore, the sustainability of the farmers and vendors supported by JLG markets.
llm_summary: Jonesborough Locally Grown (JLG) is undertaking a strategic project designed to enhance the viability and expand the reach of its two markets, Boone Street Market and Jonesborough Farmers Market, with the primary purpose of increasing sales and ensuring the long-term sustainability of the organization and the farmers it supports. This project will focus on implementing an online ordering system to facilitate increased sales at both locations, building upon previous sampling and advertising efforts, and anticipates a 15% increase in sales by the end of the project period. JLG will utilize FMPP funds to develop and implement this online ordering system, which is expected to attract new consumers and provide existing customers with increased convenience. The anticipated outcomes include strengthened sales figures at both BSM and JFM, leading to greater financial stability for JLG and the farmers who rely on the markets. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers and ranchers who supply products to the markets, as well as the consumers seeking locally sourced agricultural goods. JLG aims to support these stakeholders by broadening market access and bolstering sales volume, ultimately improving the overall health and operational capacity of the Jonesborough Farmers Market and Boone Street Market. This initiative directly addresses the need for expanded market channels for agricultural products, promoting the growth of the local food system and the success of the participating vendors.

Published Project Description: Through this project, the Mother Road Farmers Market in Winslow, Arizona, will: Develop, coordinate, and expand local direct producer-to-consumer markets; Increase access to locally grown agricultural products; and Support small farms, new and beginning farmers, and/or underserved producers. The project will establish a full-time Farmers Market Coordinator to support current vendors, add additional food vendors (targeting produce), create programs, promote the market to the community, and evaluate project activities. Expected outcomes are to increase the amount of locally grown produce and food products available to residents by adding 10 produce vendors and creating a consignment program; increase income for local growers – with a focus on small, new, and/or under resourced growers; and improve access to fresh, locally grown food for low-income residents, which includes the community’s Indigenous and Hispanic populations.
llm_summary: Through the Mother Road Farmers Market in Winslow, Arizona, this project aims to develop, coordinate, and expand local direct producer-to-consumer markets, significantly increasing access to locally grown agricultural products. The core of this initiative involves establishing a full-time Farmers Market Coordinator to support current vendors, introduce an additional ten produce vendors, and implement a consignment program for local growers. Anticipated outcomes include increased income for farmers and ranchers involved in the market, alongside improved access to fresh produce for residents. Specifically, the project focuses on providing increased market opportunities for growers, processors, and stakeholders within the Winslow community, with a particular emphasis on expanding the availability of locally sourced agricultural commodities. The project seeks to bolster the supply chain by facilitating direct sales between producers and consumers. This will create a more robust system for distributing goods. The primary beneficiaries of this project include the farmers and ranchers who will participate in the market, as well as the consumers who will have greater access to locally grown produce. The project will also benefit those involved in the processing and distribution of these agricultural goods. Ultimately, the Mother Road Farmers Market will contribute to a more reliable supply of fresh agricultural products for the Winslow community, strengthening local food systems and supporting economic activity within the region.

Organizaton: Nalwoodi Denzhone: Strength and Beauty Community, Inc.
Published Project Description: This project will address the economic hardships facing the San Carlos Apache communities by building the Tribe’s capacity of supporting local-food enterprises with direct producer-to-consumer marketing technical assistance. Project activities include creating a marketing plan, the development of regional networks supporting local-food aggregation and distribution, establishing operation policies, food safety plans, standard operating procedures required for a successful direct producer-to-consumer marketing. Project deliverables will be utilized in the provision of targeted technical assistance and training to beginning and socially disadvantaged farmers, ranchers, and food businesses as a form of job/career training for Apache people. Project outcomes include a strengthened regional food economy on the San Carlos Apache Reservation, increased access to and consumption of local food, and job creation spurred by related economic development.
llm_summary: The San Carlos Apache project aims to strengthen the economic viability of the San Carlos Apache community through the development of local-food enterprises, focusing on direct producer-to-consumer marketing. This initiative will create a comprehensive marketing plan and establish regional networks for the aggregation and distribution of locally produced agricultural commodities, including organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, and other rotational crops. Key elements of the project involve the creation of operational policies, the implementation of food safety plans, and the establishment of standard operating procedures necessary for successful direct producer-to-consumer marketing. The anticipated outcomes include a strengthened regional food economy and increased access to and consumption of locally grown agricultural products by farmers, ranchers, and consumers. Ultimately, this project seeks to spur economic development within the San Carlos Apache community, generating opportunities for those involved in food production and related businesses. The project will prioritize the development of viable pathways for the production and distribution of a range of agricultural commodities, contributing to a more robust and self-sufficient local food system. The project will benefit all stakeholders involved in the production, processing, and distribution of these commodities, supporting economic growth and enhancing food security for the San Carlos Apache community.

Published Project Description: The purpose of the People’s Produce Mobile Farmers Market is to bring healthy, fairly-priced, locally-grown produce and other nutritious foods to low-income residents and food assistance beneficiaries using a refrigerated food truck operated by Project New Village, a 501(3)(c) grassroots nonprofit. The project’s service area will encompass eight weekly sites throughout Greater Southeastern San Diego, including the City of San Diego’s Promise Zone, the City of Lemon Grove, and National City. The project will provide a food retail shopping experience to consumers, meeting them at natural points of service such as libraries, YMCAs, community clinics, church parking lots, and other community-oriented gathering spaces. This project will improve equitable access to good food, which Project New Village defines as food that is: sustainable, healthy, affordable, and accessible to all residents. The project will engage new small farmers and producers, conduct culturally-competent marketing activities to market healthy food products and promote food assistance programs, reaching more than 15,000 customers.
llm_summary: Project New Village’s People’s Produce Mobile Farmers Market is designed to increase equitable access to good food for residents of Greater Southeastern San Diego. This project will operate a refrigerated food truck, offering a retail shopping experience at eight weekly locations throughout the City of San Diego’s Promise Zone, the City of Lemon Grove, and National City, including sites such as libraries, YMCAs, community clinics, and church parking lots. The primary goal of this initiative is to provide consumers with access to sustainably produced, healthy, and affordable food items, with a particular focus on expanding market pathways for domestically produced organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes and other rotational crops, and organic ingredients. Anticipated outcomes include reaching more than 15,000 customers and supporting the growth of local producers and processors involved in the supply chain. The project directly benefits residents of the targeted communities by providing a convenient source of fresh food and by supporting the growth of organic agricultural commodities. Producers and stakeholders will be supported through the project, creating a network of farmers and food providers. The project aims to facilitate the availability of nutritious food to consumers seeking a reliable source of fresh produce and other food items, representing a valuable contribution to the region’s food system.

Organizaton: Central Coast Ag Network dba City Farm SLO
Published Project Description: “Scaling and Expanding San Luis Obispo (SLO) County Farmer Collaborative Partnerships” will measurably address major local and regional barriers to central coast farmers as well as vulnerable/underserved/ socially disadvantaged (low income- low access) communities relating to equitable and inclusive market opportunities and consumer access. This project will build a Farmer Collaborative that offers sustained supportive services and trainings to empower, and benefit limited resource, beginning, socially disadvantaged, and veteran farmers. In addition, the project will collaborate with Harvestly to expand online sales and Slow Money SLO to integrate farmers with the SLO County Farm to School Program. This project provides capacity needed to unify small-scale, new/ beginning farmers and ranchers, as well as underserved/ socially disadvantaged and veteran producer/ consumer communities. Direct beneficiaries include current and future City Farm SLO tenants participating in the Farmer Collaborative, SLO County Farmers, consumers, school districts, and the regional economy. The project’s work plan acts as a strategic and structural backbone to growing partnerships in a way that enables farmers to share administrative, knowledge, equipment, and other resources. The project also provides farmers access to extensive trainings, toolkits, onboarding, marketing, and support services. It is intended that this project will act as a pilot demonstration that can be rapidly adopted, replicated, and scaled throughout the County.
llm_summary: Scaling and Expanding San Luis Obispo (SLO) County Farmer Collaborative Partnerships aims to measurably address critical barriers faced by farmers and consumers within the central coast region, specifically focusing on expanding equitable market opportunities and consumer access. This project will establish a Farmer Collaborative designed to provide sustained supportive services to limited resource, beginning, and veteran farmers, alongside facilitating collaborations with Harvestly to expand online sales and Slow Money SLO to integrate farmers with the SLO County Farm to School Program. The project’s core function will be to unify small-scale, new, and beginning farmers and ranchers, as well as supporting consumer engagement with local agricultural products. Direct beneficiaries include current and future City Farm SLO tenants, SLO County Farmers, consumers, school districts, and key stakeholders within the regional economy. The project will focus on building a robust infrastructure that enables farmers to share administrative resources, knowledge, and equipment, significantly enhancing operational efficiency. Furthermore, the project will provide access to comprehensive support services, including onboarding assistance and marketing support. The anticipated outcomes include increased access to markets for SLO County agricultural products and the establishment of sustainable partnerships among producers and consumers. The project seeks to foster a stronger local food system through the collective action of farmers and consumers, creating a more resilient and connected agricultural community.

Published Project Description: The project seeks to strengthen the regional food system infrastructure in Siskiyou County, CA by expanding the Mount Shasta Farmer’s Market and providing development opportunities for the area’s beginning farmers. Through collaboration with other organizations and farmers’ markets, and by supporting the business development of small-scale farmers and producers, this project seeks to strengthen the role of regional farmers’ markets in the direct-to-consumer supply chain while also supporting the development of beginning farmers. Project goals include increasing the number of customers patronizing the Mount Shasta Farmers’ Market, actively integrating beginning farmers/producers into the market, facilitating the creation of  new value-added products, providing workshops on subjects identified by project stakeholders, identifying opportunities for regional farmers’ markets to collaborate, and creating new organizations focused on outreach to new customers.
llm_summary: The Mount Shasta Farmer’s Market project seeks to strengthen the regional food system infrastructure in Siskiyou County, CA, by expanding the market’s operations and providing development opportunities for beginning farmers. This project will focus on increasing the number of customers patronizing the Mount Shasta Farmers’ Market and actively integrating these beginning farmers/producers into the market’s offerings. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of new value-added products through the efforts of local processors and ranchers, as well as the identification of opportunities for collaboration among regional farmers’ markets. The project aims to support the growth of a more robust direct-to-consumer supply chain, benefiting farmers, consumers, and other stakeholders within the community. Specifically, the project will support the development of new products and facilitate connections between producers and consumers. This will directly impact the availability of organic grains and livestock feed, and organic dairy, fibers, legumes, and other rotational crops currently available within the region. Ultimately, the project intends to bolster the overall strength of the local food system, creating a more sustainable and accessible pathway for producers to reach their markets, while satisfying consumer demand for locally sourced agricultural commodities. The project will prioritize the development of new organizations focused on outreach to new customers and strengthening the connections within the local food network.

Published Project Description: This project will sustain and build the capacity of El Mercado, a California-certified, seasonal, and health-centric farmer’s market located in an area with concentrated poverty, limited access to supermarkets or locally grown food, and high rates of health disparities. The project’s goals are to build the long-term organizational capacity of El Mercado by doubling the foot traffic, number of agricultural producers, and average gross sales over a three-year period. Project activities will focus on increasing foot traffic through consumer- centric marketing efforts and community engagement, and subsequently growing the number of participating California-certified agricultural producers. The project will enable the expansion of a direct producer-to-consumer market, increasing access to and availability of locally and regionally produced agricultural products.
llm_summary: El Mercado will sustain and build the capacity of this California-certified, seasonal, and health-centric farmer’s market operating in an area experiencing concentrated poverty and limited access to locally grown food. The project’s purpose is to significantly enhance the market’s operational strength by achieving a three-year goal of doubling foot traffic, expanding the number of participating agricultural producers, and increasing average gross sales. Specifically, the project will focus on growing the direct producer-to-consumer market, thereby increasing the availability of locally and regionally produced agricultural products. This expansion will benefit farmers, ranchers, and processors by creating increased market opportunities for their goods. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened market infrastructure capable of supporting greater volumes of agricultural products. Ultimately, El Mercado aims to positively impact consumers seeking fresh food options within the community. This project will support a wider range of agricultural goods, including grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, and organic legumes, catering to the needs of various stakeholders. By increasing the volume of locally sourced products available, El Mercado will address a critical need for expanded market pathways for these agricultural commodities. The overall impact will be a more robust local food system, better serving the needs of the community and supporting the growth of agricultural production within the region.

Published Project Description: The project will bring together a multidisciplinary team to Shepard a group of Colorado agricultural producer through a process to identify available consumer markets, assess each operation’s challenges and opportunities, and map a process to successfully reach the market(s) that best fits each operation. Project deliverables include a toolkit for producers to enhance their market strategy within modern marketing frameworks, and a facilitated information exchange between farmers and partners specializing in aggregating and advertising local farm produce. Project outcomes include enabling local farms to maximize their capacity, reach new markets, and expand their presence in incumbent markets.
llm_summary: AMS will implement a project designed to support Colorado agricultural producers in identifying and accessing viable consumer markets for their operations. The project’s primary purpose is to facilitate a process where farmers and ranchers can determine the most suitable markets for their products, encompassing a range of agricultural commodities including organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, and organic legumes. This initiative will result in the creation of a comprehensive toolkit for producers, equipping them with strategies aligned with modern marketing frameworks to enhance their market approach. Furthermore, AMS will establish a facilitated information exchange between farmers and partners specializing in aggregating and advertising local farm produce, creating a robust system for connecting supply and demand. The anticipated outcome of this project is to enable Colorado agricultural producers to maximize their operational capacity, reach new markets, and strengthen their presence within existing markets. Ultimately, this project will benefit farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders by providing a pathway to increased market access and expanded sales opportunities. The project will directly contribute to the availability of organic agricultural products and aims to support the continued growth of local agricultural production within Colorado.

Published Project Description:
The New Castle County (NCC) Department of Community Services (DCS) will develop, coordinate, and expand direct producer-to-consumer markets, increase producers' economic opportunity, and expand access and availability of locally and regionally produced agricultural products through the acquired Bellevue Farmers Market and its new Reader's Café Farm-to-Table, Farm Fresh Initiative. This project aligns with the NCC DCS' Live Healthy Initiative to provide access to fresh, healthy agricultural food to low-income and low-access (LI/LA) communities while providing a viable market for producers to earn an income. The NCC DCS will use the FMPP funding to develop new market opportunities for and expand direct producer-to-consumer sales opportunities at the Bellevue Farms Market and the Reader's Café Farm-to-Table, Farm Fresh Market. This project will also target outreach, marketing, and promotion to engage new and existing regional and local farmers and producers and promote agricultural products available at the Bellevue Farmers Market and the Reader's Café Farm-to-Table, Farm Fresh Market. The goal is to create new economic opportunities for regional and local farmers and producers by recruiting new and established repeat customers through partnerships and community engagement with USDA LI/LA Census Tracts, other low-income communities, and the general public.
The NCC DCS is committed to increasing consumption and access to locally and regionally produced agricultural products, as demonstrated through years of experience engaging producers at its weekly farmers markets throughout New Castle County.
llm_summary: The New Castle County (NCC) Department of Community Services will develop, coordinate, and expand direct producer-to-consumer markets to increase producers’ economic opportunity and expand access and availability of locally and regionally produced agricultural products. This project will utilize funding to enhance the Bellevue Farmers Market and establish a new Reader’s Café Farm-to-Table, Farm Fresh Initiative, creating new sales avenues for farmers and ranchers. The anticipated outcome is to increase consumption of agricultural commodities and strengthen the local food system by connecting producers directly with consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project include local farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders seeking viable market channels for their products. Specifically, the initiative will focus on boosting the supply of regionally produced agricultural goods within New Castle County. The goal is to generate economic advancement for agricultural producers by cultivating new relationships with customers through community engagement. The New Castle County Department of Community Services is committed to supporting the growth of the local food system. This project aims to create and expand market opportunities, ensuring a steady flow of regionally produced agricultural commodities from the farm to the consumer.

Published Project Description: The Village of Wellington will use grant funding to improve the promotion and marketing of the Lakeside Market at Wellington Town Center Farmers Market.  The goals for the Wellington Farmers Market Project are to increase the farmers market attendance, increase the number of vendors, improve the cultural diversity of those vendors, and engage the public through more active participation in healthy educational presentations.
llm_summary: The Village of Wellington will implement a grant-funded project to enhance the promotion and marketing efforts for the Lakeside Market at Wellington Town Center Farmers Market. This initiative will focus on increasing attendance at the market, expanding the number of vendors participating, and improving the range of agricultural products available. Specifically, the project will concentrate on bolstering the market’s offerings to include a wider selection of grains, livestock feed, dairy products, fibers, legumes, and other rotational crops – items currently not readily available in organic form. The anticipated outcomes of this project include a significant increase in the volume of domestically produced organic agricultural commodities reaching consumers and supporting farmers and ranchers. The primary beneficiaries of this project will be farmers, ranchers, and processors involved in the production and distribution of these agricultural commodities. Furthermore, the project seeks to engage consumers who are interested in purchasing fresh, locally sourced grains, feed, dairy, and other agricultural products. By expanding the variety of available goods, the Village of Wellington aims to create a more robust and attractive market environment, ultimately supporting the continued growth and success of the Lakeside Market at Wellington Town Center Farmers Market.

Published Project Description: The Clara White Mission (CWM) will use FMPP Capacity Building grant funds to support their efforts to expand a regional farmers market network and training program at the Mission’s agritourism destination in Northwest Jacksonville, White Harvest Farms (WHF). The White Harvest Regional Farmers Market will strengthen local food system infrastructure in a food desert community. This project will include up to 50 local farmers, ranchers, and regional food stakeholders to sell in-person at the farmers market, online and stock products in a retail space. This project builds a regional network of farmers for marketing goods direct-to-consumer and increases market opportunities for farmers, ranchers, and regional food stakeholders.  The program will also expand CWM training in food safety.
llm_summary: The Clara White Mission will establish the White Harvest Regional Farmers Market as a key component of its efforts to strengthen local food system infrastructure within Northwest Jacksonville. This project will facilitate the participation of up to 50 local farmers, ranchers, and regional food stakeholders who will sell their products in-person at the farmers market, online, and through a retail space. The primary goal of this initiative is to expand market opportunities for these stakeholders and to build a regional network for the direct-to-consumer sale of agricultural commodities. Furthermore, the project will create a centralized location for the aggregation and distribution of organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops. The anticipated outcome is an increased availability of these commodities within the region, supporting farmers and consumers alike. The project will benefit local farmers, ranchers, and regional food stakeholders by providing a platform to reach new markets and grow their businesses. The expanded market will also supply consumers with access to locally sourced agricultural products. This project’s success will rely on the effective organization and operation of the White Harvest Regional Farmers Market, ensuring efficient product flow and a strong connection between producers and consumers.

Published Project Description: Retaaza will build a new supply chain pathway (infrastructure) in rural Southeast Georgia.  Our project establishes a Mobile Market to change the food landscape in Clinch and Ware counties, serving as a much-needed oasis in a food desert to overcome barriers to healthy eating and increase access to fresh foods in pockets of extreme poverty. Local farmers are also important piece of the solution, to achieve the mission of connecting hungry Georgians to available local foods.  Families will have healthy options available to them without the limitation of lack of transportation and farmers will be able to increase their income by selling produce that previously went to waste
llm_summary: Retaaza will establish a new supply chain pathway in rural Southeast Georgia, focusing on addressing food access challenges within Clinch and Ware counties. This project centers on the creation of a Mobile Market, designed to serve as a critical resource in areas experiencing limited access to fresh foods and combat the effects of a food desert. The initiative aims to connect hungry consumers with available local foods while simultaneously supporting local farmers by providing a channel for selling produce that would otherwise be wasted. The core of the project involves the development of infrastructure to facilitate the movement of agricultural products, with the goal of increasing the availability of healthy food options for the affected population. Specifically, Retaaza will build a mobile market and related logistical support to enable the efficient distribution of locally sourced agricultural commodities. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened local food system, benefiting both consumers seeking healthy food choices and farmers striving to maximize their income. Ultimately, this project will improve access to fresh food within these communities, supporting the economic viability of local agricultural producers and fostering a more reliable food supply.

Published Project Description: The City of Fort Oglethorpe requests funding to support and promote a domestic direct producer to consumer market, increase healthy food options to low-income populations in and around the city, and educate consumers about healthy food options. Activities performed will include the development, coordination, and expansion of direct produce to consumer market opportunities. Expected outcomes are to increase the number of consumers that visit the market.
llm_summary: The City of Fort Oglethorpe is requesting funding to establish and promote a domestic direct producer to consumer market, with the primary purpose of increasing the availability of healthy food options for residents and supporting local farmers. This project will focus on the development and expansion of market opportunities, creating a system where farmers can directly sell their produce to consumers. Anticipated outcomes include an increase in the number of consumers visiting the market, fostering greater access to fresh agricultural commodities. The project will support stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of these goods, including farmers, ranchers, and processors. The intended beneficiaries are local residents and consumers seeking access to a wider range of food choices. The project aims to establish a direct channel for these producers to reach consumers, enhancing the accessibility of fresh food within the Fort Oglethorpe community. Ultimately, this initiative seeks to improve the supply of agricultural products available to the community’s residents.

Organizaton: Regents of the University of Idaho
Published Project Description: The goal of this project is to expand the Tuesday Community Market (TCM) in Moscow, Idaho, by recruiting more vendors and customers. The program will increase consumption of locally produced fresh vegetables, fruits, eggs, meat, and value-added foods. The promotion program will include a new online farmers market, a marketing and advertising campaign for the three-year old TCM, and the project team working with and training producers to expand their businesses to better meet local demand. The online and in-person farmers market development will necessitate collaboration between University of Idaho (UI) Extension, local producers, U.S. Military Veteran-Producers, the Soil Stewards Student Club (UI agriculture students), Latah County Fair and Event Center staff, Latah County Master Gardeners, Robin Ohlgren Consulting (a local rural strategy expert), Backyard Harvest (a local non-profit that works with low-income customers), and community members who are the customers. These partners have already been working together in various ways. This project has the potential to empower the next stage of development in the local food system via the TCM Promotion Program. This next stage of development utilizes connections to help increase sales and income for local producers and increase the consumption of fresh, local foods.
llm_summary: The Tuesday Community Market project in Moscow, Idaho, aims to expand the market’s reach and increase the consumption of locally produced fresh vegetables, fruits, eggs, meat, and value-added foods within the community. This initiative will achieve this through the development of a new online farmers market platform and a targeted marketing and advertising campaign for the existing three-year-old market. Furthermore, the project team will collaborate closely with local producers, including U.S. Military Veteran-Producers, to bolster their businesses and better meet local demand, alongside support from the Soil Stewards Student Club and Latah County Master Gardeners. The anticipated outcomes of this project include a significant increase in sales and income for participating farmers and ranchers, and a heightened awareness among consumers regarding the availability of locally sourced agricultural products. The primary beneficiaries of this project encompass local producers, processors, and the wider community, all stakeholders seeking access to fresh, regional food supplies. The project will support the growth of the Tuesday Community Market, which will ultimately benefit the producers and consumers of Moscow, Idaho, by connecting them in a way that supports the local food system. This expansion seeks to create new market pathways for regionally produced goods, while also establishing a robust supply chain for fresh food within the community.

Organizaton: City of Chicago Depart. of Cultural Affairs & Special Events
Published Project Description:
The FMPP grant will support City of Chicago’s Department of Cultural Affairs & Special Events (DCASE) efforts to increase awareness of farmers markets through a major marketing campaign throughout Chicago. A component of this wide- ranging campaign is out-of-home advertising, to include digital billboards across the city encouraging viewers to shop at farmers markets. To reach the widest audience, this grant will help to implement an extensive Chicago Transit Authority advertising campaign, to reach riders of both buses and trains. Targeted community outreach and a social media campaign will help to connect with people negatively impacted by a lack of affordable and accessible fresh foods.
Vetted marketing professionals, rooted in communities identified as the most under- resourced, will be engaged to create grassroot campaigns specific to targeted areas, including Austin, Bronzeville and West Humboldt Park. Desired outcomes are healthy food access for everyone, a rise in farmers markets sales, and strengthened relationships between local farmers and residents.
llm_summary: The City of Chicago’s Department of Cultural Affairs & Special Events (DCASE) will implement a comprehensive marketing campaign designed to increase awareness of farmers markets throughout Chicago. This initiative will encompass a significant out-of-home advertising component, including digital billboards strategically placed across the city to encourage shoppers to visit farmers markets, alongside an extensive Chicago Transit Authority advertising campaign targeting bus and train riders. The campaign aims to connect with consumers and stakeholders who may lack convenient access to fresh food sources. Specifically, the project will engage vetted marketing professionals with local roots to develop targeted campaigns within communities such as Austin, Bronzeville, and West Humboldt Park. These campaigns will focus on increasing sales among farmers and supporting the distribution of agricultural commodities. The anticipated outcomes include enhanced access to fresh food for residents and a rise in the sales volume of products from local farmers markets. This project seeks to strengthen relationships between farmers and the communities they serve, ultimately fostering a more robust local food system. The campaign’s overall goal is to provide a greater variety of food options and improve access for consumers and ranchers alike.

Organizaton: The Farm School At Gibbs Road Inc.
Published Project Description: “Stronger Together: Growing a robust farmers market system in Wyandotte County” unites a network of four separate farmers markets in Wyandotte County, Kansas. The project will grow capacity for individual markets, maximize opportunities for consumers in low income, low access tracts to access local food, and increase opportunities for local farmers and value-added goods producers in the region. Project activities include collective impact resource sharing, bilingual marketing, promotion, educational materials creation and outreach efforts. Immediate project outcomes include increasing capacity, economic opportunity, and consumer impact for all project partners. The long-term goal of this project is to develop a robust Wyandotte County farmers market coalition that maximizes access to nutrient-dense local food for consumers and increases economic opportunity for local food and value-added goods producers.
llm_summary: “Stronger Together: Growing a robust farmers market system in Wyandotte County” aims to unite and strengthen four existing farmers markets within Wyandotte County, Kansas, to maximize access to local food for consumers and provide increased economic opportunity for farmers and value-added goods producers. This project will focus on bolstering the capacity of each market, promoting the availability of locally sourced agricultural products, and developing a cohesive regional network. Anticipated outcomes include increased market volume, enhanced economic prospects for participating farmers and producers, and a greater positive impact on the local consumer base. The primary beneficiaries of this project encompass farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the Wyandotte County agricultural sector, as well as the consumer population seeking access to fresh, locally produced goods. The project’s goal is to establish a robust Wyandotte County farmers market coalition, facilitating the distribution of organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops currently unavailable in organic form. By consolidating resources and promoting coordinated marketing efforts, this initiative seeks to significantly improve the accessibility of nutrient-dense food for the community and to expand the economic viability of local food production businesses. Ultimately, “Stronger Together” envisions a strengthened food system that better serves the needs of both the agricultural producers and the consumer population of Wyandotte County.

Published Project Description: “Expanding Resources and Sales Opportunities for Local Food Producers with Crescent City Farmers Markets” will support and promote local direct producer-to-consumer marketing for farmers markets, develop marketing strategies for producers of local food and value-added products, and respond to changing technology needs in direct producer-to-consumer marketing. The project will expand vendor Technical Assistance (TA) capacity with a focus on expanding staff capacity to provide greater small business and marketing TA to prospective and existing vendors, with the goal of helping small food producers start and operate successful small businesses. Assistance will target increasing vendor sales and brand visibility, diversification of products at market, and increasing the demographic diversity of vendors represented at markets. The project will also develop a new Community Marketing Strategy focused on growing the customer base for community markets in order to increase total vendor sales.
llm_summary: Crescent City Farmers Markets will expand its resources and sales opportunities for local food producers by developing targeted marketing strategies for producers of local food and value-added products, alongside increasing vendor Technical Assistance capacity. This project aims to support farmers, ranchers, and processors by helping them start and operate successful small businesses, focusing on increasing sales and brand visibility for these producers. Specifically, the project will concentrate on expanding the range of products available at the markets, addressing identified market needs for organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, and organic legumes. Furthermore, Crescent City Farmers Markets will cultivate a new Community Marketing Strategy designed to grow the customer base for community markets, directly contributing to increased total vendor sales. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened network of local food producers, better equipped to meet consumer demand and expand their market reach. Ultimately, this project benefits farmers, ranchers, and processors, alongside the consumers who value locally produced food. The project’s success will be measured by an increase in the number of producers operating at the markets and a corresponding growth in sales volume.

Organizaton: Organization for Refugee and Immigrant Success
Published Project Description: This project will use capacity building funding to support the development of two direct-to-consumer farmers market opportunities and associated sales and marketing training for advanced practice trainee farmers. ORIS currently maintains an agricultural production training program focused on the economic development of New American refugee and immigrant farmers. The goal of this FMPP project is to develop successful and sustainable direct-to-consumer market opportunities for 25 refugee and immigrant farmers in New Hampshire at the Morningstar and Pustizzi Farm Stand markets. The program is designed to develop these opportunities through:
llm_summary: ORIS will develop two direct-to-consumer farmers market opportunities, Morningstar and Pustizzi Farm Stand markets, to support 25 refugee and immigrant farmers in New Hampshire. This project aims to establish sustainable market channels for these farmers, increasing the availability of domestically produced agricultural commodities. The initiative will focus on providing farmers with the resources needed to operate successful market stands, ultimately benefiting consumers seeking fresh, locally sourced agricultural products. The project will support these farmers as they establish and operate these market locations, contributing to the overall supply of organic agricultural products. The anticipated outcome is an expanded network of farmers able to directly engage with consumers, creating additional economic opportunities within the farming community. The project seeks to strengthen the agricultural sector by facilitating the production and sale of organic commodities, and supporting the economic viability of these 25 farmers. These farmers and associated stakeholders will benefit from increased market access and enhanced economic prospects, contributing to a more robust and resilient agricultural landscape within New Hampshire.

Organizaton: Cornell Cooperative Extension of Cortland County
Published Project Description: This project will improve upon food system viability, sustainability, and resiliency by identifying new and appropriate producer-to-consumer opportunities and by supporting and promoting existing producer-to-consumer efforts. This project will ensure community members continue to have access to locally produced foods by assisting new producers in our communities. These objectives will be met through a market analysis, developing new and existing farmer educational opportunities and resources (focusing on producer-to-consumer direct market education), hosting an annual farm trail, and the development of an underserved farmer plan. Beneficiaries include community members and new and existing farmers in the 4-county region of New York that includes Broome, Chenango, Cortland, and Tioga Counties.
llm_summary: This project aims to enhance the viability, sustainability, and resilience of the local food system by cultivating new and appropriate producer-to-consumer connections, alongside supporting existing initiatives. The project will achieve this through several key components, including a comprehensive market analysis to identify specific needs, the development of enhanced resources for farmers, and the creation of an annual farm trail to increase visibility. Anticipated outcomes include expanded access to locally produced agricultural commodities for consumers and increased opportunities for farmers to connect directly with their customer base. The primary beneficiaries of this work are farmers, ranchers, and processors within the four-county region of Broome, Chenango, Cortland, and Tioga Counties. The project will support the creation of new market pathways for agricultural products, ensuring continued availability of locally sourced goods. Specifically, efforts will focus on expanding the range of commodities available through direct sales, strengthening relationships between producers and consumers, and bolstering the overall stability of the region’s food supply chain. Ultimately, this project seeks to strengthen the economic viability of agricultural operations and improve access to fresh food options for the communities served.

Published Project Description:
Community Supported Agriculture  (CSA) is a critical distribution channel for New York City’s neighborhoods and regional farmers. While the COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated the critical nature of CSA to New York City residents, other non-local food distribution services have created a more competitive environment for local farmers. Coordinated marketing efforts, innovation, farmer education, and community collaborations are essential to maintaining and growing CSA in NYC.
In this project, led by the Farm Generations Cooperative, three organizations will come together to address these needs through educational opportunities and technological innovation. The organizations include: the Farm Generations Cooperative, a national cooperative of small and midscale farmers that develops technology to support farm viability; GrowNYC, an NYC-based organization that manages farmers markets and farmer education programs in the city; and Just Food, an organization with decades of experience managing CSA, food security, and equity initiatives in NYC. (Partner letters are provided.) In addition to these organizational partners, we will include both farmers and community members in this effort to enliven and grow the New York City CSA marketplace for decades to come.
Within the scope of this project our team will: assess the current state and needs of CSA programs in New York City with a survey and publicly available summary report; add two new community-facing features to GrownBy, a cooperatively-owned farm sales app, that support marketing and expansion of CSA programs in New York City; train 40 farmers on best practices for CSA; and release an updated digital toolbox and guide for managing New York City CSA programs.
llm_summary: Farm Generations Cooperative recognizes the critical role of Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) in New York City’s food distribution network and aims to bolster this vital channel for farmers and consumers. This project, spearheaded by Farm Generations Cooperative, GrowNYC, and Just Food, will focus on enhancing the New York City CSA marketplace through a series of targeted initiatives. Specifically, the project will deliver a comprehensive digital toolbox and guide for managing New York City CSA programs, alongside the development of two new community-facing features for the GrownBy app, a cooperatively-owned farm sales platform. The project’s anticipated outcomes include increased market access for farmers, expanded consumer engagement with local agricultural products, and a strengthened CSA network throughout the city. The primary beneficiaries of this work will include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of agricultural goods. The project’s activities will also support consumers seeking access to fresh, locally sourced food. Furthermore, the project will produce updated materials to aid in the efficient management of CSA programs, streamlining operations for all involved. The cooperative will contribute to the growth of the CSA model in New York City by equipping stakeholders with the tools and knowledge necessary to sustain and expand these valuable programs, ultimately creating a more robust and resilient food system.

Published Project Description: Since 2007, the RiseBoro Farmers Markets (RBFM) locations have connected first-generation immigrant farm owners to the predominantly Dominican, Puerto Rican, Mexican, Central American, and Ecuadorian neighborhood of Bushwick, Brooklyn. In their implementation of intergenerational farming knowledge, seed-saving, and low-impact ecological practices, the participating farmers at RBFM maintain elements of agricultural heritage while establishing themselves as business-owners. In bringing culturally familiar (yet hard-to-find in New York) products to the Bushwick community, the farmers have built a loyal following among customers who are not typical participants in local food channels. By bridging these groups of farmers and customers, RBFM demonstrates how farmers markets can encourage economic growth for small farmers while expanding affordable food access in a low-income community. This project, “Maintaining Community Traditions from the Farm to the Market” will equip us to identify and open a third farmers market location, recruit sixteen new local producers, and further establish our markets as an affordable and accessible source of heritage agricultural products. Aiming to increase farm income, we will also assist in establishing wholesale opportunities with neighborhood restaurants, markets, and non-farmer RBFM producers. In partnership with RBFM farmers, we will further evaluate the feasibility of new retail opportunities, including farm-to-institution sales and value- added product lines.
llm_summary: RiseBoro Farmers Markets’ project, “Maintaining Community Traditions from the Farm to the Market,” aims to expand its reach and impact within the Bushwick community of Brooklyn. This project will focus on establishing a third farmers market location and recruiting sixteen new local producers, supporting farmers and expanding access to heritage agricultural products. The core activities involve increasing farm income by facilitating wholesale opportunities with neighborhood restaurants, markets, and other stakeholders, alongside evaluating potential new retail avenues, including farm-to-institution sales and value-added product lines. Specifically, the project will bolster the existing market infrastructure and support the producers by fostering connections with a wider range of consumers. The anticipated outcomes include a strengthened local food system, greater availability of products that are currently unavailable in organic form, and a more robust economic foundation for the participating farmers. Ultimately, this project seeks to empower these producers and benefit the local community by providing access to fresh, culturally relevant agricultural goods, with the goal of expanding the reach of RiseBoro Farmers Markets and supporting the livelihoods of those involved in the market system.

Published Project Description: East End Food Institute is a New York based nonprofit organization dedicated to improving eastern Long Island’s food system. With this funding the East End Food Market will expand the Indoor Farmers Market to become a year-round sales opportunity for local producers on Long Island, NY.  Expand Virtual Farmers Market serving direct-to-consumer and mid-tier value chain to diversify sales channels for small scale producers on Long Island, NY.  Launch a new website and marketing campaign to increase awareness of the Indoor Farmers Market and Virtual Market as a means of boosting sales for local producers on Long Island, NY.  In addition to providing an important year-round sales channel for local farms and producers, East End Food Market will benefit small business owners, institutions, and members of the public with increased access to affordable local foods.
llm_summary: East End Food Institute is undertaking a project to expand the East End Food Market’s capabilities, primarily through the development of a year-round Indoor Farmers Market and an enhanced Virtual Farmers Market. This initiative will provide increased sales opportunities for local farmers and producers on Long Island, New York, by establishing a continuous sales channel for agricultural commodities. The project involves the creation of a robust online marketplace designed to connect small-scale producers directly with consumers and mid-tier value chain businesses, thereby broadening the distribution network for locally sourced products. Furthermore, East End Food Institute will launch a comprehensive website and marketing campaign to heighten awareness of both the Indoor Farmers Market and the Virtual Market, directly contributing to a rise in sales volume for participating producers. The anticipated outcome of this project is to significantly improve access to local foods for farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders, while also benefiting consumers with a readily available supply of fresh agricultural goods. By establishing these expanded market channels, the East End Food Market aims to support a range of agricultural operations and strengthen the overall local food system on Long Island, New York.

Published Project Description: The Niagara Falls City Market has been in existence since the horse-and-buggy days of the late 1800s. It has been a place where local food and culture has been celebrated for more than 100 years. However, as population has declined and poverty rates have increased over the last few decades, the market has dealt with some challenges. Funding through the Farmers Market Promotion Program will allow the market to take more steps forward by providing the resources necessary for the market to build capacity and reimagine itself with the input of key stakeholders (farmers, consumers, and others).  This project centers around the idea of reimagining the Niagara Falls City Market, which perfectly aligns with the Local Agriculture Market Program (LAMP) objective of supporting “the development, coordination, and expansion of direct producer-to-consumer marketing, local and regional food markets and enterprises, and value-added agricultural products.”
llm_summary: The Niagara Falls City Market project aims to revitalize a historic local institution with the support of Farmers Market Promotion Program funding, focusing on building capacity and reimagining the market’s future through collaborative input from farmers, consumers, and other stakeholders. This project will support the development of a strengthened market infrastructure, enabling increased sales of organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops, currently unavailable in organic form. Anticipated outcomes include a more robust market offering a wider selection of locally sourced agricultural products, benefiting farmers by providing new avenues for sales and enhancing the market’s position within the community. The primary beneficiaries of this project are farmers seeking expanded market access, consumers desiring a greater variety of fresh, local products, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the regional food system. By addressing specific market needs for these organic commodities, the Niagara Falls City Market project seeks to stimulate economic activity and strengthen the connections between producers and consumers within the community, ultimately fostering a more sustainable and vibrant local food system.

Published Project Description:
SPSA wants to continue its work to rebuild the Pearl Market to help boost the overall sales and number of local farmers participating in the market.
Using knowledge and research from its prior USDA grant experience, SPSA seeks to re-deploy a highly targeted digital ad and outreach campaign to re-connect employees and downtown residents with the market and help farmer increase sales,  continue to target low income/low access community members, and recruit emerging new farmers and retain current farmers by providing marketing support and training.
llm_summary: SPSA seeks to revitalize the Pearl Market to stimulate sales and encourage greater participation from local farmers. This project will focus on implementing a targeted digital advertising and outreach campaign designed to reconnect employees and residents with the market, ultimately supporting increased sales for farmers. The core of this initiative involves deploying a strategic advertising campaign aimed at expanding market reach and attracting new stakeholders, with a particular emphasis on connecting with low-income individuals and those with limited access to agricultural products. SPSA intends to bolster the market’s capacity to support a wider range of agricultural commodities, including grains and livestock feed, dairy, fibers, legumes, and other rotational crops, currently unavailable in organic form. The anticipated outcome of this project is a strengthened market presence capable of providing increased opportunities for farmers and expanding access to organic agricultural products for consumers. This will positively impact farmers by providing a pathway to increase sales and encourage participation, while also benefiting consumers by offering additional sources of organic agricultural goods. SPSA is committed to supporting a robust and dynamic market environment for all involved stakeholders.

Published Project Description: The project “Expanding Full Farm CSA Outreach” will enhance the accessibility to high quality, organic, locally produced food to people living in Oregon’s Willamette Valley. Full Farm CSA, LLC (FFCSA) plans to expand geographic outreach, increase members, and improve operational efficiencies for its full-diet CSA program. Offering a wide range of food in a single package increases food access by the simplicity and convenience of having it all delivered at once while also providing economies of scale for the distribution, packaging, and marketing for participating farms. We propose to expand geographic outreach to serve additional communities in the Portland Metro area, Salem, Corvallis, and Albany. We also propose to build to a target of 600 full diet CSA subscriptions, from a baseline of 320 subscriptions, by the end of the project with a $2,400 average annual subscription covering the array of available products. Intended beneficiaries of this project are farmers who can double product sales to FFCSA and the additional consumer members, (adding 280 subscriptions through the project). Baseline revenue is $768,000 per year with a target of $1,440,000 by the end of the project. Operational efficiencies will be achieved through the purchase of food handling equipment to reduce labor in packing boxes. Marketing support, graphic design assistance, and engagement of an online marketing (e.g. Google ad-words) expert are included to engage and boost sales. All activities for CSA implementation will be complete by September 29, 2025.
llm_summary: Full Farm CSA, LLC plans to expand its reach and impact within the Willamette Valley, aiming to significantly increase access to high-quality, organic food for consumers and farmers. This project will achieve this through a phased expansion, initially targeting a total of 600 full-diet CSA subscriptions, representing a substantial growth from the current baseline of 320. The organization will purchase food handling equipment to streamline packing operations, reducing labor costs and improving efficiency. Furthermore, Full Farm CSA intends to increase its annual revenue from $768,000 to a target of $1,440,000 by the completion of the project, September 29, 2025. This expansion will benefit participating farms by doubling their product sales through the CSA program, alongside the increased consumer membership base. The project anticipates providing a greater selection of organic food options, consolidating purchases for greater convenience. The anticipated outcomes include increased sales volume for organic producers and an enhanced customer experience for consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers who will receive increased product sales and the consumers who will gain access to a wider range of organic food choices. The project will focus on operational improvements and marketing support, including graphic design assistance and online marketing expertise, to drive sales growth and broaden the customer base.

Organizaton: South Central Oregon Economic Development District
Published Project Description: Medium-scale producers in Klamath County are few in number and must persist against increasing environmental pressures, perpetual socioeconomic factors, and lack of capacity to increase production and sales. To increase the number of Klamath County (local) and regional producers (Central Oregon, Rogue Valley), we will conduct a series of feasibility studies with producers, regional supply chain networks, and customers. We will implement orientation and standards through regular communication and by farm training/networking events to increase capacity of new and existing producers. We will create a digital directory of local producers, facilitate school bulk sales, and initiate a local foods marketing campaign to increase the direct producer-to-consumer sales. A first-of-its kind Harvest Box will cap our efforts by aggregating, storing and delivering a value added product of local and regional foods for some of our most underserved residents. An estimated 50 local and regional farmers and ranchers will produce more products of greater variety and quality because of this project. A regional supply chain and local marketing campaign will increase consumer and bulk sales. Sales of Klamath Grown Online Marketplace will be sufficient to sustain the networking purpose of the nonprofit, Klamath Grown, as will the rich data gleaned from needs assessments. The successful launch of a local value added product will spawn other similar ventures. Advancements of established partnerships will ignite other food markets and opportunities that increase access to locally and regionally produced foods.
llm_summary: Klamath Grown’s purpose is to bolster the capacity of medium-scale producers in Klamath County and expand market access to regional stakeholders, including farmers, ranchers, and processors. This project will achieve this through a series of feasibility studies with producers, regional supply chain networks, and consumers, coupled with the implementation of standards via regular communication and farm networking events. A key element of the project involves creating a digital directory of local producers, facilitating bulk sales to schools, and initiating a local foods marketing campaign to increase direct producer-to-consumer sales. Furthermore, a first-of-its-kind Harvest Box initiative will aggregate, store, and deliver a value-added product comprised of locally and regionally sourced foods, benefiting vulnerable populations. The anticipated outcome is that approximately 50 local and regional farmers and ranchers will produce a greater volume of products with improved quality, driven by increased sales through the Klamath Grown Online Marketplace. This marketplace will sustain the networking activities of the nonprofit organization. The project aims to strengthen existing partnerships and ignite new market opportunities, ultimately increasing access to locally and regionally produced foods for consumers and supporting the economic viability of local producers. The success of the Harvest Box initiative is expected to stimulate similar ventures within the region, solidifying the long-term growth and stability of the local food system.

Published Project Description: The St. Johns Farmers Market (SJFM), a program of St. Johns Center for Opportunity (SJCO), is preparing for its fourteenth season. Much of the market’s service area is within the Low Income/Low Access Census Tract where community members are impacted by rising housing costs as the populace migrates from Portland’s city center into adjacent neighborhoods. In 2020, the market was forced to relocate unexpectedly due to construction of a luxury condominium in the neighborhood’s downtown core, then Covid-19 emerged, imposing size restrictions on the market. While the market now exceeds its pre-2020 size, cash reserves were expended to prioritize food access and sta?ng needs through a period of instability. SJCO's project will invest in long neglected marketing and equipment upgrades needed to revitalize the market for its second decade of operation. In strengthening customer communications and supporting their preferences, we support vendors in achieving desired sales, allowing SJFM to grow and reinvest in our farmers for years to come. In addition to external communications, marketing funds will be used to develop and translate materials to better promote SJCO’s business development resources to our market vendors. By helping our current vendors be successful through greater sales and access to resources, SJFM will also become a more appealing marketplace for vendors, which will in turn support long term sustainability.
llm_summary: The St. Johns Farmers Market is undertaking a critical project to revitalize its operations for its second decade, addressing significant challenges within the St. Johns Center for Opportunity’s service area, which includes a Low Income/Low Access Census Tract impacted by shifting populations and rising housing costs. This project will focus on strategic investments in marketing and essential equipment upgrades, designed to support vendors in achieving desired sales and ultimately foster market growth. Specifically, funds will be allocated to enhance customer communications, develop translated marketing materials, and provide resources to current vendors, aiming to increase sales and attract new stakeholders to the marketplace. The anticipated outcomes include a stronger, more sustainable St. Johns Farmers Market capable of meeting the needs of local farmers and consumers seeking fresh agricultural products. The primary beneficiaries of this initiative are the farmers participating in the market, the consumers who rely on access to these products, and the processors involved in supplying goods to the market. By strengthening vendor success, the St. Johns Farmers Market intends to create a more appealing environment that supports long-term viability and growth for all involved. The project’s success will contribute to a robust local food system and provide increased access to a range of agricultural commodities, promoting a thriving marketplace for years to come.

Published Project Description: The purpose of the Central Market Trust Business Development Program is to facilitate the expansion of programming outside the Market walls. The Trust will establish an online ordering platform, establish delivery mechanisms for online orders, benefitting shut ins, people earning low incomes, and people who earn low incomes and have low access to fresh and healthy foods and establish pop up markets that serve low income/low access census tract numbers. The trust will also create a marketing plan for new and existing services and product lines.
llm_summary: The Central Market Trust Business Development Program aims to expand programming beyond the Market’s current boundaries by establishing a comprehensive online ordering platform, alongside the development of efficient delivery mechanisms. This initiative will specifically address the need to provide access to fresh and healthy foods for a range of populations, including farmers, ranchers, processors, and consumers who face limited access to these products. The project anticipates creating pop-up markets strategically located within low-income census tracts, ultimately increasing the availability of organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops. These markets will serve a key role in expanding market pathways for these agricultural commodities. The Central Market Trust intends to increase the quantity of domestically produced organic agricultural products available to stakeholders. The anticipated outcomes of this program include a greater volume of organic products reaching consumers and supporting the production activities of farmers and ranchers involved in organic agriculture. The project will benefit those individuals and communities with restricted access to fresh food options, offering them a viable route to acquiring essential agricultural commodities.

Published Project Description:
Lewisburg Farmers Market (LFM) was established in 1937 providing a venue for local farmers and producers to sell locally grown food products directly to consumers. This is the only year-round farmers market in the Central Pennsylvania region.  Changes that occurred as a result of new ownership and the Covid pandemic exposed a crucial need for marketing technical assistance to broaden the market’s appeal to the next generation of customers, re-engage shoppers lost during the Pandemic, enhance sense of community, and attract more low-income consumers. “LFM Technical and Marketing Support Project” will develop a viable business plan to assure longevity of providing healthy foods to consumers in the region, maximize the profitability of new, disadvantaged, and low income farmers and producers, increase the variety of vendors, and improve the complex relationship between vendors, customers and Market management. 
LFM will develop public and private partnerships and retain the services of a top-tier marketing and consulting firm with proven track records of providing strategy-based marketing advice and initiatives. LFM
management will monitor the data driven approach and will share the data and initiatives with Penn State Extension Farm Market Educational Program to disseminate to all Farmer Markets in Pennsylvania.
llm_summary: Lewisburg Farmers Market (LFM) has operated since 1937, providing a year-round venue for local farmers and producers to offer their goods directly to consumers within the Central Pennsylvania region. This project aims to develop a comprehensive business plan to ensure the long-term viability of the market and maximize profitability for new and existing farmers and producers. The project will involve retaining the services of a top-tier marketing and consulting firm to implement strategic initiatives, focusing on broadening appeal to attract the next generation of customers, re-engage shoppers who were lost during the pandemic, and enhance the sense of community among stakeholders. Specifically, the LFM will seek to increase the variety of vendors and improve relationships between vendors, customers, and market management. A key objective is to expand market access for farmers and producers, with a particular focus on supporting the availability of organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened market presence with increased consumer engagement and expanded sales for participating farmers and producers. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and consumers within the region who will have increased access to a wider selection of locally sourced agricultural products. The LFM management team will diligently monitor data-driven approaches and share relevant data and initiatives with Penn State Extension’s Farm Market Educational Program to disseminate information to all farmer markets across Pennsylvania.

Published Project Description: Family Health Centers, Inc. (FHC) is a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) that serves Orangeburg, Bamberg, Calhoun and Upper Dorchester Counties in SC. The area is rural, with high rates of poverty and numerous census tracts which have been identified as Low Income /Low Access priority areas. Many area residents find it difficult to access fresh fruits and vegetables needed for a healthy diet. FHC created Farmer’s Markets in LI/LA census tracts in Orangeburg and Denmark for the dual purpose of creating economic opportunity for local farmers by providing direct to consumer sales venues, and providing underserved residents with access to fresh produce. FHC received FMPP funding in 2017 to enhance the Orangeburg market and create the market in Denmark. That grant was closed out in good standing 02/28/2022. The farmer’s markets have been successful and vendors and consumers have requested an increase in market days and sites. Because many residents in small rural communities contend with low income and limited access, FHC seeks continuing funding to add a mobile farmers market that will bring locally grown produce to consumers in priority areas. FMPP funds will be used to retrofit a bus, purchased with health center funds, for use as the mobile market. Grant funds will be used to hire a Market Manager/Driver and a Sales Assistant to staff the mobile market. Host sites will include FHC satellite sites and Senior Centers in priority areas. SC State University’s 1890 Extension Program will assist in recruitment of additional local vendors.
llm_summary: Family Health Centers, Inc. (FHC) is undertaking a project to expand access to fresh produce for residents in Orangeburg, Bamberg, Calhoun, and Upper Dorchester Counties in South Carolina, addressing a critical need within rural communities grappling with limited access to healthy food options. The core of this initiative involves the retrofitting of a bus, purchased with existing health center funds, to serve as a mobile market, alongside the procurement of necessary supplies and equipment for operation. Anticipated outcomes include increased availability of locally grown agricultural commodities for farmers and consumers, particularly focusing on organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, and organic legumes, and other rotational crops, creating direct sales venues for vendors and expanding market access for consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project will be local farmers, processors, and ranchers seeking new markets for their products, as well as residents in priority areas who will gain access to a reliable source of fresh produce. Host sites will include FHC satellite sites and Senior Centers, supported by the SC State University’s 1890 Extension Program’s assistance in recruiting additional local vendors. The mobile market will operate by delivering fresh agricultural products directly to these locations, providing a vital service to those experiencing difficulty obtaining needed food items, and contributing to a stronger local food system.

Organizaton: Axis 1 Center of Barnwell/ Barnwell County Commission On Alcohol & Drug Abuse
Published Project Description:
Healthy Eating Active Living Partners (HEALing Partners) is a multi-organization regional coalition that is building community food security in rural Barnwell, SC by redeveloping and enhancing a direct-to-consumer market that makes locally produced foods more accessible and supports farmers and food entrepreneurs through a vital local farmers market. Working collaboratively with other nonprofits and the City of Barnwell, HEALing Partners will redevelop the Barnwell Farmers Market (BFM), establishing an enduring seasonal market that actively works to improve food accessibility and economic stability. The BFM will provide a reliable marketplace to local farmers and food producers, provide healthy food access within our community, educate on the connection between local food choices and quality of life, and provide the community access to resources needed to improve their health.
The BFM redevelopment project will reach its goals through development of a market manager position; recruitment, outreach, and retention of new, beginning, and underserved farmers; increased number and types of vendors; developing a viable business model that can assure profitability, accessibility, and sustainability for the market as a whole; and develop a branding and marketing strategy to increase community reach.
Expected outcomes that will result from a robust local market include: increased overall awareness of local farm products and producers, increased direct-to-consumer sales for local growers, increased ability of low-income individuals to access and purchase healthy local foods directly from farmers, increased numbers and varieties of local food producers vending at the BFM, and increased knowledge about healthy food choices and preparation.
llm_summary: Healthy Eating Active Living Partners is undertaking a vital project to bolster community food security in rural Barnwell, South Carolina, by redeveloping and enhancing the Barnwell Farmers Market (BFM). This initiative will establish a sustainable, seasonal market, providing a reliable marketplace for local farmers and food producers, while simultaneously increasing access to healthy foods for community members. The project’s core activities include the development of a market manager position, recruitment and retention of farmers and food producers, and the expansion of vendor offerings. Furthermore, HEALing Partners will develop a viable business model to ensure the market’s long-term profitability and sustainability, alongside a targeted branding and marketing strategy to broaden community reach. The anticipated outcomes of this project are numerous, including heightened awareness of local farm products among consumers, increased direct-to-consumer sales for local growers, and improved access to healthy food options for the community. Specifically, the project aims to increase the number and varieties of local food producers participating in the BFM.
