The beneficiaries of this project encompass farmers, ranchers, and food processors, alongside the wider community seeking access to locally produced goods. Ultimately, Healthy Eating Active Living Partners seeks to strengthen the local food system and positively impact the health and economic stability of the Barnwell region.

Published Project Description: Knowledge Quest (KQ) operates Green Leaf Learning Farm (GLLF) (https://www.knowledgequest.org/programs/green-leaf-learning-farm/), a three-acre USDA certified organic, urban farm where we grow affordable, fresh produce for Memphis families and provide a place for the entire community to learn about and celebrate fresh, locally grown food. The overarching goal of GLLF is to expand our impact and reach to serve the many low-income families that struggle with food insecurity and access to healthy affordable foods. Formally initiated in 2010, GLLF is located in the historically black neighborhood of South Memphis, a known food desert, where low-income residents face the combined impacts of low access to nutritious, fresh produce and limited economic opportunity. Therefore, GLLF seeks USDA FMPP funding to hire a full-time Program Manager and secure services of a PR firm who will together assess the existing consumer need for food, farmers markets, and food assistance programs. This role will expand our partnership base, develop recruitment and promotional materials, and design and deploy a cohesive advertising and promotional campaign to increase awareness of and participation in community-based fresh-food sales and events. The overall objective is that this project will ultimately lead to the development of an informed, diverse consumer base and an increase in demand for local products through marketing strategies that target our generationally, culturally, and socio-economically diverse community. This work will be accomplished through the collaboration from both the public and private sectors, all committed to the success of the farm and local producers.
llm_summary: Knowledge Quest operates Green Leaf Learning Farm (GLLF) to address food insecurity within the South Memphis community. This project seeks USDA FMPP funding to hire a full-time Program Manager and engage a public relations firm, aiming to assess current consumer needs regarding food, farmers markets, and food assistance programs. The anticipated outcome is the development of an informed consumer base and an increase in demand for local products through targeted marketing strategies. GLLF will focus on expanding its reach to serve low-income families in the South Memphis area, who face limited access to fresh produce. The project will support farmers and producers by increasing sales opportunities and bolstering the availability of locally grown food options. The primary beneficiaries will include consumers seeking access to healthy food choices and producers involved in local agricultural operations. The goal is to stimulate greater interest in locally sourced products through a coordinated marketing campaign, thereby strengthening the farm’s position within the community. Through this effort, GLLF intends to build stronger relationships with stakeholders and contribute to a more robust local food system, supporting those who need access to fresh food.

Published Project Description: This project will develop and implement a new, bi-weekly farmers’ market in Huston, TX. The new market will increase access to healthy fresh food options to the area, especially the adjacent LI/LA census tracts. The project will encourage participation from approximately 30 climate-smart farmers/producers from within a 99-mile radius of the market site and will provide vendors with access to the local restaurants, thereby forming an additional access point for the delivery of local, climate-smart food. Project outcomes include establishment of a market for local food, provision of logistical support to vendor and promotion of local food, and increased consumer education and demand for locally grown food. Project beneficiaries include local farmers, growers, and ranchers as well as Huston area consumers.
llm_summary: This project will develop and implement a new bi-weekly farmers’ market in Houston, TX, with the primary purpose of increasing access to fresh food options for the local community, specifically targeting the adjacent LI/LA census tracts. The project will facilitate the establishment of a market for local food, providing logistical support to approximately 30 farmers and producers within a 99-mile radius, and creating an additional access point for local food delivery to area restaurants. Anticipated outcomes include increased consumer demand for locally grown products, as well as the creation of a market channel for local farmers and ranchers. The primary beneficiaries of this project will be local farmers, ranchers, and processors, alongside the Houston area consumers. This initiative aims to strengthen the local food supply chain by connecting producers with retail outlets. The project will support the sale of a variety of agricultural products. Furthermore, the project will focus on creating a sustainable market for locally sourced food, benefiting all stakeholders involved in the production and distribution process.

Published Project Description: The purpose this project is to establish and implement the new and permanent “Northeast Art and Farmers Market” in El Paso, Texas. The new market will be the first of its kind to operate in Northeast El Paso and include fresh produce from area farmers and ranchers, local handmade art and artisan products and workshops for the entire family. The proposed location at the former Cohen Stadium location is part of a revitalization project to enhance a historically underserved community. A key component to the new market, will be a partnership with the 915 Pop Up Market which will operate the Farmer and Food Education Co-op which will increase the availability of fresh produce and healthy foods while supporting local food producers and makers. The introduction of this new market location, along with the implementation of a strong marketing campaign, will increase tourism and economic development in Northeast El Paso. The new venue will allow for a larger demographic of visitors and an increase in sales for local vendors. The project’s outcomes include a range of economic development activities related to and resulting from the project. Project beneficiaries include area agricultural producers, consumers (individuals, business and institutions).
llm_summary: The Northeast Art and Farmers Market project aims to establish a permanent market location in Northeast El Paso, Texas, designed to foster economic development and support local producers. This innovative market will feature fresh produce sourced from area farmers and ranchers alongside handcrafted art and artisan products, complemented by family-friendly workshops. The proposed location at the former Cohen Stadium site is central to a revitalization effort, and a key partnership with the 915 Pop Up Market will operate a Food Education Co-op, increasing the availability of fresh produce and promoting healthy food options for consumers. The project anticipates increased tourism and sales for local vendors, generating a range of economic development activities. The primary beneficiaries of this project include local farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of agricultural commodities and artisan goods. Furthermore, the market will serve a broader consumer population seeking fresh, local products. The anticipated outcomes include a strengthened local economy and expanded market access for agricultural products. The project intends to stimulate economic activity and provide increased sales opportunities for farmers and artisan producers. Overall, the market is designed to benefit a variety of stakeholders within the Northeast El Paso community.

Published Project Description: This project will provide regionally produced Natural Beef via direct-to-consumer beef sales to Austin area consumers. The beef will be sourced from USDA Process Verified Program cattle produced a group of independent producers, and processed/packaged by a local processor, resulting in beef halves available to customers in the Austin area. Project goals include the development and promotion of a direct-to-consumer beef market for regionally raised natural beef. Project beneficiaries include actors along the value chain including the processors/packagers, independent small to medium size ranches, and area consumers.
llm_summary: This project aims to establish a direct-to-consumer beef market for regionally produced natural beef within the Austin area. The initiative will facilitate the sale of beef halves, sourced from a group of independent ranchers utilizing the USDA Process Verified Program, and processed/packaged by a local processor. Anticipated outcomes include the development of a viable market channel for this regionally raised beef, increasing access to natural beef products for consumers. Key stakeholders benefiting from this project include the farmers involved in raising the cattle, the processors and packagers handling the beef, and the consumers seeking this type of product. The project seeks to strengthen the entire value chain, providing a new market pathway for ranchers and supporting the local processing industry. Ultimately, this project will contribute to increased availability of natural beef to consumers in the Austin area, addressing a specific need within the regional food system. The project's success depends on establishing a reliable supply of natural beef halves, ensuring quality control throughout the process, and effectively marketing this product to interested consumers.

Published Project Description: This project will support Utah’s farmers market sector through increased capacity, heightened visibility, increased collaboration, and improved operations. Project activities include increasing the success of new and beginning market managers through designing and distributing a market manager handbook, hosting an annual online training for new and beginning market managers, and hosting quarterly, online Ask a Manager sessions. Additional project activities include increasing support for and visibility of Utah farmers markets by creating a nonpro?t, hosting an annual forum for network members, and creating a public-facing social media page. The project will also assess the economic and community impact of Utah farmers markets partnering directly with markets to gather data with Farmers Market Coalition guidance. Through these activities, Utah farmers markets will see increased support and capacity, heightened visibility, increased collaboration, and improved operations. Consumers and market stakeholders will bene?t through improved operations, as well as heightened visibility of Utah farmers markets.
llm_summary: Utah Farmers Markets will see enhanced support and capacity through a multifaceted project designed to bolster the sector’s operations and visibility. This project will achieve this by providing a market manager handbook, hosting an annual online forum for network members, and establishing a public-facing social media page to increase market stakeholder engagement. Furthermore, the project will conduct assessments of the economic and community impact of Utah farmers markets, working directly with market participants to gather data and ensuring the availability of organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes and other rotational crops, and organic ingredients. Anticipated outcomes include increased operational efficiency for farmers and processors, enhanced visibility of Utah farmers markets for consumers, and strengthened collaboration among market stakeholders. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and market stakeholders across Utah, who will benefit from improved market capacity and increased demand for organic agricultural commodities. Ultimately, this project aims to create a more robust and visible network of farmers markets, providing greater access to locally produced organic goods.

Published Project Description: God’s Pantry Food Bank (GPFB) serves 50 counties in Central and Eastern Kentucky, supporting more than 450 member food pantries and meal programs. Their total food distribution of 41.8 million pounds in 2021 included 13 million pounds of fresh produce. With team partners Appalachian Regional Healthcare (ARH) and Kentucky Educational Development Corporation (KEDC), GPFB is coordinating efforts to increase farm to institution distribution in southeast Kentucky, anchored by the food warehouse GPFB is developing in Hazard. GPFB’s planned facility will serve as a satellite distribution facility to improve food supply to member pantries in the distressed seven-county area. This facility will also provide supply chain infrastructure supporting farm-to-institution initiatives currently underway at ARH and KEDC. Anchoring efforts to supply more fresh fruits, vegetables, and other foods from local and regional sources, this facility will improve nutrition for patients, students, employees, and the community at large. GPFB’s food warehouse, with dry and cold storage, will fill an important gap in the regional food system, currently served by facilities located up to 230 miles away.
llm_summary: God’s Pantry Food Bank is developing a food warehouse in Hazard, Kentucky, to significantly improve the regional food supply chain and increase farm-to-institution distribution throughout southeast Kentucky. This project involves the construction of a facility equipped with dry and cold storage, designed to serve as a satellite distribution center for GPFB’s member pantries, particularly within the distressed seven-county area. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened capacity to receive and distribute fresh produce, grains, and other food commodities sourced from local and regional producers, ultimately enhancing nutrition for a wide range of stakeholders, including farmers, ranchers, processors, and consumers. The warehouse will address a critical gap in the existing food system, currently reliant on facilities located up to 230 miles away, offering a more localized and efficient supply. By facilitating the movement of fresh food directly to patient care at Appalachian Regional Healthcare, student populations at Kentucky Educational Development Corporation, and broader community needs, the project will improve access to nutritious foods. This enhanced distribution network will directly benefit the people of central and eastern Kentucky, ensuring a greater availability of fresh food sources.

Published Project Description: Celebrating its 30th season in 2022, the nonprofit Jefferson County Farmers Market (JCFM), operates the Port Townsend and Chimacum Farmers Markets in Jefferson County, WA. JCFM’s mission is to support local farmers and artisans with vibrant marketplaces that cultivate community and provide access to healthy food for all. The JCFM offers low-bar, low-fee sales venues that support new, emerging, and established small businesses in growing and thriving. Jefferson County is unique in many ways including its geographical isolation on the Olympic Peninsula, higher than average population living below the poverty level (13.6% compared to 10.2% in Washington State), and its large proportion of small and micro farms. These distinctive attributes present added challenges to sustaining a thriving farmers market organization. The Growing Farms, Thriving Markets project includes three core initiatives: 1) market assessment and research to identify gaps in the JCFM shopper base and strategies to reach under met populations; 2) support and professional coaching for new and growing farm vendors; 3) targeted outreach to grow and diversify JCFM’s regular shopper base supporting vendor sales growth. These initiatives are expected to help our community farmers markets thrive, improve the economic sustainability of local farmers and producers, and increase community access to nutritious, locally grown food for years to come.
llm_summary: The Jefferson County Farmers Market’s primary purpose is to bolster local farmers and artisans through vibrant marketplaces, fostering community and providing access to nutritious food within Jefferson County, Washington. This project will focus on three key initiatives designed to support growth and sustainability of the market organization and the farmers it supports. First, comprehensive market assessment and research will identify gaps in the shopper base and strategies to reach a broader range of consumers. Second, the project will provide support and guidance to new and expanding farm vendors, assisting them in developing their businesses. Finally, targeted outreach efforts will expand the regular shopper base, aiming to increase sales for participating vendors. These actions are expected to positively impact the economic sustainability of local farmers and producers, ultimately increasing the availability of locally grown food to the community. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within Jefferson County. The goal is to strengthen the market’s capacity and ensure continued access to fresh, locally sourced agricultural products. By addressing identified market needs and expanding consumer reach, this project anticipates a significant increase in sales volume for participating vendors, contributing to the long-term viability of the Jefferson County Farmers Market and the economic wellbeing of the producers who contribute to its success.

Published Project Description: The intent of the project is to expand the reach of our farmers market (FM) by increasing promotion and capacity to handle an increase in the number of vendors. The project would expand the footprint of the market beyond its current boundaries, by expanding outreach activities and by hiring a market coordinator to take on the responsibility for soliciting new vendors, serving customers and general expanded activities. To increase outreach, place additional adds in the local newspapers and billboards near the FM location to attract drive by customers. The project would provide training and support services for continuing and first-time vendors. The project will also provide learning opportunities and educational/nutritional materials for FM clients to encourage their participation and consumption.
llm_summary: The Farmers Market project aims to significantly expand the reach and capacity of the local farmers market to increase the availability of domestically produced organic agricultural commodities. This project will achieve this through a multi-faceted approach, including targeted advertising campaigns in local newspapers and on billboards near the market location to attract drive-by customers and the hiring of a market coordinator responsible for soliciting new vendors and overseeing expanded activities. Furthermore, the project will provide support services for continuing and first-time vendors, alongside learning opportunities and nutritional materials for market clients, encouraging their participation and consumption of organic products. The anticipated outcomes of this project are an increase in the number of vendors participating in the market, a greater volume of organic agricultural products available to consumers, and a strengthened local market for organic goods. Key beneficiaries of this initiative include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of organic agricultural commodities. The project seeks to address the critical need for additional market paths for organic grains, livestock feed, dairy, fibers, legumes, and other rotational crops currently unavailable in organic form, directly supporting the growth of the local organic market. Ultimately, this project will bolster the local economy by connecting producers of organic goods with consumers seeking these products, creating a more robust and accessible market for organic agricultural commodities within the community.

Published Project Description: The Platteville Farmer’s Market Revitalization project will revitalize and expand the Platteville Farmer’s Market (PFM) to benefit both producers and consumers. Producers will benefit by increased opportunities for direct producer-to-consumer sales and consumers will benefit by increased access to fresh, locally grown and produced agricultural products. The project will develop and implement a comprehensive marketing plan to promote the market and market producers; survey the community to determine consumer wants and needs; survey producers to determine educational, business development, and other support needs; work to retain and recruit market vendors; and provide start- up and continuing education to local food entrepreneurs and connect them with resources to help diversify and increase revenue streams. Expected outcomes include increased overall awareness of the PFM and local agricultural products and producers, increased direct-to-consumer sales and income for individual farmers through the market, increased knowledge for producers engaged in the PFM, and improved access to locally produced products for consumers, including the low-income population.
llm_summary: The Platteville Farmer’s Market Revitalization project aims to revitalize and expand the Platteville Farmer’s Market to benefit both producers and consumers. This project will focus on increasing opportunities for direct sales between farmers and consumers, as well as enhancing access to locally grown and produced agricultural products within the community. Anticipated outcomes include increased overall awareness of the Farmer’s Market and the local agricultural products offered by producers, alongside increased direct-to-consumer sales and income for individual farmers through market participation. Furthermore, the project will contribute to improved access to locally produced products for consumers, with a particular emphasis on supporting producers of grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops. The primary beneficiaries of this revitalization effort will be the farmers and ranchers involved in supplying the market, as well as the consumers seeking access to fresh agricultural commodities. The project intends to strengthen the market’s capacity to support producers by addressing their needs, including resources to potentially broaden revenue streams. Ultimately, this initiative seeks to bolster the local agricultural economy and provide a valuable marketplace for producers to connect with their customer base.

Published Project Description: The goal of Greensgrow’s Community Connections Program is to build the long-term capacity and stability of Greensgrow through the development of a strategic community connections plan including development of supportive infrastructure by transitioning to a “farm without walls” and thereby addressing food insecurity and increasing connection between producers and consumers. The intended beneficiaries are residents of Kensington, Port Richmond, and Fishtown who are experiencing poverty, food insecurity, and lack of access to farm-fresh produce. Activities include 1) conducting a data-driven community needs assessment and market analysis, 2) employing a Community Connections Manager to oversee the program as well as coordinate outreach activities, participate in strategic planning process, develop and maintain connections with community partners, producers, and other urban farms, etc., 3) creation of a board to facilitate a strategic planning process, 4) development of new outreach and engagement programs to connect growers/producers to the community/consumers, 5) develop and host training opportunities for urban farms/farmers to present the new model as well as technical knowledge about producing, preparing, procuring, and/or accessing local/regional foods, and 6) develop and produce video content for social media and other outlets to connect producers with consumers.
llm_summary: Greensgrow’s Community Connections Program aims to strengthen the organization’s long-term stability and capacity through the implementation of a strategic community connections plan, incorporating a “farm without walls” model to address food insecurity and foster stronger relationships between producers and consumers. This project will involve the development of supportive infrastructure, including establishing connections with local farmers, ranchers, and processors to ensure access to a wider range of organic agricultural commodities, specifically focusing on grains, livestock feed, dairy, fibers, legumes, and other rotational crops currently unavailable in organic form. The anticipated outcomes include increased availability of these organic products within the Kensington, Port Richmond, and Fishtown communities, supporting local food systems and enhancing consumer access to fresh, locally-sourced goods. The primary beneficiaries of this initiative are residents experiencing food insecurity and limited access to farm-fresh produce, as well as the stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of these agricultural commodities. Greensgrow will establish a board to facilitate strategic planning, coordinate outreach activities, and maintain connections with community partners. Furthermore, the project will generate video content for social media channels to connect producers with consumers and expand market opportunities for organic agricultural products.

Published Project Description: The Refugee & Asylee Market Promotion (RAMP) project will increase refugee farmers’ integration into Sacramento’s thriving farm-to-fork market, providing community development training and technical assistance to expand financial stability and increase access to culturally relevant produce. The project aims to close the gap between Sacramento’s refugee and underserved farmers and local markets by training and assisting small-scale farmers to sell to local farmers markets, and enter mid-tier value chain suppliers, including ethnic grocery stores. RAMP’s goal is to increase supply by upskilling the farmer base and increasing demand by expanding the portfolio of buyers. By facilitating market linkages through ethnic markets and roadside stands, developing a ‘refugee grown’ label to increase demand outside of ethnic markets, and marketing a variety of culturally appropriate fruits and vegetables, the project aims to improve healthy food access and consumption for low- income immigrant communities, while developing new market opportunities for small-scale farming businesses.
llm_summary: The Refugee & Asylee Market Promotion (RAMP) project seeks to enhance the integration of refugee and asylee farmers into Sacramento’s thriving farm-to-fork market, focusing on expanding financial stability and increasing access to culturally relevant produce. This project aims to bridge the gap between local farmers and refugee farmers by equipping small-scale agricultural businesses with the support needed to sell their goods through local farmers markets and to engage with mid-tier value chain suppliers, including ethnic grocery stores. The project anticipates increased supply through the upskilling of the farmer base and expanded demand by broadening the range of buyers. RAMP will facilitate market linkages through ethnic markets and roadside stands, and will develop a ‘refugee grown’ label to stimulate demand beyond these channels. A core component involves marketing a variety of culturally appropriate fruits and vegetables, ultimately improving access to nutritious foods for low-income immigrant communities. The project expects to benefit farmers by creating new market opportunities and provide consumers with a wider selection of produce. This initiative supports agricultural businesses involved in the production and distribution of these goods, creating a more robust local food system. The project’s overall goal is to strengthen the agricultural sector while improving access to fresh food for the communities it serves.

Published Project Description: Augusta Locally Grown (ALG) plans to provide business best practices training to mostly underserved farmers of all scales and to regional farmers markets in order to increase sustainability for our regional food system. Through our years of market management and with partnering business professionals, ALG has developed an effective model for supporting both the farmer and the market that enhances product-to-consumer and mid-tier value chain opportunities, increases visibility through marketing, and leverages regional and state partnerships for scaling. Through ALG’s new position as a regional food hub at our location in The HUB for Community Innovation of Augusta, ALG will serve as the regional authority on farmers market best practices, moving to enhance our food system’s infrastructure. Partnerships with the South Carolina Food Hub Association and Georgia Organics, as well as with other markets in the region, will bring more connectivity and capacity to our regional food system and thus to local food economies. Overall, strengthening the farmers, the farmers markets, and the food systems will result in increased access and availability of local agriculture products for underserved communities.
llm_summary: Augusta Locally Grown (ALG) plans to establish a regional food hub at The HUB for Community Innovation of Augusta to bolster the sustainability of the local food system. This project will focus on providing business best practices support to farmers of all scales and to regional farmers markets, aiming to enhance product-to-consumer and mid-tier value chain opportunities while increasing market visibility through strategic marketing initiatives. ALG will function as the regional authority on farmers market operations, facilitating greater connectivity and capacity within the food system. Specifically, ALG will support farmers, ranchers, and processors by providing resources to optimize their operations and increase the availability of organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops. The anticipated outcomes include an expanded range of locally sourced agricultural commodities, improved access for consumers to fresh, regional products, and strengthened relationships among stakeholders within the food system. Ultimately, this project seeks to increase the supply of agricultural products, creating a more robust and reliable regional food economy. The beneficiaries of this project encompass farmers, ranchers, processors, and consumers who will benefit from the improved access to regional agricultural products and the increased efficiency of the food system.

Published Project Description: Ecommerce has grown in recent years, but farmers, ranchers and seafood harvesters focused on selling locally-produced meat and fish have struggled to adapt. Changing technology needs and a lack of knowledge regarding online marketing and shipping frozen meat have deterred producers who serve local markets from rapidly adopting ecommerce as a way to increase their sales of locally-produced meat and seafood. ChopLocal, an “online farmer’s market” for niche meat producers, will provide training and technical assistance to 500 livestock farmers, ranchers and seafood harvesters selling direct-to-consumer, to assist them with digital marketing and ecommerce platform establishment and maintenance. Training will include an educational blog, webinar series and online course. Technical assistance will also be provided to assist producers one-on-one in establishing an ecommerce store. This project will result in at least 150 participating producers establishing ecommerce stores.
llm_summary: ChopLocal is a project designed to assist farmers, ranchers, and seafood harvesters who focus on selling locally-produced meat and fish. The project will provide technical assistance and support to 500 livestock producers operating within direct-to-consumer sales models, facilitating the establishment and maintenance of ecommerce stores. This initiative anticipates the creation of at least 150 participating producers with functional online stores, thereby expanding market access for these stakeholders. The core of the project involves providing individualized support to establish and manage these online retail platforms, directly addressing the barriers preventing widespread adoption of ecommerce among these producers. By streamlining the complexities of online sales, ChopLocal aims to significantly increase the volume of locally-sourced meat and seafood reaching consumers. The project will focus on building the capacity of these producers to effectively engage in digital marketing and manage their online operations. Ultimately, the project seeks to enhance the availability of domestically produced meat and seafood, improving the operational efficiency of the producers and supporting their sales growth within their local markets.

Organizaton: Greater Lafayette Commerce Community & Economic Development
Published Project Description: This project is to help create a sustainable method for vendors of the Downtown Lafayette Farmers Market to promote and market themselves. The goal is to equip the vendors with tools they can utilize to enhance their marketing efforts, and train them to use these tools and others at their disposal. The project is broken into 3 key initiatives:  1) Development of Marketing Tools: An enhancement of the Lafayette Farmers Market website to allow vendors to create and manage their own pages on the site; 2)  Online training Library and in-person training covering a variety of marketing strategies for vendors to engage directly to consumers; and 3)  Individualized, 1-1 technical assistance and training on digital marketing initiatives, ecommerce implementation, social media, etc. to help eliminate barriers for vendors to market directly to consumers.
llm_summary: The Lafayette Farmers Market project aims to establish a sustainable marketing framework for vendors, equipping them with the necessary tools and resources to effectively engage with consumers. This initiative will encompass the development of a customized website portal, enabling vendors to independently manage their online presence and promotional materials. Furthermore, the project will provide resources to support farmers, ranchers, and processors in expanding their direct-to-consumer marketing efforts. The anticipated outcome is an increase in the availability of domestically produced organic agricultural commodities, facilitating stronger connections between producers and consumers. Specifically, the project will support vendors in implementing digital marketing strategies, including ecommerce implementation and social media engagement, to broaden their reach and sales. The primary beneficiaries of this project include the farmers, ranchers, and processors participating in the Lafayette Farmers Market, as well as the consumers who purchase these goods. By providing tools and resources, this project seeks to strengthen the market for organic agricultural products and improve the operational capabilities of the vendors. Ultimately, the project will create a more robust and accessible market for organic goods, benefitting the producers and those who utilize their products.

Organizaton: Central LA Economic Dev. Alliance dba Louisiana Central
Published Project Description: The Alexandria Farmers Market’s FMPP project will reinforce and expand its current State, land-grant university, local government and community-based partnerships to catalyze better market access and farm business viability for rural small-scale agricultural producers in central Louisiana. These objectives will be achieved by: improving farmer success and vendor retention through training on food safety, cottage food laws and business financial literacy; intentionally recruiting a more diverse range of prospective market vendors for training in order to improve economic prospects for lower-income rural residents and expand the multicultural appeal of the market; and attracting record numbers of Federal nutrition benefit recipients to the market through a variety of innovative outreach and promotional strategies and family-oriented community events. The results of this project are anticipated to yield important findings and strategies that can be applied to rural farmers markets across the country.
llm_summary: The Alexandria Farmers Market’s FMPP project aims to bolster market access and farm business viability for rural small-scale agricultural producers in central Louisiana through strengthened partnerships with state, land-grant university, local government, and community-based organizations. This initiative will focus on attracting record numbers of Federal nutrition benefit recipients to the market, alongside intentional recruitment of a broader range of prospective vendors, to enhance economic prospects for lower-income rural residents and broaden the market’s appeal. The project seeks to support farmers and ranchers by increasing the availability of organically produced grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes and other rotational crops, and organic ingredients. Anticipated outcomes include an expanded market offering and increased sales for participating producers. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the central Louisiana agricultural sector, alongside the consumers seeking access to domestically produced agricultural commodities. The project will contribute to developing markets for organically produced goods, ultimately increasing the supply of these goods to the public. The Alexandria Farmers Market’s FMPP project expects to yield important findings and strategies applicable to rural farmers markets nationwide, promoting sustainable agricultural practices and supporting local food systems.

Published Project Description: Through this project, farmers and community members will create safe, on-farm festivals that generate local sales, build customer loyalty, and strengthen rural communities. Project partners will bring together an experienced event and community organizing team to identify and train eight community-based teams, made up of farmers and food advocates, to produce a series of unique, on-farm festivals. Project activities include: Development of trainings, website, and a toolkit of best practices; Employ peer-based learning to train cohorts across Minnesota; Create an asset maps to identify community resources; Incorporation of a input from a range of local food producers and businesses to build capacity for entire communities; Creation of fun, interactive educational materials about the value of local food; Conducting communications campaigns to promote events; and Evaluation to assess the economic impact and sustainability of the on-farm festival model. As a result of this project, it is anticipated that 2,600 local farmers and consumers/community members will engage with local food.
llm_summary: Through this project, farmers and community members will develop and implement safe, on-farm festivals designed to generate local sales, cultivate customer loyalty, and strengthen rural communities. The project will support eight community-based teams, comprised of farmers and food advocates, in producing a series of unique events, utilizing the development of a comprehensive toolkit of best practices, a dedicated website, and asset maps to identify relevant community resources. Anticipated outcomes include the engagement of 2,600 local farmers and consumers, fostering a stronger local food system. These activities will prioritize input from a range of local food producers and businesses to bolster capacity within entire communities, creating fun and interactive educational materials about the value of locally sourced agricultural products. The project aims to increase the availability of organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops, addressing a critical need for additional market paths. The farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved will contribute to the creation of a more robust and accessible local food system, ultimately benefiting the communities where these events are hosted. This project’s activities will concentrate on building relationships among producers and consumers, leading to increased sales and enhanced community connections.

Published Project Description: This project addresses those needs by offering key tangible infrastructure and technical assistance services, including: processing capacity, sales point access, and expanded consumer marketing to increase accessibility of regionally produced food for both direct to consumers and public institutions. This project represents a transformative investment in regional agriculture, rural development, food access, and equity, to build a strong localized food economy. LFPP funding will support the staffing expansion necessary to accommodate any and all farmers and food businesses throughout Greater Washington County, Maine that could benefit from Minke Food Hub.
llm_summary: The Minke Food Hub project represents a transformative investment focused on increasing accessibility of regionally produced food for farmers, consumers, and public institutions within Greater Washington County, Maine. This project will provide key infrastructure and technical assistance services, encompassing processing capacity, access to sales points, and expanded consumer marketing initiatives, ultimately building a strong localized food economy. The core objective is to facilitate the increased movement of domestically produced agricultural commodities, particularly those aligned with identified market needs such as organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops. The project’s anticipated outcomes include enhanced market opportunities for regional producers, improved access to food for consumers, and support for processors and other stakeholders involved in the food supply chain. By providing these services, the Minke Food Hub aims to address the need for additional market paths for regional agricultural products, fostering greater economic viability for farmers and ensuring a broader availability of these commodities. The project’s success will be measured by the increased volume of regionally produced food reaching consumers and institutions, contributing to a more robust and resilient local food system.

Organizaton: Board of Regents, NSHE, obo University of Nevada, Reno / Nevada System of Higher Education
Published Project Description:
Nevada is one of the fastest-growing states in the US. Farmers markets can be part of the solution to feeding the expanding population while addressing climate concerns and access to fresh produce.
Farmers markets also support the local agricultural economy, serve as community spaces for newcomers, and ameliorate food insecurity in rural and poor urban neighborhoods. Throughout the state of Nevada, farmers markets have been operating with some success. However, they urgently need help with consumer marketing. The vast majority of farm vendors are small operations with limited marketing resources. According to NevadaGrown, a quasi-association of Nevada farmers markets, typical farmers markets are also small operations not equipped to engage in comprehensive consumer marketing. To address these challenges, we will conduct a community development training and technical assistance project. The first year will be devoted to a comprehensive needs assessment and a marketing plan development. In the second year, we will implement the marketing plan by providing training and technical assistance to farmers market managers and farm vendors during the off-season and orchestrating a community-based integrated marketing campaign during the peak season. In the third year, we will repeat the training/technical assistance and campaign cycle to enhance retention and fluency of the knowledge and skills gained. In every stage of this project, the needs of farmers, farmers market managers, and consumers—especially those in underserved communities—will be prioritized and the project team composition and structure will reflect the community orientation.
llm_summary: Nevada’s burgeoning population presents significant challenges in ensuring access to fresh produce, and this project aims to bolster the state’s farmers markets to address these needs. The project will provide comprehensive assistance to farmers and market managers, focusing on developing and implementing marketing plans for Nevada’s existing farmers markets. Anticipated outcomes include increased consumer awareness of locally available agricultural products and strengthened market connections for Nevada’s farming operations. The primary beneficiaries of this project are farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of agricultural commodities. Specifically, the project will concentrate on supporting the growth of markets for organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops. The project team will prioritize the needs of these involved parties and will work to establish robust marketing campaigns during the peak season and provide ongoing support to ensure market stability and expansion. Through this collaborative effort, the project seeks to enhance the viability of Nevada’s farmers markets and support the overall agricultural economy of the state.

Published Project Description: The purpose of “Harnessing technology to enhance the expertise of Oklahoma agricultural producers while partnering with community organizations for long-term sustainability of the Scissortail Park’s Farmers Market” is to simultaneously improve producer sustainability and consumer access to local foods.  The project will expand the skills of local producers harnessing technology, training, community building, implementing a secondary mid-week market, and marketing to increase sales and attendance. Project beneficiaries include local producers as well as the Oklahoma City community more broadly. Project outcomes are anticipated to include increased producer sales, increased vendor recruitment, and increased participation in the market from consumers in the surrounding neighborhoods.
llm_summary: The Scissortail Park’s Farmers Market project aims to simultaneously improve the sustainability of local agricultural producers and expand consumer access to locally sourced foods. This project will focus on increasing sales and attendance at the market through the implementation of technology enhancements for farmers, the creation of a secondary mid-week market, and targeted marketing efforts. Anticipated outcomes include increased sales volume for participating farmers, expanded recruitment of vendors to the market, and greater participation from consumers residing in surrounding neighborhoods. The primary beneficiaries of this project encompass local farmers, ranchers, and agricultural processors, alongside the broader Oklahoma City community. Specifically, the project seeks to address the need for greater availability of organically produced grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops – commodities currently limited in organic form. This expansion will provide new market pathways for these products, supporting the economic viability of agricultural operations. The project will concentrate on enhancing operational efficiency and broadening consumer reach within the Scissortail Park’s Farmers Market. Through strategic market development, the initiative anticipates a positive impact on the agricultural sector and increased access to locally available food products for the community.

Published Project Description: Lane County Farmers Market (LCFM) is our region’s oldest and largest farmers market and an integral part of Lane County’s economic and cultural infrastructure.  LCFM requests financial support through the Farmers Market Promotion Program to enable us to fulfill our potential to support the viability of our producers, create a more inclusive marketplace, and better engage our community.  The City of Eugene has constructed a new pavilion and plaza area for the purpose of housing LCFM and creating a more active civic center downtown.  This new market space allows LCFM to provide vending space to more producers.  We plan to recruit and mentor new and socially disadvantaged farmers to become long-term market members.  LCFM seeks to create new marketing options for farmers and to develop a value-added products training program.  The program will allow farmers to enjoy greater revenues through expanded product offerings and the ability to sell year-round.  LCFM will also develop a mid-tier value chain by creating new pathways for farmers to vend with local restaurants, grocery stores, and co-ops; developing relationships that serve buyers and sellers.  Local chefs who are proponents of using locally grown foods have expressed interest in giving cooking demonstrations at the market.  Demonstrations will serve three purposes: creating alliances between restaurants/chefs and our market, disseminating recipes on how to use seasonal produce, and showcasing farmers’ value-added products.   LCFM plans to share materials developed and findings from these new programs with other farmers markets that are interested in developing similar programs.
llm_summary: Lane County Farmers Market is seeking financial support to enhance its role as a vital component of Lane County’s economic and cultural landscape, building upon the recently constructed pavilion and plaza area in downtown Eugene. This project will expand market capacity by providing more vending space for producers, directly addressing the need for increased market pathways for farmers and other agricultural stakeholders. The Lane County Farmers Market anticipates creating new opportunities for farmers to generate greater revenues through the development of value-added products, alongside the creation of direct-to-consumer relationships with local restaurants, grocery stores, and cooperatives. Specifically, the project will facilitate the development of new pathways for farmers to aggregate and process organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, and organic legumes, aligning with the goals of increasing the availability and demand for domestically produced organic agricultural commodities. By fostering these connections, the Lane County Farmers Market intends to support farmers, processors, and other stakeholders in the agricultural supply chain. The project’s anticipated outcomes include a strengthened market infrastructure, expanded product offerings, and a network of relationships that benefit both producers and consumers who seek access to fresh, locally sourced food products. Ultimately, the Lane County Farmers Market aims to contribute to a more robust and resilient local food system while strengthening connections among farmers and the community they serve.

Published Project Description: The Chatham University program supports farmers and other food business owners in implementing better business practices and developing new products, consumer experiences, and other revenue streams. It does so at a critical time in Pennsylvania agriculture where an aging farmer population is under increasing market pressure to transition farmland out of production. The program will support farmers in developing viable value- added products, provide specialized courses in business model diversification, offer individual consulting services, conduct hands-on consumer workshops, and enhance a network of retail and promotional partners. The program is anticipated to increase the longevity of regional farmers, ranchers, and food businesses, sustain vibrant communities of informed consumers, and ultimately foster a stronger regional food system.
llm_summary: The Chatham University program is designed to support farmers and other food business owners in implementing improved business practices and developing new products, consumer experiences, and revenue streams, addressing a critical need within Pennsylvania agriculture. This project will provide farmers, ranchers, and processors with assistance in creating viable value-added products, exploring business model adjustments, and securing individual consulting services. Furthermore, the program will facilitate hands-on consumer workshops and cultivate a network of retail and promotional partners, aiming to increase the longevity of regional food businesses and sustain vibrant communities of informed consumers. The anticipated outcomes include bolstering the production of organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops, which are currently unavailable in organic form, directly addressing a gap in the market. By supporting the development of these products, the program intends to strengthen the regional food system, providing increased market opportunities for farmers and processors while enhancing the availability of organic agricultural commodities. Ultimately, this project seeks to positively impact the entire food chain, from producers to consumers, by fostering a more robust and resilient regional food system.

Published Project Description: The Food Trust’s 2022–27 three-year project, “Stronger Together: Growing Philadelphia Farmers Markets and Agricultural Businesses Through Citywide Partnerships, Promotion and Technology” (Stronger Together), The Food Trust (TFT) will strengthen our partnerships with the Philadelphia Department of Public Health (PDPH) and Philadelphia Parks & Recreation (PPR) to create a city-wide promotional campaign for all Philadelphia farmers market and farm stands; support the City of Philadelphia’s coordination of farmers market operator resources; and identify and further develop an online platform that will support the creation of a regional network of local agricultural businesses and a variety of purchasers. The goals of this project are to support new and existing market operators' processes and market growth, increase revenue streams for market vendors through online marketing and direct producer-to-consumer opportunities, and strengthen nutrition security and healthy food access throughout the city of Philadelphia. In addition, TFT plans to reconvene its Farmers Market Advisory Group (FMAG), which includes urban and rural farmers, community members, and other local food stakeholders, in order to guide capacity building and market planning. FMAG will provide continuous peer-to-peer technical assistance and support on skills and strategies for farmers in Pennsylvania (PA) to increase sales in the communities they serve through workshops, webinars and the creation of a community of learning for farmers.
llm_summary: The Food Trust’s “Stronger Together” project aims to bolster Philadelphia’s farmers markets and agricultural businesses through collaborative partnerships with the Philadelphia Department of Public Health and Philadelphia Parks & Recreation, culminating in a comprehensive citywide promotional campaign. This project will support the coordination of resources for farmers market operators and establish an online platform designed to foster a regional network connecting local agricultural businesses with various purchasers, including farmers, ranchers, and processors. The anticipated outcomes of this initiative include increased revenue streams for market vendors through enhanced online marketing opportunities and direct producer-to-consumer sales, alongside strengthened nutrition security and improved access to wholesome food options throughout the city. Specifically, The Food Trust intends to convene its Farmers Market Advisory Group to provide ongoing, peer-to-peer technical assistance and support to farmers across Pennsylvania, focusing on strategies to boost sales within their communities. This will be achieved through workshops and webinars, creating a community of learning for agricultural businesses. The project will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, and processors, as well as consumers seeking locally sourced products. Ultimately, The Food Trust’s efforts will contribute to expanding market pathways for Pennsylvania agricultural commodities, supporting the growth of local businesses and enhancing food accessibility for the population.

Published Project Description:
This project will support and promote direct-to-consumer (D2C) marketing of locally processed food products that are primarily made by a diverse and inclusive community of members at Hope & Main, Rhode Island’s premier food business incubator. 

We expect that 150 new food producers, 40% of whom are expected to be minority-owned businesses, will participate along with 100+ current members and other local food processors, growers, and  producers in the State. 

The project will support four main D2C channels including Hope & Main’s onsite markets and other famers markets throughout Rhode Island e-commerce, two mid-tier value chain partners—the Farm Fresh RI Market Mobile program and Coastal Food Shed’s Virtual Market and the annual RI Tabletop Show.  Hope & Main is able to provide training and technical assistance that is targeted toward proven pathways to safely launch, scale, and de-risk small food businesses on their journey toward sustainability.
llm_summary: Hope & Main’s project aims to support and promote direct-to-consumer marketing of locally processed food products originating from Hope & Main, Rhode Island’s food business incubator, with the expectation of engaging 150 new food producers, 40% of whom are anticipated to be businesses focused on agricultural products, alongside 100+ existing members and other local food processors, growers, and producers within the state. This initiative will leverage four distinct direct-to-consumer channels, including Hope & Main’s onsite markets, participation in farmers markets throughout Rhode Island, engagement with the Farm Fresh RI Market Mobile program, and presence at the RI Tabletop Show. The project seeks to expand market access for these food producers by facilitating sales to consumers and supporting the growth of regional food businesses. The anticipated outcomes include increased sales volume for these producers and a broader distribution network for locally processed food products. The primary beneficiaries of this project are farmers, ranchers, food processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of food products. This effort intends to strengthen the local food system and provide greater opportunities for businesses to reach their target markets.

Published Project Description:
Though the COVID-19 pandemic was highly challenging for small farmers and ranchers and our food systems overall, consumers found new reasons to see these producers as reliable sources of fresh foods. FRESHFARM is poised to innovate to meet the needs and opportunities of this post-pandemic food and economic landscape by: supporting increased economic sustainability for our more than 250 producers through farmers markets and farm stands; growing the customer base and loyalty for local food with promotion and education through at-market signage, video, our website, and loyalty programs; mobilizing new frontiers for market data with a sophisticated platform benefitting all producers in our network; and creating and sustaining vibrant direct producer-to-consumer outlets for
low-income/low-access communities.
llm_summary: FRESHFARM is undertaking a project to bolster economic sustainability for its network of over 250 farmers and ranchers through expanded market channels, primarily via farmers markets and farm stands. This initiative will focus on cultivating a stronger customer base and fostering consumer loyalty by implementing targeted promotional strategies, educational materials, and a loyalty program, all accessible through the organization’s website and on-site signage. A key component of the project involves developing a sophisticated data platform designed to provide valuable market insights to all stakeholders within the FRESHFARM network, facilitating more informed decision-making and strategic growth. Furthermore, FRESHFARM intends to establish and maintain vibrant, direct producer-to-consumer outlets specifically aimed at supporting low-income communities with limited access to fresh food sources. The anticipated outcomes of this project include increased sales volume for participating farmers and ranchers, improved market reach, and a strengthened connection between food producers and the communities they serve. Ultimately, this project seeks to enhance the overall viability of local food systems, supporting farmers and ranchers while ensuring access to fresh agricultural commodities for a broad range of consumers and processors. This work will provide a critical pathway for expanding the availability of organic grains, livestock feed, dairy, fibers, legumes, and other rotational crops, catering to the specific needs identified within the FRESHFARM network.

Published Project Description:
Butte County is burdened by some of the highest food insecurity rates in the state and nation, with nearly 31,300 residents in the rural Northern California county struggling with basic access to healthy food. At the same time, 98% of the food produced in the agriculturally‐rich county is sold out of the area, according to a 2022 assessment conducted by the Butte County Local Food Network. Though local need is strong, there are significant gaps constricting access to locally‐produced food.  The purpose is to increase access and availability of local fruits and vegetables to food insecure Butte County residents, Jesus Provides Our Daily Bread  seeks to develop and expand the capacity of its successful Harvesting Hope Community‐Supported Agriculture Program aka Harvesting Hope. The program currently serves Butte County residents with bi‐weekly local produce boxes, with much of the produce cultivated by individuals experiencing homelessness, through a holistic vocational training program
offered by the Jesus Center. Through this new effort, Harvesting Hope will expand infrastructure to launch a new retail access point for direct‐to consumer‐sales in a disadvantaged community, expand experiential vocational training serving beginning, underserved, and small farmers and drive increased consumption of local produce through new educational marketing efforts targeting food‐insecure consumers. Expected outcomes are 30 trained in small farm production practices and total annual sales beginning in Year 2 of $90,000, with intended beneficiaries the 1,000 individual consumers and 10 farms served by the new retail market access point and the 30 trained through experiential vocational training.
llm_summary: Jesus Provides Our Daily Bread seeks to increase access and availability of local fruits and vegetables to food insecure Butte County residents by developing and expanding the capacity of its successful Harvesting Hope Community-Supported Agriculture Program, also known as Harvesting Hope. This project will establish a new retail access point for direct-to-consumer sales within a disadvantaged community, alongside expanding the existing program’s infrastructure to support increased production and sales. Anticipated outcomes include 30 farmers receiving support in small farm production practices and an estimated total annual sales revenue of $90,000 beginning in Year 2, driven by increased consumption of local produce. The primary beneficiaries of this initiative will be the 1,000 individual consumers and 10 farms served by the new retail market access point, as well as the stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of local agricultural commodities. This effort aims to support the growth of local farms and processors, fostering greater access to fresh, locally grown produce for the community. The program’s success will be measured by the volume of sales generated and the number of farmers engaged in developing and implementing sustainable agricultural practices.

Organizaton: County of Riverside Office of Economic Development
Published Project Description: This grant award is being requested by Riverside County Office of Economic Development in partnership with the Blythe Chamber of Commerce to improve the economic conditions of the agricultural producers in the underserved communities of Blythe and the Palo Verde Valley and their residents by developing, operating and expanding a direct producer to consumer Farmers’ Market, to improve access to and consumption of locally and regionally produced agricultural goods, provide critical business and marketing training programs to increase sales, retain existing jobs and create new jobs, respond to the climate crisis and water allocation cuts. A subaward will be granted to the Blythe Chamber of Commerce for outreach, recruitment and retention of producers, outreach, recruitment and retention of Farmers’ Market vendors, outreach, recruitment and retention of customers, management of Farmers’ Market administrative staff, weekly operations oversight of markets, electronic marketing and social media marketing, data collection and sharing with Project Director and local stakeholders and direct community engagement. The intended beneficiaries are the agricultural producers and residents of Blythe and the Palo Verde Valley areas. This grant award is critical to improving the economic outlook for the local economy.
llm_summary: Riverside County Office of Economic Development, in partnership with the Blythe Chamber of Commerce, is seeking a grant to improve the economic conditions for agricultural producers and residents in Blythe and the Palo Verde Valley. This project will develop and operate a direct producer-to-consumer Farmers’ Market, aiming to enhance access to and consumption of locally produced agricultural goods. The core element of this initiative involves creating a marketplace where farmers, ranchers, and processors can sell their products directly to consumers. Anticipated outcomes include increased sales volume for these producers, contributing to the retention of existing jobs and the potential creation of new employment opportunities within the agricultural sector. The project will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, and processors who supply goods to the market, as well as the consumers who purchase these items. Furthermore, the Farmers’ Market will be overseen by the Blythe Chamber of Commerce, who will manage outreach, recruitment, and retention of both producers and vendors, alongside administrative staff, market operations, and electronic marketing strategies, including social media campaigns. Data collection and sharing will be a crucial aspect, facilitating communication with the Project Director and other local stakeholders. This initiative represents a significant step toward bolstering the local economy and establishing a reliable market channel for agricultural products within the Blythe and Palo Verde Valley communities.

Organizaton: San Luis Obispo County Community College District dba Cuesta
Published Project Description:
Cuesta College will collaborate with local economic and food production stakeholders to provide a new direct-to-consumer market that supports underserved farmers and ranchers and provides expanded food access to residents. This project’s purpose is to address accessibility to local food and direct-to-consumer food systems and cultivate regional food economies through collaborative partnerships. Activities include a feasibility study, business development plan, and initial implementation for a new farmers' market in San Luis Obispo County. 
Cuesta College will initiate a sustainable, community-based enterprise with a triple bottom line – benefit to local producers (with additional support for underrepresented producers), local consumers with limited access to local food infrastructure, and community college students. The project’s projected impacts include expanded direct-to-consumer market opportunities for local farm and ranch operations, increased participation from underrepresented producers, and increased access to local food for community residents, particularly those living within or adjacent to the designated low-income/low-access area. Intended outcomes include one new direct producer-to-consumer market access point established, at least 50 producers reporting increased engagement with the new market, and a minimum of 100 new local agricultural product customers. 
Income from the market will help fund student employment at the market, introducing them to higher education and opportunities to study and pursue careers in agriculture that require training beyond high school.
llm_summary: Cuesta College will initiate a new direct-to-consumer market project designed to expand access to local food products and cultivate regional food economies through collaborative partnerships with farmers, ranchers, and other stakeholders. This project will establish a sustainable community-based enterprise focused on creating multiple market access points for local producers and providing increased food options for consumers within San Luis Obispo County. The anticipated outcomes include the successful implementation of one new market access point, with a minimum of 50 producers reporting increased engagement through the market, and the development of a customer base of at least 100 individuals seeking local agricultural products. The primary beneficiaries of this project encompass local farmers and ranchers, as well as consumers seeking increased access to fresh food. Revenue generated from the market will be utilized to fund student employment opportunities, introducing students to higher education and potential careers within the agricultural sector. This initiative aims to support the growth of local food production and strengthen the connections between food producers and the communities they serve, ultimately creating a more robust and resilient regional food system.

Published Project Description: The purpose of the Greater Reedley Farm-To-Table Farmer's Market is to bring consumers face-to-face with farmers to increase consumption of fresh fruits and vegetables while also providing a low-barrier entry point for local farmers to sell produce. Market activities and deliverables are two 10-week markets annually (fall and spring) that will include 1) fresh fruit and/or vegetable vendors (local producers/vendors preferred); 2) food preparation demonstrations, allowing participants to observe the preparation of fresh fruit and vegetables and taste testing; 3) a demonstration and participation in a physical activity such as Zumba, yoga, pickle ball, etc. To increase Market attraction, vendors selling processed foods such as local honey, almonds, olive oil, roasted coffee, crafts booths, and local entertainment will also be included. Market activities are uniquely designed to increase the consumption of fresh produce as a strategy to address the high occurrence of obesity/diabetes in this geographically isolated area where rates are roughly 35%, which is significantly higher than California rates of only 25%.
llm_summary: The Greater Reedley Farm-To-Table Farmer’s Market project aims to foster increased consumption of fresh fruits and vegetables by directly connecting farmers with consumers, creating a low-barrier entry point for local producers to sell their produce. This initiative will encompass two annual markets – a fall and a spring market – each featuring fresh fruit and/or vegetable vendors, prioritized as local producers, along with food preparation demonstrations allowing participants to observe and sample fresh produce. To enhance market appeal and broaden stakeholder engagement, the project will include booths offering processed foods such as local honey, almonds, olive oil, roasted coffee, and crafts. Furthermore, physical activity demonstrations, such as Zumba or pickle ball, will be incorporated to stimulate market attraction. The anticipated outcome of this project is a measurable increase in the consumption of fresh fruits and vegetables within the Reedley area, strategically addressing the elevated rates of obesity and diabetes, which currently stand at approximately 35% within the geographically isolated community. This project will benefit local farmers, processors, and consumers alike, providing a direct channel for the sale of agricultural commodities and promoting healthier eating habits. The project seeks to support the local agricultural economy by facilitating direct sales and establishing new market pathways for fresh produce, ultimately contributing to a healthier population and strengthening the connections between producers and consumers in the Reedley region.

Organizaton: Historic St. Andrews Waterfront Partnership, Inc.
Published Project Description: The Historic St. Andrews Waterfront Partnership, in collaboration with the Panama City Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA) and The LEAD Coalition of Bay County, seeks funding to implement “Farm to Town,” and initiative that will solidify an existing local farmers market—The Market at St. Andrews— and the proposed new Glenwood Farmers Market as reliable and flourishing resources that improve access to fresh, healthy food. This proposed project involves three primary components: • Launch a new farmers market to serve the Glenwood neighborhood of Panama City, classified a food desert, modeled after The Market at St. Andrews, which is owned and operated by the Waterfront Partnership; • In collaboration with a contracted full-service marketing firm (TBD), develop and implement a consumer marketing strategy that aims to increase market visitation while ensuring visitors understand the benefits of healthy eating and are prompted to take advantage of the markets’ provision of fresh food, and • Under the direction of the consulting services of Red Tomato (Providence, RI), establish a food distribution network that allows farms/farmers outside of the conveniently drivable range of Panama City to utilize the St. Andrews and Glenwood markets as sales mechanisms for their produce, meats, poultry, and other locally grown agricultural products. Ultimately, these activities will further activate public community gathering places, secure and grow the base of agricultural producers and growers participating in local farmers markets, and improve conditions surrounding the lack of access to fresh, healthy food for those residing in the St. Andrews and Glenwood neighborhoods and beyond.
llm_summary: The Historic St. Andrews Waterfront Partnership, in collaboration with the Panama City Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA) and The LEAD Coalition of Bay County, seeks funding to implement “Farm to Town,” an initiative designed to establish and grow two thriving farmers markets – The Market at St. Andrews and the proposed Glenwood Farmers Market – as reliable sources of fresh, healthy food. This project will encompass several key components, including the launch of the Glenwood Farmers Market, mirroring the successful model of The Market at St. Andrews, and the creation of a robust distribution network utilizing farms and ranchers outside of immediate driving distance. The Historic St. Andrews Waterfront Partnership will collaborate with a contracted full-service marketing firm to develop and implement a strategy aimed at increasing market visitation while educating consumers on the advantages of consuming fresh produce. Simultaneously, Red Tomato will provide consulting services to establish a comprehensive food distribution system, facilitating the sale of a variety of agricultural products – encompassing grains, livestock feed, dairy, fibers, legumes, and other rotational crops – from producers across the region. Anticipated outcomes include the activation of public gathering places, the expansion of the base of agricultural producers and growers participating in local markets, and ultimately, the improvement of access to fresh food for consumers and stakeholders in the St. Andrews and Glenwood neighborhoods, as well as those utilizing the broader distribution network. The Historic St. Andrews Waterfront Partnership envisions increased sales for farmers and ranchers, greater market presence for agricultural products, and the strengthening of local food systems.

Organizaton: ID IND FOOD AGRICULTURE RESTAURANT & BEVERAGE EST
Published Project Description: FARE Idaho is a trade association structured around the local food system that represents over 340 food and beverage businesses, including over 80 small farmers, ranchers, farmers markets, and livestock processors across Idaho. For this project, FARE Idaho will implement strategies for building local food supply chains in Idaho that provide the skills, knowledge, and resources to increase small producers’ profitability through relationship‐building, marketing, and direct sales to chefs, consumers, and restaurants and reduce waste. Project activities include the following: 1) FARE Idaho will provide marketing assistance for a minimum of 20 farmers, ranchers, and farmers markets with logos, basic websites, digital assets, and social media assistance; 2) Every year in January, FARE Idaho will host a large Field to Fork Festival to connect Idaho producers with Idaho chefs, buyers, and consumers to enhance buying relationships with a focus on strengthening the local food system; 3) FARE Idaho will expand use of its recently launched online platform, which connects producers and buyers to facilitate sales; 4) FARE Idaho will hold in‐person workshops and create accompanying videos that add to our current workshop series on butchering and using whole animals focused on making fresh cheese, bone broth, sausage, and seasonal meal preparations.
llm_summary: FARE Idaho is undertaking a project to build robust local food supply chains within Idaho, aiming to increase the profitability of small producers and reduce food waste. This initiative will achieve this through a multi-faceted approach, including providing marketing assistance – encompassing logos, basic websites, digital assets, and social media support – to a minimum of 20 farmers, ranchers, and farmers markets. Furthermore, FARE Idaho will continue to host its annual Field to Fork Festival, held each January, which connects Idaho producers with Idaho chefs, buyers, and consumers, strengthening buying relationships. The organization will also expand the utilization of its recently launched online platform to facilitate direct sales between producers and buyers.
