Recognizing the challenges faced by farmers who struggle to make a living solely through farm sales, leading to farm closures and reduced food production, this initiative aims to strengthen the LFFN by making direct-to-consumer farms more economically sustainable and facilitating the establishment of new small-scale regenerative farms. The anticipated outcomes include increased sales and consumption of local products, supported by a more robust and resilient LFFN. The primary beneficiaries of this project are farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the Upper Fox River watershed. Specifically, this project addresses critical issues such as the low revenue received by producers – just 14.5 cents per food dollar – and the lack of convenient access to locally sourced products for consumers. Furthermore, it seeks to alleviate the disconnection between food production and consumption, creating a more efficient system where local food systems can thrive. Ultimately, this project intends to support the long-term viability of agricultural operations and bolster the supply of locally produced goods within the region.

Published Project Description: Leprendo is dedicated to empowering small and mid-size farmers, particularly those in traditionally underserved communities throughout Southern California. Our mission is to overcome traditional economic barriers by directly connecting these farmers with consumers through the innovative use of the Leprendo online marketplace. This approach takes on a popular media format consumed by customers through short-form video formats (Tiktok, YouTube shorts, Instagram Reels). Initially focusing on Southern California, from the Central Valley to San Diego, we are set to enhance our platform's functionality and engage farmers through comprehensive digital marketing training. Collaborations with local micro-influencers will play a pivotal role, as they produce compelling short- form videos that showcase the unique stories and high-quality products of our farmers. This strategy is designed to drive consumer interest and sales, significantly boosting farmer visibility and market access. The project goals are: (1) develop online marketplace integrated w/ short-form video, (2) increased sales for farmers through online direct-to-consumer, (3) educating our farmers on short-form video marketplaces and online direct-to-consumer success, and (4) developing and implementing a logistical support system.
llm_summary: Leprendo is dedicated to significantly enhancing market access for small and mid-size farmers throughout Southern California, specifically targeting those in the Central Valley to San Diego region. This project’s purpose is to establish a novel online marketplace integrated with short-form video content, capitalizing on platforms such as TikTok, YouTube Shorts, and Instagram Reels to directly connect farmers with consumers. The core of this initiative involves the development of a digital platform designed to showcase high-quality agricultural products through engaging video content produced in collaboration with local micro-influencers. Anticipated outcomes include a measurable increase in sales for participating farmers via a direct-to-consumer channel and a heightened visibility for their products within the regional market. Furthermore, Leprendo will establish a logistical support system to manage the efficient flow of goods from farm to consumer. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers themselves, alongside the consumers seeking fresh, locally sourced agricultural commodities. The project will also benefit processors and other stakeholders involved in the supply chain. Ultimately, Leprendo aims to create a more robust and accessible market for Southern California’s agricultural producers, fostering economic growth and strengthening the local food system.

Published Project Description:
Moon Valley Farm's (MVF) Year-Round Online Farmers Market (OFM) Expansion project will 
strategically grow our partnerships by 75+ regional producers, market them through storytelling and 
expand our delivery routes by thousands of new customers. The mission is to increase the capacity 
of our farm hub to collaborate with more farmers, sell to more local customers and to reach 
communities in low-income and low-access areas. To accomplish growing our farmer partnerships, we 
will collaborate with the Department of Agriculture of Frederick County and Beginner Farmer 
Training Programs run by two regional non-profits: Future Harvest and ECO City Farms to link with 
specialty crop growers who will benefit from additional sales outlets. Through investing in 
videography, photography, advertising and marketing funnels and by launching a new delivery route 
to 4 Mid-Atlantic cities: Baltimore, Maryland, Washington, DC, Frederick, Maryland and Northern 
Virginia, the OFM will provide a robust sales channel for producers and healthy local food to over 
5000 new customers.
The first objective of this project is to form partnerships with 75 or more new producers with a 
commitment that over half are socially-disadvantaged. To accomplish this, MVF will hire an 
Aggregation Manager to strategically form and cultivate new farm producer relationships by 
collaborating with the Office of Agriculture and non-profit organizations Future Harvest and ECO 
City Farms. Outside of this, the Aggregation Manager will onboard the new farmers by showcasing 
this opportunity to a wide pool of regional growers, field their questions and cultivate mutually 
beneficial partnerships. For long term proficiency and resilience, the Aggregation Manager will 
ensure the new farmers' logistics are streamlined and attended to, their products are food safe, in 
attractive packaging and that their farm operations and products are highlighted in our marketing. 
The second objective is to generate professional, evergreen marketing materials for the growers by 
contracting with graphic design, photography and videography professionals to capture their 
stories. Our marketing team will employ the collaborative strategies outlined in our marketing plan 
to engage our robust network of email subscribers and social media followers to expand this retail 
channel. We'll profile the new producers on our website, which boasted an impressive SEO score of 
97/100 in a 2023 digital audit to reach our 5000 unique visitors every month. The first 2 years of 
the project will capture the lives and stories of our network of farmers so that we can utilize 
these materials in targeted, optimized marketing campaigns and these will be utilized in a 
strategic advertising campaign to generate thousands of new leads across four cities.
llm_summary: Moon Valley Farm’s Year-Round Online Farmers Market Expansion project aims to strategically grow its producer partnerships to over 75 regional farmers, marketing them through compelling storytelling and expanding delivery routes to reach thousands of new customers across four Mid-Atlantic cities: Baltimore, Maryland; Washington, DC; Frederick, Maryland; and Northern Virginia. This project will establish a robust sales channel for producers and provide healthy local food to an anticipated 5,000 new consumers, primarily farmers, ranchers, and other stakeholders involved in the agricultural supply chain. The core of this initiative involves onboarding new producers through an Aggregation Manager who will collaborate with the Office of Agriculture and non-profit organizations Future Harvest and ECO City Farms to build mutually beneficial partnerships, ensuring the new farmers’ logistics are streamlined, their products are food safe, and their operations are highlighted in marketing efforts. Simultaneously, professional graphic design, photography, and videography services will be utilized to create evergreen marketing materials showcasing the stories and products of these producers, leveraging a website with a strong SEO score to drive targeted marketing campaigns and generate leads. Ultimately, this project will bolster the capacity of Moon Valley Farm to collaborate with more farmers, sell to a larger customer base, and connect producers with new market opportunities, benefiting the entire agricultural community and creating a reliable supply of organic food for consumers.

Published Project Description:
Locally Grown is an Uber Eats-style marketplace for small farms selling direct to consumers. Our mission is to simplify
marketing and operations for local producers by connecting them directly to their target market and providing a simple way to
manage orders and inventory. We currently support 50 farms in North Carolina and over 4,500 consumers.
This initiative is designed to generate $750,000 in total farmer revenue by expanding our capacity to onboard additional farms
up to our goal of 1,000 local U.S producers, and to attract 100,000 app downloads from consumers eager to support our farm
partners. This will be accomplished by adding marketplace features requested by many of our farm partners and applying
targeted marketing strategies to boost consumer engagement and subsequently farm revenues.
Key activities funded by this grant include enhancing technical resources, deploying new marketplace features like notifications
for past customers and localized promotions to help farmers reach their audience, and developing marketing materials to
promote our farm partners and attract new customers. These enhancements will increase the visibility of local farms and make
the buying process more accessible and efficient for consumers, contributing to a more connected local food system.
llm_summary: Locally Grown is a marketplace designed to simplify marketing and operations for small farms, connecting them directly to their target market and offering a straightforward way to manage orders and inventory. This project aims to generate $750,000 in total farmer revenue by expanding the platform to include 1,000 local U.S. producers, concurrently attracting 100,000 app downloads from consumers eager to support our farm partners. The core of this initiative involves the development of enhanced technical resources and the implementation of new marketplace features, including notifications for past customers and localized promotions, to increase the visibility of local farms and make the buying process more accessible and efficient for consumers. Specifically, Locally Grown will focus on supporting farmers by providing tools to manage their inventory and connect with their customer base, thereby boosting sales and streamlining operations. The anticipated outcomes include a significant increase in revenue for participating farmers and expanded access to locally sourced agricultural products for consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers, ranchers, and processors involved in the local agricultural supply chain, alongside the consumers seeking fresh, regional food options. By facilitating direct connections between producers and buyers, Locally Grown contributes to a more connected local food system, ultimately supporting the economic viability of farms and providing consumers with convenient access to a wider range of organically produced goods.

Published Project Description:
This project will equip local producers with the knowledge, practical experience, and continued guidance needed to successfully market, sell, and scale their agricultural products at Farmers Markets. This four-month program will be offered twice a year, with each session enrolling a cohort of 10 producers, four of whom will be producers with 0-1 years of experience in markets. The program will be delivered through online gatherings, in-person workshops, mentoring, and peer-to-peer support offered in three phases: Farmers Market Foundations, Farmers Market Success, and Farmers Market Longevity. In addition, a Farmers Market 101 workshop will be offered monthly and open to the public.During the pilot of the program we will focus on beneficiaries associated with the Moreno Valley Market, Rancho Cucamonga Market, or Chino Hills Market, 67% of whom are POC. The ongoing evaluation of this program will measure business and profit growth for producers, increases in the quality and customer engagement of markets supporting the local community, and decreases in retail- level and consumer-level food waste. At the conclusion of this project, each participant will have:
-Certifications, equipment, and permits for operating as a vendor -An identifiable brand, marketing strategy, and social media content calendar -In-person marketing strategies for increasing customer engagement -business evaluation systems, and -A step-by-step plan to expand their business to additional markets
llm_summary: This project aims to equip local farmers with the knowledge and resources needed to successfully operate and expand their agricultural product sales through Farmers Markets. The initiative will provide a comprehensive four-month program, delivered twice annually, enrolling cohorts of ten producers, with a focus on supporting those with limited market experience. The program will progress through three phases – Farmers Market Foundations, Farmers Market Success, and Farmers Market Longevity – incorporating monthly 101 workshops open to the public. Participants will receive certifications, necessary equipment, and required permits to operate as vendors, alongside the development of identifiable brands, tailored marketing strategies, and social media content calendars. Furthermore, they will gain access to in-person marketing strategies designed to increase customer engagement and establish business evaluation systems. Upon completion, each participant will have a step-by-step plan to expand their business operations to additional markets, contributing to increased sales volume for agricultural products within the local community. The project will measure success through business and profit growth among the participating farmers, improvements in market quality and customer engagement, and a reduction in food waste at retail and consumer levels. The primary beneficiaries of this project include local farmers, ranchers, and processors, as well as the consumers who purchase these agricultural products. The project’s objective is to bolster the existing organic market infrastructure and drive increased demand for locally sourced agricultural commodities.

Published Project Description: The City of Torrance, California requests $157,628.35 to implement the Torrance Farmers' Market - Service for Seniors project. The project will improve the Market's accessibility and reach through a distribution program targeted at senior citizens, residents with disabilities, and all others facing mobility obstacles which prevent them from navigating the busy Marketplace. Participating residents will receive pre-boxed, assorted fresh produce packages at public distribution sites strategically located throughout the City, allowing them ease of access to local grown food while still engaging with their local community on a frequent basis. Produce packages will include carefully chosen, diverse products along with recipe cards including ingredients from the package, promoting culinary education and widening participants' food experiences. The program is expected to increase Market usage and sales by 6%. This project will additionally benefit Torrance's local farmers and ranchers who utilize the Market, providing them with wider distribution opportunities to their customer base and allowing them to strategize on food products to include in the boxes, in order to minimize produce waste and promote new, unique, or surplus produce. Market staff will work closely with supplying producers and program recipients to improve producer-to-consumer operations, ensuring that Torrance's senior community has access to healthy, fresh, locally grown produce.
llm_summary: The City of Torrance requests $157,628.35 to implement the Torrance Farmers’ Market – Service for Seniors project, a comprehensive initiative designed to enhance access to locally grown produce for a significant segment of the community. This project will establish a distribution program targeting senior citizens, residents with mobility challenges, and others who experience difficulties navigating the busy Torrance Farmers’ Market. Through this program, participants will receive pre-boxed packages of assorted fresh produce, strategically distributed at public locations throughout the City, offering convenient access to locally sourced food while simultaneously fostering community engagement. These packages will feature a carefully selected range of products, alongside recipe cards incorporating ingredients from the boxes, encouraging participants to broaden their culinary experiences. The anticipated outcome of this project is an increase of 6% in Market usage and sales, directly benefiting Torrance’s local farmers and ranchers by providing expanded distribution opportunities and facilitating strategic planning to minimize produce waste. This will ensure that producers can effectively manage their inventories and offer a wider selection of goods. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the senior community members and the farmers and ranchers who supply the market. The project seeks to improve producer-to-consumer operations, fostering stronger relationships between stakeholders within the Torrance Farmers’ Market ecosystem and ultimately ensuring access to fresh, healthy produce for the community.

Published Project Description: The Tukwila Village Farmers Market (Tukwila Village) provides important food access to Low Income/Low Food Access (LI/LA) communities in Tukwila, Washington. The market was founded in 2017 to specifically support entry-level immigrant, refugee, and BIPOC vendors, support customers to use food benefits, and to create a unique and welcoming market space for the diverse community. Tukwila Village was co-founded by Global to Local's Food Innovation Network and International Rescue Committee's New Roots Program, with ongoing technical assistance provided by Public Health - Seattle & King County. This project will support Tukwila Village in strategically increasing their customers, vendors, and operational capacity. To accomplish this, they will conduct community outreach to assess needs and desires, revamp their promotional activity, restructure their market's incentive program (Heart Bucks), conduct targeted recruitment to diversify the vendors, develop a volunteer program, and complete a strategic plan. Through this project, Tukwila Village will be able to grow to a new level to support more vendors and customers in accessing fresh, local, cultural produce.
llm_summary: The Tukwila Village Farmers Market aims to significantly expand its reach and operational capabilities to better support local farmers and consumers. This project will focus on increasing the number of vendors and customers accessing the market, achieved through a multi-faceted approach including targeted community outreach to assess needs and preferences, a revamped promotional strategy, and a restructured incentive program – Heart Bucks – to encourage participation. Furthermore, the project will undertake targeted recruitment efforts to broaden the range of vendors participating in the market, seeking to incorporate a wider selection of agricultural products. To support this expansion, the market will establish a volunteer program to bolster its daily operations. Ultimately, the Tukwila Village Farmers Market seeks to create a more robust and accessible space for the exchange of fresh, local agricultural commodities, serving as a key resource for the community. Through these efforts, the market intends to enhance its capacity to facilitate the movement of agricultural goods, strengthening connections between producers and those seeking access to nutritious food options. The project anticipates a positive impact on local producers and a greater availability of fresh produce for the community, building a stronger, more resilient local food system. This initiative will serve a wide range of stakeholders involved in the agricultural supply chain, from farmers to consumers, and will contribute to improved access to a variety of food products.

Published Project Description:
The Jacksonville Farmers Market (JFM), North Florida's oldest and largest operating farmers market, is
grappling with a significant decline in vendors, customers, and overall vibrancy. Despite being situated
in a USDA Priority Area, the market has lost its prominence as a primary food source for the
community.
The current landowner approached Feeding Northeast Florida (FNEFL) to assume management of the
Jacksonville Market. With prompting and support from the City, we are exploring how best to revitalize
the market that benefits both consumers and local food producers. FNEFL's objective is to boost the
involvement of local food producers and restore the market's prominence as a leading sales venue in
the region. By collaborating strategically with community partners, the JFM can expand market access,
aggregation, and distribution channels for small and medium-sized producers.
FNEFL is seeking a grant to develop a comprehensive business and management plan in preparation
for assuming operational control. FNEFL will enlist the expertise of a consultant to devise a phased
implementation process to reestablish the market as a primary sales outlet. We recognize that our
plans remain contingent on input from our neighbors, farmers, food producers, and regional
stakeholders, and we stand to listen and learn from people and families who will frequent this space to
ensure the market reflects their preferences and requirements.
llm_summary: The Jacksonville Farmers Market is undertaking a project to revitalize its operations and restore its prominence as a key sales venue for local food producers within North Florida. The primary goal of this initiative, supported by a grant, is to significantly increase the involvement of farmers, ranchers, and other food producers, alongside boosting customer engagement to reinvigorate the market’s overall vibrancy. Specifically, Feeding Northeast Florida (FNEFL) will develop a comprehensive business and management plan, utilizing the expertise of a consultant, to implement a phased approach for market restoration. This plan will focus on expanding market access, aggregation, and distribution channels for small and medium-sized producers, aiming to provide greater sales opportunities for agricultural commodities. The anticipated outcomes include a substantial increase in the volume of locally produced goods available at the market, ultimately benefiting both consumers seeking fresh food sources and the producers supplying them. The project will prioritize supporting those involved in the production of organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops—items currently representing a critical need within the regional market. The beneficiaries of this project encompass a broad range of stakeholders, including farmers, ranchers, processors, and ultimately, the local community who rely on access to fresh, locally sourced agricultural products. Through strategic collaboration and market expansion, FNEFL seeks to reestablish the Jacksonville Farmers Market as a central hub for regional agricultural commerce and enhance the availability of key agricultural commodities.

Published Project Description:
Schenectady Greenmarket's project aims to foster diversity among market vendors and customers through recruitment,
outreach, and retention strategies, with a focus on historically underserved populations. It seeks to support historically
underserved producers by providing resources such as a Vendor Success Toolkit and small business trainings, facilitated
by the Community Loan Fund. Additionally, mentorship opportunities will be offered by senior vendors to new vendors to
refine their marketing strategies. The project also intends to create an inclusive environment by expanding the market’s
Food Box Program and increasing marketing and outreach efforts to low-income and socially disadvantaged community
members. Expansion of the Food Box Program will provide additional revenue streams for local producers and increased
access to fresh, affordable foods for low-income Schenectady residents. Collaboration with community partners like Soul
Fire Farm will enhance awareness and accessibility of the Food Box Program and other market services among low-income
communities, while also supporting the market in increasing customer diversity through educational food demonstrations
and workshops highlighting culturally significant foods. Overall, these efforts aim to support the success and sustainability of
historically underserved producers, increase vendor and customer diversity within the market space, and improve access to
local foods for low-income residents._x000D_
llm_summary: Schenectady Greenmarket’s project aims to bolster the success and long-term viability of local producers while simultaneously expanding access to fresh food for Schenectady residents. The core of this initiative involves several key elements, including the provision of a Vendor Success Toolkit and support for small businesses, alongside mentorship opportunities facilitated by experienced market vendors. Specifically, the project intends to grow the market’s Food Box Program, creating additional revenue streams for producers and increasing the availability of affordable food options for the community. Collaboration with partners like Soul Fire Farm will enhance awareness and accessibility of the Food Box Program and other market services, targeting those with limited resources. The anticipated outcomes include increased sales for participating farmers and ranchers, alongside greater consumer engagement with local agricultural products. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers, ranchers, and processors involved in supplying the market, as well as the consumers seeking access to fresh food. Through expanded market offerings and strategic outreach, Schenectady Greenmarket seeks to strengthen its position as a vital local resource, supporting sustainable agricultural practices and promoting equitable access to wholesome food for all stakeholders. Ultimately, the project strives to enhance the market’s overall capacity and foster a stronger connection between producers and the community they serve.

Published Project Description:
This project will improve food access for refugees and low-income residents in the Mountain View and Muldoon neighborhoods of East Anchorage by supporting multiple food access channels through Catholic Social Services' Refugee Assistance and Immigration Services (RAIS) program, aligning with the Farmers Market Promotion Program's "Capacity Building" focus.
Our objectives for this project include 1) To create a food access hub at Grow North Farm through the coordination of a CSA, roadside stand, and farmers market. Our current program conducts limited outreach to nearby residents despite our ability to provide discounts for nutritional assistance recipients, which is something that we plan to expand.2)  We will assist beginner refugee farmers with selling their produce through various sales channels - CSA, farmers markets, wholesale, etc.  3)  We will expand our value-added goods program to promote increased earning potential for refugee farmers. Our current value-added goods program needs strategic business planning to ensure long-term sustainability. We will equip refugees with skills to create value-added products and foster entrepreneurship. Refugee entrepreneurs face significant barriers in starting businesses and accessing markets such as language barriers and unfamiliar regulations. 4) We will develop a strategic plan to expand and operate the Muldoon Farmers Market. This long-standing community farmers market in a low-income area of Anchorage is at risk of closing.
llm_summary: Catholic Social Services’ Refugee Assistance and Immigration Services (RAIS) program is undertaking a vital project to enhance food access for refugees and low-income residents in the Mountain View and Muldoon neighborhoods of East Anchorage. This initiative will establish a multi-faceted food access hub centered at Grow North Farm, integrating a Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) program, a roadside stand, and a farmers market to increase the availability of fresh produce to local consumers. Simultaneously, the project will provide support to beginner refugee farmers, enabling them to sell their produce through various channels, including CSA, farmers markets, and wholesale opportunities. A key component of this effort is the expansion of a value-added goods program, which will equip refugee entrepreneurs with the skills and resources needed to create and market processed agricultural products, fostering increased earning potential and promoting self-sufficiency. Specifically, the project will address the critical need to develop a strategic plan for the operation and expansion of the Muldoon Farmers Market, a long-standing community market at risk of closure, ensuring continued access to agricultural products for the local population. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened local food system, improving access to fresh food for farmers and consumers alike, and building a more resilient local economy. Through these focused efforts, RAIS aims to support the economic viability of refugee farmers and enhance the overall food landscape within the targeted communities, creating sustainable pathways for agricultural production and sales.

Published Project Description: Northwest Agriculture Business Center seeks to contribute towards breaking down barriers to economic success, and meet USDA objectives to develop, coordinate, and expand direct producer-to-consumer marketing and strategies for local producers to enhance existing market channels and develop new revenue opportunities. Through this project, our organization will facilitate expansion of existing markets via the Genuine Skagit Valley program’s Farmstand Fresh and other promotional campaigns. Consumers will be drawn to Skagit County and surrounding communities through promotion of agritourism activities and farm stand products through paid advertising, social media, website links, and cross-promotion partnerships and collaborations.  Consumers will be encouraged to favor Skagit farm products in buying choices, as identified by the Genuine Skagit Valley certification mark.  Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) transaction education will introduce the opportunity of new markets and consumer segments to farm stand operators, with access to governmental entity resources and enrollment technical assistance. Program participation will be improved through farmer outreach. Barriers to program benefits for non-English speaking Latinx producers will be lowered through translation and interpretation of promotional toolkit and other materials into Spanish, and by working with producers to improve culturally relevant pathways to participation.
llm_summary: Northwest Agriculture Business Center seeks to enhance economic opportunities for local producers within Skagit County and surrounding communities, aligning with USDA objectives for direct producer-to-consumer marketing strategies. This project will expand existing market channels through initiatives like the Genuine Skagit Valley Farmstand Fresh program and related promotional campaigns, aiming to attract consumers to agritourism activities and farm stand products utilizing paid advertising, social media engagement, website links, and strategic cross-promotion partnerships. The core objective is to encourage consumer preference for Skagit farm products, signified by the Genuine Skagit Valley certification mark, thereby increasing sales and revenue streams for participating farmers and ranchers. A key component of this effort involves providing farm stand operators with Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) transaction education, offering access to relevant governmental resources and enrollment technical assistance, allowing them to tap into new consumer segments. To maximize participation, Northwest Agriculture Business Center will address barriers faced by non-English speaking Latinx producers through the provision of translated promotional toolkit materials and interpretation services, working collaboratively with producers to establish culturally relevant pathways to engagement. This initiative anticipates increased sales volume for farmers and ranchers, improved access to markets for processors and stakeholders, and a greater volume of Skagit farm products available to consumers. Ultimately, this project intends to strengthen the local agricultural economy by facilitating greater market access for producers and broadening the reach of Skagit County’s agricultural offerings.

Published Project Description: To meet the surging demand for affordable and accessible food during the pandemic, CJ formed the Produce Buyers Club by building a coalition of Atlanta nonprofits serving low-income, low-access (LILA) communities to purchase and distribute Georgia farmers' surplus produce. With our ongoing efforts, a significant portion of this market remains untapped.
llm_summary: CJ initiated the Produce Buyers Club to address the growing need for accessible food options during a period of increased demand. This project focuses on facilitating the purchase of surplus produce from Georgia farmers by establishing a coalition of Atlanta nonprofits serving low-income, low-access communities. The core activity involves the aggregation and distribution of agricultural commodities, specifically targeting grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, and other rotational crops currently unavailable in organic form. The anticipated outcome is to significantly increase the market reach for these commodities, ensuring greater access for consumers and supporting farmers in moving excess production. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the agricultural supply chain. The project aims to create new market pathways for these commodities, improving access to food resources for the communities served by the coalition of nonprofits. By connecting producers with consumers, the Produce Buyers Club intends to maximize the utilization of agricultural resources and contribute to a more robust and efficient food distribution system.

Published Project Description:
The proposed initiative aims to provide new markets for local produce farms and wider access to their produce for residents
of at least three underserved neighborhoods in South Jersey by operating weekly farmers markets in areas that have not
been able to sustain commercial farmers markets in the past. The core objective is to connect more local and hyper-local
growers with more underserved consumers, to the benefit of both. Our premise is that nonprofits can facilitate markets that
are financially worthwhile for growers while providing access to produce at prices low-income residents can afford.
The collaborating farms and nonprofits will work with additional local growers to aggregate and transport produce from rural
and urban growers and sell the produce through at least three farmers market stands at prices each neighborhood can
support, including but not limited to consumers using SNAP and other benefit programs. Through experience and customer
surveys, we will learn about the produce varieties, pricing, presentation and food education services that can sustain each
market into the future. By serving as anchor stands and demonstrating the methods that make each location economically
successful, the initiative aims to recruit additional farmers (in addition to Rancocas Creek Farm) and individual retailers to
join each site. The proposed grant will enable the collaborating farms and nonprofits to work with at least nine additional
growers and create at least three markets. Over the two-year grant period, we will develop business plans based on local
experience to sustain each market into the future.
llm_summary: The Rancocas Creek Farm initiative aims to establish weekly farmers markets in three designated locations within South Jersey, fostering new market opportunities for local produce farms and expanding access to their goods for residents. This project will facilitate the aggregation and transport of produce from multiple growers, including Rancocas Creek Farm and at least nine additional farmers and producers, through the operation of at least three market stands. The anticipated outcomes include increased sales for participating farmers and the provision of fresh produce to consumers in the target communities. The project will focus on developing market strategies that ensure each location can sustain operations, supported by data gathered through customer surveys and market analysis. Specifically, the initiative will explore optimal pricing structures and presentation methods to maximize sales volume and consumer engagement. The beneficiaries of this project encompass local farmers, producers, and consumers seeking access to locally grown agricultural commodities. Through the establishment of these markets, the project seeks to create a viable business model for farmers and provide affordable produce options to residents. The project’s success will be measured by the number of participating farmers, the volume of produce sold, and the establishment of sustainable market operations, leading to increased access to fresh produce for the target communities.

Published Project Description:
This project will leverage community resources for enhancing the grower-consumer relationship at the Main Street Market of Tyndall. The project will support a local market for growers and consumers. Project work includes regular food demonstration
meals held at area venues to promote local products.  The market will serve a a venue for a Community Supported Agriculture 'food box subscription' program that establishes season-long sales demand for growers. The project will also work with the local school system to create age-appropriate programs that explain all aspects of the local food market.
llm_summary: The Main Street Market project aims to strengthen the connection between growers and consumers at the Tyndall market by establishing a robust local market system. This project will facilitate the creation of regular food demonstration meals held at various locations to promote the sale of locally produced agricultural commodities, and it will support a Community Supported Agriculture ‘food box’ subscription program, which will generate consistent sales demand for local growers and ranchers. A key component of this initiative is collaboration with the local school system to develop age-appropriate educational programs that explain the entire local food market system to consumers and stakeholders. The anticipated outcome of this project is an increased availability of locally grown products for consumers and a more stable market channel for growers. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the local agricultural community. The project will concentrate on building a sustainable system for the distribution of agricultural goods, contributing to a stronger and more resilient local food economy. This project seeks to establish a predictable market for growers’ products, increasing their operational stability and supporting their long-term viability. The project’s success will be measured by the volume of locally produced goods sold through the market and the level of consumer engagement within the community.

Published Project Description: The intent of this FMPP proposal is to connect, coordinate and cultivate our local food economy through public-private partnerships to create a new International Farmers Market in West Boise. This new direct producer-to-consumer market will increase the capacity of our local food system and expand mid-tier value chains. It will create a new fresh food resource in an economically diverse LI-LA neighborhood and expand economic opportunities for small acreage producers of ethnic produce.  Global Lounge, a multi-cultural enterprise, will add coordination, volunteers, entertainment, and food vendors. Activities include planning, supporting partnerships, marketing, and adding structure including vendor agreements, staffing, operations, and technology. Effectively incorporating technology for sales will be supported by a consultant from the Boise Farmers Market. The farmers will have an active role in shaping a culturally rich marketplace and new access point for sales.  Global Gardens refugee farmers will gain an alternative to large up-scale markets where their profits are lower than their investment. The LI-LA community will have a new opportunity to access fresh, local, and ethnic varieties, and increase fresh food consumption. Strong community participation, and increased sales for farmers will result. It will allow farmers to pilot new value-added products. Deliverables will record farmer adaptation to technology, marketing materials, data on sales and customer traffic.
llm_summary: The Global Lounge International Farmers Market project aims to establish a new direct producer-to-consumer market in West Boise, fostering a strengthened local food economy through public-private partnerships. This initiative will encompass the creation of a marketplace that increases the capacity of the local food system and expands mid-tier value chains, specifically targeting ethnic produce grown by small acreage farmers. The project’s core activities involve meticulous planning, active partnership support, comprehensive marketing efforts, and the implementation of structured operational processes, including vendor agreements, staffing protocols, and technology integration, all supported by a consultant from the Boise Farmers Market. Anticipated outcomes include increased sales for farmers, providing them with a new access point for sales and enabling them to pilot new value-added products. The market will benefit farmers, consumers, and processors by generating a fresh food resource in a geographically concentrated area, and bolstering economic opportunities for those producing a range of agricultural commodities. Specifically, the project will support farmers in the LI-LA community providing them with access to fresh, local, and ethnic produce varieties. Furthermore, Global Gardens refugee farmers will benefit from a market alternative to larger, less profitable markets. The project will record farmer adaptation to technology and collect data on sales and customer traffic as key deliverables. These outcomes will contribute to a strengthened market for farmers and support a broader range of agricultural production.

Published Project Description:
Since 2008, Catholic Charities of Northeast Kansas, in partnership with Cultivate KC, has managed the New Roots program, a 4-year farmer training program and incubator farm for refugees and immigrants with agricultural backgrounds who wish to launch their own small farm businesses. Forty six families have graduated from the program (32 of which are still actively farming in the area), and approximately 12 families are in the 4-year training program each year. Both organizations are committed to growing the program. Through many years of experience and with the input of program participants, we have built a strong program emphasizing participatory education, language access, equity, self- sufficiency, and graduate success. Though participants have a wealth of agricultural experience, marketing and expanding sales continue to be a challenge due to language and cultural barriers, amongst other factors.
Additionally, the local community lacks consistent and convenient access to fresh produce. “New Roots Marketing and Sales Expansion to Support Farmers with Language Barriers in Kansas City” aims to address these challenges by increasing opportunities for the community to access fresh, local produce while expanding farmers' sales through a variety of avenues and increasing the number of new farmers in Kansas City.
llm_summary: Catholic Charities of Northeast Kansas, in partnership with Cultivate KC, is undertaking a project to address critical market needs for organic agricultural commodities within the Kansas City area. The primary goal of this initiative is to increase the availability of fresh, local produce to consumers and to expand sales opportunities for farmers participating in the New Roots program. This project will focus on providing resources to support farmers in overcoming marketing and sales challenges, a consistent obstacle for the program’s graduates. Specifically, the project will concentrate on building enhanced pathways for these farmers to reach a wider customer base, facilitating increased sales of their products. Anticipated outcomes include a greater volume of locally sourced produce reaching the community and strengthened financial stability for the farmers involved. The beneficiaries of this project encompass a range of stakeholders, including farmers, ranchers, and processors operating within the Kansas City region. Ultimately, this project aims to bolster the local food system by connecting producers with consumers seeking fresh agricultural goods, supporting increased sales and facilitating greater access to local food sources.

Published Project Description: The Ivanhoe Farmers Market, in partnership with Kansas City Black Urban Growers, will utilize USDA Farmers Market Promotion Program funds to strengthen the capacity of a crucial direct-to-consumer farmers market operation within the local food system, support food producers in the development of marketing strategies that are culturally and technologically relevant, and drive access and consumption of locally produced agriculture products. In alignment with key project goals and identified objectives of the FMPP, the collaborative partnership and probetween the two community-based organizations will drive the following outcomes: an increase in community engagement in the local food economy, an increase of upward mobility opportunity for local producers, and an increase in the local food consumption. The successful expansion of market operations, awareness of fresh, locally grown foods producers, and the training and development of minority, urban farmers will create significantly more direct to-consumer sales that benefit both the small, historically underserved producers and an urban community facing food insecurity.
llm_summary: The Ivanhoe Farmers Market, in partnership with Kansas City Black Urban Growers, will utilize USDA Farmers Market Promotion Program funds to strengthen a critical direct-to-consumer farmers market operation within the local food system. This project aims to support farmers and producers in the development of marketing strategies that are relevant to the current market conditions, driving increased access and consumption of locally produced agricultural products. The core of this initiative involves expanding the market’s capacity to facilitate sales of fresh, locally grown products, directly benefiting consumers and supporting the operations of producers and processors. Anticipated outcomes include a measurable increase in engagement within the local food economy, alongside opportunities for producers to advance their businesses. Specifically, this project will support the availability of a wider range of agricultural commodities, including grains, livestock feed, dairy, and other rotational crops. The successful expansion of market operations and increased awareness of local products will create more direct sales channels for producers and those involved in processing. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, and processors, as well as the consumers seeking access to fresh agricultural goods. The project’s overall goal is to bolster the local food system and facilitate economic advancement for those involved in its production and distribution.

Published Project Description: This project will develop and expand the capacity of a successful Farmers Market and Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) program to operate year-round. The result will be increased revenue for local farmers and improved access and availability of healthy foods for an underserved community. St. Luke's Episcopal Church, located in the heart of downtown Jamestown, NY, oversees the Jamestown Public Market, a vibrant program that has operated in the area for over 100 years. Currently running from June-October, the initiative includes a weekly outdoor farmers market and the Eat Fresh, Do Good CSA. In response to a growing push from farmers and consumers, this project will launch an extended direct-to-consumer-sales schedule by adding winter and spring CSAs as well as an indoor farmers market in the offseason. Like the current programming, SNAP and the Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program will be accepted. This project will help develop new product offerings, and retain customers and farmer vendors, including at least two historically underserved producers. Free training for farmers will be offered in partnership with Cornell Cooperative Extension in Chautauqua County and will include education on business, marketing, and the development of value-added agricultural products. Targeted outreach to people in Jamestown's low-income households and food desert neighborhoods will help ensure that the expanded programming is accessed by the community members who need it most.
llm_summary: St. Luke’s Episcopal Church is undertaking a project to expand the Jamestown Public Market and Eat Fresh, Do Good CSA program to operate year-round, aiming to increase revenue for local farmers and improve access to healthy foods within the Jamestown community. This initiative will encompass the development of new offerings, including winter and spring CSAs, as well as an indoor farmers market during the off-season, alongside the existing weekly outdoor market. The project anticipates bolstering the supply chain for farmers and consumers alike, facilitating the growth of agricultural production and distribution. Key to this expansion is the support of at least two historically limited producers, ensuring a broader range of agricultural goods are available. The project will focus on the aggregation, storage, and distribution of organic agricultural commodities, creating additional market channels for farmers. The anticipated outcomes include an increased flow of organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes and other rotational crops, and organic ingredients. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers and ranchers involved in the supply chain, along with the consumers who will have greater access to fresh food options. St. Luke’s Episcopal Church recognizes the need to support those involved in the production and distribution of these goods, and to ensure that these goods are accessible to all stakeholders. This expansion will create opportunities for greater economic viability for agricultural businesses and will strengthen the local food system.

Published Project Description: The purpose of the project is to collect key indoor farmers market facility and stall design needs and specifications from 20 interested Fulton Stall Market farmers and producers. After design needs and specifications are identified, a farmer- focused architectural design plan will be created, and a financial proforma and business plan developed for the Seaport Public Market, a multi-vendor indoor farmers market in Lower Manhattan. The intended beneficiaries are participating New York and regional farmers, consumers, low-income residents of adjacent Lower East Side and Chinatown neighborhoods served by Fulton Stall Market. Also, this project will benefit the economy and social vitality of Lower Manhattan harmed by 9/11, Hurricane Sandy, and COVID-19 pandemic
llm_summary: The Fulton Stall Market project aims to collect critical indoor farmers market facility and stall design needs and specifications from twenty interested farmers and producers. This project will result in a farmer-focused architectural design plan for the Seaport Public Market, a multi-vendor indoor farmers market in Lower Manhattan, alongside the development of a financial proforma and business plan. The anticipated outcome is the creation of a functional market space designed to meet the specific requirements of participating farmers, processors, and stakeholders, supporting the aggregation and distribution of organic agricultural commodities. This market will directly benefit farmers and ranchers seeking new distribution channels for their products, as well as consumers seeking access to fresh agricultural goods. The primary beneficiaries include New York and regional farmers, consumers, and low-income residents of adjacent Lower East Side and Chinatown neighborhoods served by Fulton Stall Market. Furthermore, this project contributes to the economic and social vitality of Lower Manhattan, addressing challenges stemming from past events like 9/11, Hurricane Sandy, and the COVID-19 pandemic. The Seaport Public Market is designed to facilitate the movement of organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes and other rotational crops, and organic ingredients.

Published Project Description: Nourish Knoxville’s (NK) Digging Deeper project will help bridge the gap between producers’ need for more direct-to-consumer market opportunities and buyers’ increasing interest in local food. The project will enlist marketing professionals, producers, buyers, and seven partnering organizations to develop and promote a marketing campaign with impactful, user-friendly, accessible resources to connect the East Tennessee local food system. NK will overhaul their printed local food directory into an agritourism-focused local food guide that will expand to cover 36 counties with a combined population of 2.5 million. Concurrently, NK will launch the online East Tennessee Local Food Guide, offering user-specific gateways to find agritourist experiences with maps and farm trails, wholesale providers, CSAs, restaurants and stores featuring local foods, local artisanal food producers, and farmers markets. NK and its partners across the region will actively promote registrations into and use of both guides to their networks and the public; partners will receive subawards for their efforts. By 2027, the project will provide 30,000 print copies to 190 locations, inform 1,300 producer beneficiaries about new market opportunities, promote over 300 producer beneficiaries, and provide local food information to 58,000 East Tennesseans. Digging Deeper will increase producers’ economic opportunities, increase access to local food, and strengthen the capacity of our regional local food network.
llm_summary: Nourish Knoxville’s (NK) Digging Deeper project aims to bridge the gap between local food producers and consumer demand, ultimately strengthening the East Tennessee regional food network. This initiative will develop and promote comprehensive marketing resources, including a redesigned print agritourism-focused local food guide and an online East Tennessee Local Food Guide. The project will expand to cover 36 counties, encompassing a population of 2.5 million, offering consumers access to agritourism experiences through maps and farm trails, alongside connections to wholesale providers, Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) programs, restaurants and stores featuring local foods, local artisanal food producers, and farmers markets. By 2027, NK anticipates distributing 30,000 print copies to 190 locations, informing approximately 1,300 producer beneficiaries about potential market opportunities, supporting over 300 producer beneficiaries with increased market access, and providing local food information to 58,000 East Tennesseans. The project will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the regional food system, enhancing their capacity to reach consumers and build sustainable businesses. Furthermore, NK will facilitate connections between producers and consumers seeking local food options. This project is expected to increase the economic opportunities available to producers and improve access to locally sourced food products for the wider community.

Published Project Description:
This project will inject strategic investments into improving and strengthening market systems and xperiences, benefiting
our low income shoppers, our small producers who rely on this direct market, and our community as a 
whole by creating a more robust and resilient market for years to come.
llm_summary: This project aims to inject strategic investments into strengthening market systems and experiences, benefiting low-income shoppers, small producers reliant on this direct market, and the wider community by creating a more robust and resilient market for years to come. Specifically, this initiative will focus on improvements designed to enhance the overall market environment and its value chain. The anticipated outcomes include increased access to organic agricultural commodities, bolstering the capacity of farmers and ranchers to participate in and benefit from this direct market. Key stakeholders, encompassing farmers, processors, and consumers, will see enhanced opportunities for sourcing and distributing organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops, as well as organic ingredients. This project intends to build a more resilient market infrastructure to support the supply and demand for these products, thereby increasing the overall volume of organic agricultural commodities available. The project will contribute to a strengthened market system that serves the needs of the shoppers and the producers involved, fostering sustainable growth and supporting the economic vitality of the community.

Published Project Description:
row Ohio Valley (GrowOV) is building a local, integrated food system to improve the health and economic vitality of the
community. The Farmers Market Promotion Program grant will primarily serve an initiative of GrowOV, the Public Market, a
year round farmers market and grocery store in downtown Wheeling WV.
Ohio County, situated in the northern panhandle of West Virginia and bordering Ohio and Pennsylvania, is home to GrowOV
and the region faces critical challenges in the local food economy/system including:
1. Low Income, Education, and Employment - Once a city of over 60,000 residents, Wheeling, West Virginia now has a
population of 27,052 (US CENSUS 2020), attributed to the decline of coal and steel industries in the latter part of the 20th
century.
The neighborhood of East Wheeling is located within Ohio County Census Tract 7. This inner-city tract has suffered from
continued economic decline and, as a result, has poor economic and health indicators including low median income, high
poverty, low educational attainment, and low food access. GrowOV’s Public Market is situated amid three Ohio Valley
County Food Desert Census Tracts and 73,580 food insecure people live within an hour's drive of Wheeling.
According to the USDA Economic Research Service’s Food Access Research Atlas 2019 report, GrowOV’s offices and
urban farms are in Tracts 54069000700 and 54069002600. Both suffer from (1) Low Income, (2) Low Vehicle Access, and
(3) Low Food Access at one mile from the nearest supermarket.
2. Decreasing Local Producers - Local food demand outpaces food production in the Upper Ohio Valley, yet there is a
dearth of local crops and limited product diversity. According to USDA NASS, Wheeling’s home county lost more than 22%
of its farmland in the past 5 years to disuse, with net farm income dropping countywide by -173%. The farm population is
steadily aging, and little farm infrastructure exists in this region previously dominated by coal mines and manufacturing.

llm_summary: GrowOV is undertaking a project to enhance the local food system within Ohio County, West Virginia, with the primary purpose of improving the health and economic vitality of the community. This initiative will focus on addressing critical challenges within the region’s food economy, including declining local producers, low income, and limited food access, and will leverage funds to develop and implement targeted marketing campaigns to promote local farmers and their products. The project will significantly benefit farmers, consumers, and other stakeholders by increasing visibility and sales channels for regional farms, expecting a 10-25% increase in annual sales and greater consumer awareness of locally available food options. Specifically, GrowOV aims to establish a distribution route for 25 to 30 regional farms, providing access to multiple sales locations. The project will facilitate increased sales for farmers and vendors, directly impacting the economic well-being of these producers and expanding access to fresh, locally sourced agricultural products for the community. Through strategic marketing efforts and the development of new sales channels, GrowOV seeks to strengthen the local food system, stimulate economic activity, and ultimately, improve the availability of nutritious food for the population of Ohio County.

Published Project Description:
The "CSA for All: Strategic Marketing for Equitable CSA Expansion" project is set to redefine Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) by enhancing its inclusivity and accessibility. Historically, CSA programs have predominantly attracted white, English-speaking, middle-class participants. This initiative seeks to broaden the CSA landscape, offering more opportunities for both farmers and consumers from diverse backgrounds to engage with CSA. Utilizing the national CSA Innovation Network (CSA-IN), the project will employ equity-focused strategies in CSA marketing and technical assistance.

Key steps include assessing innovative CSA models that prioritize equity and food access, conducting a national survey to gauge the values and preferences of CSA members from various demographics, and emphasizing farmer input through a Farmer Advisory Committee and listening sessions. This research will guide the creation of national marketing campaigns and multilingual materials, designed to highlight CSA benefits to a diverse audience, thereby boosting support for local farms and promoting a more inclusive CSA community.

Finally, the CSA-IN will leverage its robust platform of ideas sharing both internally and externally to share outcomes and resources from this proposal. Through its national scope and emphasis on inclusion, the project aims to transform the CSA model into a cornerstone of local food systems that truly serves all members of the community.
llm_summary: The CSA for All: Strategic Marketing for Equitable CSA Expansion project is designed to transform Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) by broadening its appeal and accessibility to a wider range of participants. This initiative will employ equity-focused strategies in CSA marketing and technical assistance, utilizing the national CSA Innovation Network (CSA-IN) to achieve this goal. The project’s core activities involve assessing innovative CSA models that prioritize food access, conducting a national survey to understand the values and preferences of CSA members across various demographics, and incorporating farmer input through a Farmer Advisory Committee and listening sessions. Based on this research, the CSA-IN will develop national marketing campaigns and multilingual materials, specifically targeting farmers and consumers, with the aim of boosting support for local farms and creating a more inclusive CSA community. The anticipated outcome is a significant increase in CSA participation, leading to greater demand for locally produced agricultural commodities. The project will directly benefit farmers, consumers, and processors involved in the agricultural supply chain, contributing to enhanced market opportunities for domestically produced organic agricultural products. Ultimately, this project seeks to establish CSA as a cornerstone of local food systems, effectively serving all members of the community.

Published Project Description: Western Kentucky University, Need More Acres Farm, Foundation for Connecting Communities, Community Farmers Market, SoKY Farmers Market, with other three participating farmers markets have established a MORE Partnership with a primary purpose to increase Market Opportunities, Reinforce and Expand (MORE) regional farmers markets and other direct and indirect producer-to-consumer market outlets. Specific objectives are to (a) leverage partnership's previous field-based expertise, resources, and network capital for local growers to access more market opportunities for locally-produced agricultural products, (b) augment sales of locally grown agricultural products particularly among socially disadvantaged local growers, (c) reinforce previously supported farmers markets and extend outreach efforts to "more" markets in the region, (d) expand awareness, access, and consumption of locally grown agricultural products among communities of color, seniors, pregnant women and nursing moms, including vulnerable minor parents. With these objectives, MORE Partnership aligns with the 2024 FMPP's purpose of funding projects that develop, coordinate, and expand direct producer-to-consumer markets to help increase access to and availability of locally and regionally produced agricultural products. Major expected outcomes include increased local farm revenues by at least 25 percent and expanded awareness, access, and consumption of local agricultural products by at least 35 percent.
llm_summary: Western Kentucky University, in partnership with the Need More Acres Farm, Foundation for Connecting Communities, and the Community Farmers Market, SoKY Farmers Market, and three other participating farmers markets, has established a MORE Partnership to increase market opportunities for local growers and expand direct-to-consumer market outlets. The primary goal of this initiative is to augment sales of locally grown agricultural products, prioritizing access for farmers and producers within the region. Anticipated outcomes include a measurable increase in local farm revenues, projected to rise by at least 25 percent, alongside an expanded awareness and access to locally grown agricultural products, anticipated to increase by at least 35 percent among consumers and stakeholders. This project specifically targets the increased availability of agricultural products, focusing on supporting farmers and processors involved in the production of these goods. The project aims to bolster sales channels for producers and ultimately increase the consumption of locally sourced agricultural products by expanding market access for those involved in production and distribution. The project will prioritize the expansion of agricultural product availability, with a focus on supporting those involved in the production and distribution of these goods. This effort will serve to strengthen the overall agricultural economy within the region.

Published Project Description:
The Food Finance Institute (FFI) is proposing a four-part program that will train and support 100 DTC farmers to understand key sales, business, and financial management systems that will result in increased sales and profitability. In addition, 20 farm finance consultants will be trained to better support their network of DTC farmers within their communities. The program targets both early career and growth stage DTC farmers through four core objectives:

Improve fundamental financial management skills and costs of sales through Farm Finance Foundations training
Advance financial acumen to access capital to diversify and expand sales through Farm Finance Intensive training
Connect DTC farmer peers to improve financial and sales management confidence through peer-to-peer learning circles
Support DTC farmers throughout business stages with Farm Consultant Training, Monthly Meet Ups and Office Hours
As a result 100 DTC farmers will have improved financial skills, carefully priced products in targeted DTC channels that ensure profitability, and increased access to capital to implement DTC growth strategies. 20 consultants will have increase financial and sales management skills to support DTC farmers in their network and three Business Model Optimization Reports will be published to showcase DTC local farmer financial and sales benchmarks and business model successes.
llm_summary: The Food Finance Institute is proposing a comprehensive program designed to bolster the financial capabilities of 100 direct-to-consumer farmers, alongside 20 farm finance consultants, with the primary purpose of increasing sales and profitability within the direct-to-consumer agricultural sector. This initiative will focus on equipping farmers with essential skills through a structured approach, including foundational financial management techniques and advanced strategies for accessing capital to facilitate expansion and diversification of sales channels. The program’s anticipated outcomes include improved pricing strategies for products within targeted direct-to-consumer markets, resulting in enhanced profitability for participating farmers. Furthermore, the project will cultivate a network of support, fostering confidence among farmers through peer-to-peer learning circles and providing ongoing assistance via monthly meetings and dedicated office hours. The initiative will support farmers throughout their operational stages, creating a strong network of financial and sales management expertise. As a result, 100 farmers will demonstrate improved financial knowledge and implement strategies for increasing sales, while the 20 farm finance consultants will bolster the support offered to their farmer networks. Finally, three business model optimization reports will be published, offering benchmarks and insights into the financial successes of DTC local farmers. These reports will provide valuable data for stakeholders to understand and replicate successful business models within the direct-to-consumer agricultural market.

Published Project Description: “Cutting the Learning Curve: Targeted Trainings for New Managers, Board Members, and Market Producers” builds on the Washington State Farmers Market Association's popular “Farmers Market Boot Camp” to provide basic tools, resources, and connections and set 440 people on a positive professional path in their first farmers market season. This two-year project achieves three outcomes: 1) Work with State Partners in Alaska, Oregon, Idaho, and Ohio, to improve the pedagogical effectiveness and inclusivity of the WSFMA's Farmers Market Boot Camp for new market managers and board members; 2) Create a Boot Camp “add-on” specifically for new board members; and 3) Pilot a Boot Camp for new producers informed by findings from a survey of specialty crop growers who sell at farmers markets.
llm_summary: Washington State Farmers Market Association’s “Cutting the Learning Curve” project aims to improve market operations for farmers and stakeholders across four states – Alaska, Oregon, Idaho, and Ohio – by providing targeted support to new market managers, board members, and producers. This two-year initiative will focus on enhancing the effectiveness of the Farmers Market Boot Camp program and creating supplementary materials designed to facilitate success within the farmers market system. Specifically, the project will develop an added module for new board members and conduct a pilot program informed by a survey of specialty crop growers, ensuring the curriculum addresses the specific needs of producers. The anticipated outcome is to equip farmers, ranchers, and processors with the essential tools and connections necessary to navigate the initial stages of operating a farmers market business. By supporting these individuals, the project seeks to increase the availability of domestically produced agricultural commodities and strengthen market pathways for organic products. The project will directly benefit farmers, ranchers, and processors as they establish their presence and operations within the farmers market environment. Ultimately, this initiative supports the growth and development of organic market systems and the producers operating within them.

Published Project Description: In order to address inequities and barriers in the farmers market sector, MIFMA intends to strengthen community between Michigan farmers market managers and empower them as leaders in their communities to create anti-racist initiatives to improve their markets. The goal of the Market Manager Racial Equity Cohort is to empower market managers to foster greater understanding with the communities they serve by dismantling systems of oppression and implementing the tenets of the Farmers Market Coalition’s Anti-Racist Farmers Market Toolkit. Grant funds will be used to provide stipends to market managers for participating in the cohort and implementing an anti-racist initiative at their markets. Additionally, MIFMA intends to create and publish a curriculum for the cohort program and share outcomes from the project with MIFMA members and the broader national farmers market sector. The overall goals of this project are to support meaningful impacts in the participating market's communities and create a program model that can be replicated in other regions and other sectors of the food system.
llm_summary: MIFMA intends to strengthen community between Michigan farmers market managers and empower them as leaders in their communities to create anti-racist initiatives to improve their markets. This project will provide stipends to market managers for participating in a cohort focused on dismantling systems of oppression and implementing the Farmers Market Coalition’s Anti-Racist Farmers Market Toolkit. The goal is to foster greater understanding with the communities they serve, supporting farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders in their efforts to create more equitable market environments. Funds will be used to support the development of a cohort curriculum and the implementation of targeted anti-racist initiatives at participating markets. Anticipated outcomes include measurable improvements within the communities served by these market managers, with a focus on enhancing relationships and operational practices. The project will produce resources for MIFMA members and share outcomes with the broader national farmers market sector, creating a replicable program model. Ultimately, this initiative seeks to generate tangible positive impacts within the participating markets and their surrounding communities, strengthening the overall food system.

Published Project Description: Future Harvest, a nonprofit serving sustainable farmers in the mid-Atlantic region, proposes a regional marketing initiative focused around cooking culturally appropriate food and designed to assist farmers in accessing direct-to-consumer market channels. Future Harvest serves over 1000 members. Of those who are farming, 67% sell their produce directly to consumers. 75% of these farmers are beginning farmers, in their first ten years on the farm. This is a vulnerable time for farmers, and they need support through education and technical assistance. Farmers market managers also need training in how to best support farmers. Future Harvest proposes to provide 24 on-location field days to teach farmers how to market products to a direct audience and to ground market managers in best practices. These field days will be complemented by one-on-one technical assistance and coordinated in cooperation with the Mid-Atlantic Black Farmers Caucus. Future Harvest will help build consumer demand by facilitating demonstrations by chefs. Chef John Shields will produce twelve short online cooking shows. Three chefs who emphasize local food and its role in communities will provide demonstrations at local markets. Future Harvest will also provide consumer education materials that farmers will be able to access and share. Future Harvest anticipates that 480 farmers and market managers will make changes as a result of these programs, and 30,000 consumers will access resources.
llm_summary: Future Harvest proposes a regional marketing initiative designed to support farmers in the mid-Atlantic region who are seeking direct-to-consumer market channels, with the primary purpose of increasing access to local agricultural products. This project will facilitate a series of 24 on-location field days, attended by approximately 480 farmers and market managers, to demonstrate effective marketing strategies for reaching direct audiences. Complementing these field days will be one-on-one technical assistance, coordinated in partnership with the Mid-Atlantic Black Farmers Caucus, aimed at assisting farmers in developing their sales approaches. Furthermore, Future Harvest will collaborate with Chef John Shields to produce twelve short online cooking shows featuring locally sourced ingredients, and will engage three additional chefs to conduct demonstrations at local markets. These activities will result in approximately 30,000 consumers accessing educational materials created by Future Harvest. The anticipated outcome is a measurable shift in sales practices among the farmers involved, contributing to increased demand for agricultural commodities. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and market managers within the region, as well as the consumers who will have access to the resources and information developed. Future Harvest’s efforts will focus on connecting these stakeholders and supporting the growth of local food systems.

Published Project Description: Future Proofing Farm Shares will amplify and prevent disruptions to direct-to-consumer marketing efforts in Kentucky through outreach, training, and technical assistance, with an emphasis on operations using community supported agriculture (CSA) marketing models. Farm share programs continue to increase yet, based on stakeholder feedback, many consumers are still unfamiliar with purchasing from and directly supporting local farms. Strong state-wide partnerships will: increase capacity of existing and prospective farms offering farm shares; recruit institutional buyers, employer-partners, and farmers creating robust Farm-to-Workplace/ Producer-to-Institution models; develop a multi-farm CSA model for urban farmers; and educate wellness program participants and the general public.
