Specifically, the project is expected to: provide technical assistance and training to more than 100 CSA operations, including development of at least 37 business plans; generate at least 3 market assessments, with 1 focused on growers in historically underserved areas; result in more than 125 collaborations within the local supply network; train 500 stakeholders on direct-to-consumer market channels; improve food safety knowledge of at least 100 farmers; and reach more than 400,000 consumers, educating them on purchasing local products. The project will increase competitiveness and resiliency of prospective, new, and experienced producers and improve access to locally-produced agricultural products.
llm_summary: Future Proofing Farm Shares is designed to amplify and mitigate disruptions to direct-to-consumer marketing efforts for Kentucky’s agricultural producers, with a particular focus on those utilizing Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) models. This project will increase the capacity of existing and prospective farms offering farm shares, alongside the recruitment of institutional buyers, employer-partners, and producers to establish robust Farm-to-Workplace/Producer-to-Institution models. A key component involves the development of a multi-farm CSA model for agricultural operations working in rural settings. Furthermore, the project will educate wellness program participants and the general public regarding the benefits of purchasing locally-sourced agricultural products. Anticipated outcomes include the creation of at least 37 business plans for over 100 CSA operations, the completion of three market assessments – one specifically analyzing growers in rural areas, and the facilitation of more than 125 collaborations within the local supply network. The project aims to reach more than 400,000 consumers, providing them with information about accessing and purchasing locally produced agricultural goods. The project will support farmers, ranchers, and processors seeking to enhance their market reach. The overall goal is to improve the competitiveness and resilience of agricultural producers while expanding access to locally-produced agricultural products. Through these efforts, the project seeks to bolster the agricultural sector and support the economic viability of farms throughout Kentucky.

Organizaton: Cornell Cooperative Extension Assoc. of St. Lawrence County
Published Project Description: This project reduces barriers for small farms and food entrepreneurs through three mutually beneficial initiatives: (1) offer a comprehensive food business incubator program across a tri-county region, (2) establish relationships with area retailers that improve the marketing channels for agricultural businesseses, and (3) boost visibility at the retail level about local purchasing. The proposed Kitchen Incubator is anchored by two shared-use kitchens: the Harvest Kitchen at the Extension Learning Farm and a burgeoning facility at Jefferson Community College. The program will be available to all farmers and food producers in northern New York. An exciting aspect of this Incubator is providing professional services to producers who have completed a critical mass of workshops. These entrepreneurs gain access to technical services from project collaborators, valued up to $3,000 per business, to improve their operations including website development, brand management, logo design, product labels, photography, and videography. The project will increase the quantity of local products in retail and restaurant locations with value chain coordination plus customized marketing. Technical assistance will benefit over 200 food producers and marketing will support 600 farms, retailers, and food businesses. Increased outreach to consumers will generate over two million impressions. At least 13 low income/access communities will benefit from targeted promotion.
llm_summary: This project aims to reduce barriers for small farms and food entrepreneurs across a tri-county region of northern New York through a multifaceted approach. The core of the initiative involves establishing a comprehensive food business incubator program, anchored by two shared-use kitchens – the Harvest Kitchen at the Extension Learning Farm and a new facility at Jefferson Community College – designed to support local producers. Anticipated outcomes include a significant increase in the quantity of local agricultural products available in retail and restaurant locations, facilitated through value chain coordination and customized marketing strategies. The project will directly support approximately 600 farms, retailers, and food businesses, with a targeted outreach effort projected to generate over two million impressions and benefit at least 13 low-income/access communities through focused promotional activities. This initiative seeks to improve operational efficiencies for food producers, offering access to professional services valued up to $3,000 per business, which may include website development, brand management, logo design, product labels, photography, and videography. Ultimately, the project intends to strengthen the local food system by connecting farmers with retail outlets and bolstering consumer awareness of locally sourced agricultural commodities. The project’s success will be measured by the increased visibility and market access for these stakeholders, with the potential to substantially enhance the volume of organically produced goods available within the region.

Published Project Description: Northeast Oklahoma City is known widely for negative statistics relating to health, food access and economic outcomes. The Eastside Fresh Market is a new food access point in Oklahoma City that was established to address the food access issues facing this community. A recent feasibility study conducted by OSU Extension was implemented to better understand the needs of this community. Hundreds of northeast Oklahoma City residents and multiple local food producers were surveyed to inform the development of the market. The Eastside Fresh Market concluded its second year in 2023 and is an established food access point for Northeast Oklahoma City residents, creating opportunities for area food producers. The market is fulfilling a community need by targeting an underserved three zip-code area and expanding opportunities for SNAP recipients and local producers. It has been communicated that there is still a need to support producers by connecting them with resources and specific training to market their producer-to-consumer enterprises. Also, existing and beginning farmers alike need support navigating the technical hurdles of sustaining their direct-to-consumer enterprises. Furthermore, there is a need to increase the capacity of the Eastside Fresh Market itself by expanding the customer base. This project addresses key producer needs through technical training and marketing support, and community needs by scaling up targeted marketing campaigns.
llm_summary: The Eastside Fresh Market’s purpose is to address critical food access challenges within Northeast Oklahoma City, a community facing significant statistics related to health, food availability, and economic outcomes. This project focuses on supporting farmers and producers by providing resources to facilitate direct-to-consumer enterprise development, which will expand market opportunities for local stakeholders. Specifically, the project will concentrate on bolstering the capacity of the market itself through targeted marketing campaigns aimed at increasing the customer base, alongside efforts to connect producers with relevant resources. The anticipated outcomes include a strengthened local food system, improved access to organic agricultural commodities for consumers, and increased sales for participating farmers and ranchers. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the residents of Northeast Oklahoma City, alongside the producers who supply the market with fresh goods. The project will aid those involved in the processing and distribution of agricultural products, ultimately contributing to a more robust local food supply chain. By expanding the market’s reach and supporting producers, the Eastside Fresh Market aims to stimulate economic activity within the community and provide a consistent source of locally-sourced agricultural products for the population.

Published Project Description:
This project will increase sales for Texas farmers and ranchers by increasing family engagement at farmers markets. A cohort of twelve Texas farmers markets will be trained in a peer-to-peer training model to create family engagement events intentionally focused on Texas-grown fruits and vegetables. The cohort will host 96 family engagement events with planning and design support from education specialists and trainers at the Texas Center for Local Food. Participating market managers will co- design events that fit their communities' strengths and needs. Localized outreach will be implemented in partnership with community organizations identified by market managers. Collaboration with community partners is an essential project component to strengthen the capacity of local food systems.

Project deliverables are (i) a toolkit of ten family engagement activities that increase local food sales, to be shared widely, (ii) a digital turnkey toolkit for other farmers markets to produce similar programming and secure local funding, and (iii) an online course on family engagement programming and customer service strategies for farmers markets and farmer vendors.

The project will directly benefit 111 farmers who vend at participating farmers markets. Short-term outcomes include increased sales of fruit and vegetables during family engagement events. Project beneficiaries will experience sustained higher sales as evidenced by an increase in dollars.
llm_summary: The Texas Center for Local Food is undertaking a project to increase sales for Texas farmers and ranchers by fostering greater family engagement at farmers markets. This initiative will involve the implementation of a peer-to-peer training model for twelve Texas farmers markets, resulting in the hosting of ninety-six family engagement events. Market managers will collaborate with education specialists and trainers to co-design events specifically tailored to the strengths and needs of their communities, focusing on the promotion of Texas-grown fruits and vegetables. A key deliverable of this project is a toolkit comprising ten family engagement activities designed to boost local food sales, alongside a digital toolkit to facilitate the replication of this programming by other farmers markets and secure local funding. Furthermore, the project will produce an online course addressing family engagement programming and customer service strategies for farmers markets and vendor participants. The anticipated outcome is a sustained increase in sales among the participating farmers and ranchers, measured by an increase in the total dollars generated during these engagement events. Specifically, one hundred eleven farmers who vend at participating farmers markets will directly benefit from this initiative. The project seeks to strengthen the capacity of local food systems by encouraging collaboration between market managers and community organizations. The intended beneficiaries encompass farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the local food system.

Published Project Description:
"The International Rescue Committee in Charlottesville’s New Roots Refugee Farmer and Consumer Market Expansion
Project will build direct-to-consumer marketing capacity of 30 beginning refugee and immigrant farmers, improve operations
of Charlottesville’s most rapidly expanding farmers market, and improve food security among Low-Income /Low-Access
consumers. Multi-sector stakeholders and project beneficiaries will include 30 beginning refugee and immigrant farmers, 87
producers and value-added vendors from 16 Central Virginia counties, and 1,200 LI/LA refugee and immigrant consumers
over the 3-year project. The IRC will engage Market Central, the non-profit farmers market manager of two weekly farmers
markets, as a project partner and sub-recipient; Market Central staff and board will improve and sustain the operations of
the markets which currently serve as critical venues for direct-to-consumer marketing in Charlottesville, reaching an average
of 3,000 customers each week year-round. Investment in training and technical assistance, and strategies to stabilize and
expand the local food economy will yield a 100% increase in sales among participating refugee and immigrant farmers over
the life of the project, 10% increase in sales revenue across local and value-added producers at Market Central farmers
markets, and accompanying improvements to food safety practices, infrastructure, and regulatory compliance by
participating producers and programs. Finally, the IRC will utilize grassroots community outreach to bolster the utilization of
public benefits by LI and LA consumers."
llm_summary: The International Rescue Committee’s New Roots Refugee Farmer and Consumer Market Expansion Project aims to bolster the local food economy by developing direct-to-consumer marketing capabilities for 30 beginning refugee and immigrant farmers, while simultaneously improving the operations of Charlottesville’s farmers markets and enhancing food security for Low-Income/Low-Access consumers. This project will support the expansion of Market Central, the non-profit farmers market manager, and will provide resources to 87 producers and value-added vendors across 16 Central Virginia counties. The anticipated outcomes include a 100% increase in sales among participating farmers, a 10% increase in sales revenue for local and value-added producers at Market Central farmers markets, and improvements to food safety practices, infrastructure, and regulatory compliance for all involved producers. The project will directly benefit approximately 1,200 Low-Income/Low-Access consumers, as well as farmers, ranchers, and processors within the region. The International Rescue Committee will leverage grassroots community outreach to increase the utilization of public benefits by these consumers. The project focuses on supporting the creation of new market channels for organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops, contributing to the overall expansion of the local food system. This initiative seeks to strengthen the supply chains for these agricultural products and to establish more accessible routes to market for the participating farmers and producers. The International Rescue Committee anticipates this work will positively impact the economic viability of numerous agricultural businesses and will ensure a greater availability of locally sourced food products for the consumer population.

Organizaton: Northeast Organic Farming Association of Vermont
Published Project Description: This project is to enhance our statewide online producer directory; To provide training and professional development for farmers market leaders, focusing on market viability and inclusion; And to provide customized marketing technical assistance and professional development to strengthen direct marketing farms and promote climate resilience.
llm_summary: This project aims to enhance our statewide online producer directory to better connect farmers with consumers and facilitate the growth of direct marketing operations. The core focus is on providing specialized technical assistance to strengthen direct marketing farms, with an emphasis on promoting robust market viability for agricultural products. Specifically, the project will deliver customized marketing support to farmers and ranchers, supporting the development of accessible markets for a range of agricultural commodities, including organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops. This support will bolster the ability of processors and producers to effectively distribute these goods to consumers. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened network of direct marketing farms, leading to increased access to domestically produced agricultural products. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the direct marketing of agricultural commodities. By providing targeted assistance, the project seeks to optimize the availability and demand for these goods within the statewide market. Ultimately, the project intends to support the operational success of numerous farms and related businesses, ensuring a reliable supply of agricultural products to consumers.

Organizaton: West Virginia National Guard Foundation, Inc.
Published Project Description:
The West Virginia National Guard Foundation and Patriot Guardens will focus project efforts on reaching veteran farmers
with the intention of reaching new markets for their whole farm products, value-added products or through the addition of
agritourism/ecotourism operations on the property. During the project, educational programming will be developed and
delivered at three primary locations: Base Innovations Small Business Center in Charleston, WV, Patriot Apple Project in
Summersville, WV and the Patriot Guardens Urban Farm in Dunbar, WV. Each of these locations represent areas which
have been deemed food insecure, but also offer opportunities to reach direct-to-consumer markets in the local areas. Patriot
Guardens staff will reach well over 150 individuals through education and on-farm technical assistance, the vast majority of
which will seek to find new market opportunities such as farmers markets, restaurants and Community Support Agriculture
to sell their products.
Patriot Guardens will seek to work primarily with military veterans, actively serving military and military family members such
as spouses and children as they look to start or expand agricultural operations in the state. Most of these military connected
individuals will be members of the West Virginia National Guard, however service members from all branches and
affiliations are welcome to participate.
llm_summary: The West Virginia National Guard Foundation and Patriot Guardens are undertaking a project focused on assisting veteran farmers in West Virginia by facilitating the expansion of their agricultural operations and the creation of new market pathways for their products. This initiative will provide technical assistance and educational programming to farmers, ranchers, and processors, aiming to connect them with direct-to-consumer markets such as farmers markets and Community Supported Agriculture programs. The project will occur at three key locations: Base Innovations Small Business Center in Charleston, WV, the Patriot Apple Project in Summersville, WV, and the Patriot Guardens Urban Farm in Dunbar, WV, all of which represent areas with potential for increased agricultural activity. The primary goal is to support over 150 veteran farmers, including members of the West Virginia National Guard and service members from all branches, as they seek to establish or grow their agricultural ventures. This support will concentrate on establishing channels for the sale of farm products, value-added products, and potentially through agritourism operations. The anticipated outcome is to strengthen the agricultural sector within West Virginia by supporting the economic viability of veteran-owned farms and increasing the availability of locally produced agricultural commodities to consumers. The project will prioritize assistance to farmers seeking to address specific market needs, especially for organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, and organic fibers, supporting the growth of these commodities within the state. Ultimately, the project aims to empower these farmers to improve their operational efficiency and increase their market reach, contributing to a more robust and resilient agricultural economy.

Published Project Description:
Small and beginning farmers in West Virginia face significant challenges in achieving profitability due to small-scale
operations, limited market access, and the rural nature of many communities. This project aims to address these challenges
by piloting a marketing and education initiative across three West Virginia counties (Pocahontas, Nicholas, and Fayette).
The project will focus on developing a living-wage pricing list and marketing toolkit for fresh produce, educating farmers on
fair pricing strategies, launching branding and marketing campaigns to educate consumers, and increasing access to local
foods, especially for vulnerable populations like seniors and participants in nutrition assistance programs.
Led by High Rocks Educational Corporation, an award-winning leader in transforming the lives of young people in West
Virginia, the project leverages the organization's mission to educate, empower, and inspire. High Rocks Educational
Corporation operates the second-largest AmeriCorps program in the state and three youth social enterprises, providing
young people with opportunities to earn while learning key personal and professional development skills and industry best
practices. The organization’s impact on local communities is profound, making it an ideal leader for this initiative.
In partnership with Five Rivers Farmer Cooperative, Coalfield Development’s Refresh Appalachia, WV Food and Farm
Coalition, and Fayette County Schools, the project will collect data, provide training, pilot new food access markets, and
engage with industry stakeholders. Key activities include creating a cost-tracking tool, developing a "Living Wage for
Appalachian Farmers" brand and certification, training farmers, and conducting consumer education campaigns.
By promoting fair pricing and increasing market opportunities, the project aims to create a sustainable and equitable local
food system that ensures living wages for Appalachian farmers and enhances food security for local communities. The
project will leverage data collection, stakeholder engagement, and targeted marketing to achieve its objectives and set the
stage for broader implementation across the state.
llm_summary: High Rocks Educational Corporation is undertaking a vital project to address the challenges faced by small and beginning farmers in West Virginia, aiming to establish a sustainable and equitable local food system. This initiative will focus on developing a living-wage pricing list and a marketing toolkit for fresh produce, alongside launching targeted branding and marketing campaigns to educate consumers and increase access to local foods, specifically for vulnerable populations such as farmers and those participating in nutrition assistance programs. The project will also involve the creation of a cost-tracking tool to support farmers in managing their operations effectively. Anticipated outcomes include increased market opportunities for farmers and enhanced food security within the three pilot counties – Pocahontas, Nicholas, and Fayette – as well as the development of a “Living Wage for Appalachian Farmers” brand and certification. Key stakeholders, including Five Rivers Farmer Cooperative, Coalfield Development’s Refresh Appalachia, and the WV Food and Farm Coalition, will collaborate to gather data and engage with industry stakeholders. The project intends to improve the viability of local food production and distribution, creating a system where farmers can achieve fair compensation for their goods. This project will ultimately benefit farmers and consumers alike by fostering a stronger, more resilient local food economy.

Published Project Description:
This project seeks to increase market opportunities and sales for direct-market farmers by providing training and technical
assistance in marketing and business planning; boosting customer demand through consumer-facing events and strategic
social media campaigns; and increasing farmers’ direct sales to independent grocers by conducting outreach to grocers and
farmers, offering marketing incentives to the grocers and facilitating connections. This work will be carried out in western
Virginia and central Arkansas, two regions where there is a young but growing local food movement and CNG has robust
collaborators. In Virginia, the Virginia Association for Biological Farming will carry out much of the project work, including
organizing consumer-facing events featuring the importance of local food and ecological farming practices. The project
aims to bolster consumers' appreciation for ecological certifications used by direct-market farmers, to help shore up the
value of this marketing tool. As a result of this project, 480 farmers will receive marketing and business development training
through online courses and conference workshops, and 66 farmers will increase sales by the end of the project period. At
least ten farmers markets will receive marketing support via our social media campaigns carried out with collaborators local
to these markets. At least 22 independent grocers will meaningfully increase the share of fresh produce sold that comes
from local farms.
llm_summary: This project seeks to expand market opportunities and sales for direct-market farmers in western Virginia and central Arkansas, focusing on bolstering consumer demand and increasing direct sales to independent grocers. The initiative will support approximately 480 farmers through access to marketing and business development resources, including online courses and conference workshops, alongside efforts to improve the value of ecological certifications utilized by these farmers. Anticipated outcomes include a measurable increase in sales for participating farmers, with a target of 66 farmers achieving enhanced sales figures by the end of the project period, and a significant shift in purchasing habits among consumers. Furthermore, the project aims to connect at least 22 independent grocers to source a greater share of fresh produce directly from local farms. The project will provide marketing support to at least ten farmers markets through strategic social media campaigns conducted in collaboration with local stakeholders. The overall goal is to strengthen the local food movement in these regions by building relationships between producers and retail outlets. Successful implementation will benefit farmers, consumers seeking fresh agricultural products, and independent grocers looking to expand their offerings with locally sourced items. This will also support processors and other related businesses within the agricultural supply chain, fostering a more robust regional food system.

Published Project Description: The project aims to empower UConn Extension's regional marketing campaign in Northeastern Connecticut (NECT), with a focus on increasing access to farms and farmers markets among SNAP participants. Through strategic media efforts and collaboration with an emerging regional food hub, the project will also help farms reach new customers via an online marketplace.
llm_summary: UConn Extension’s regional marketing campaign in Northeastern Connecticut aims to increase access to farms and farmers markets among SNAP participants, establishing a strategic approach to expanding market reach for regional agricultural producers. This project will focus on bolstering the capacity of local farms to connect with new customers through a targeted media strategy and a collaborative effort with an emerging regional food hub, facilitating the development of an online marketplace for farm products. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened network of producers and consumers, leading to increased sales and broadened market access for farmers and ranchers within the region. Specifically, the project will support the creation of a digital platform to enhance the visibility and sale of locally grown products directly to consumers. Through this initiative, stakeholders, including farmers, processors, and consumers, will benefit from enhanced access to fresh agricultural commodities. The project’s success will be measured by the increased volume of goods sold through the online marketplace and the overall growth in participation at farmers markets within the target area. Ultimately, the project will support the viability of regional farms and strengthen the local food system by providing new pathways to market and fostering stronger relationships between producers and consumers seeking high-quality agricultural products.

Published Project Description: Cornell's Agriculture Marketing Research Program will increase sales of local foods at farmers markets (FMs) with an approach using analysis of FM vendors' customer spending data obtained from Point-of-Sale (POS) software. POS data are paired with Rapid Market Assessment (RMA) consumer surveys in 3 focus regions of New York and Pennsylvania. We utilize vendor and local demographics to understand shopper and vendor diversity dynamics, vendor sales performance, and identify opportunities for vendors and FM Managers (FMMs) to make FMs a more inclusive environment. We compare individual (vendor and FM) and aggregate results to identify practical marketing practices to increase access to and sales of locally grown foods. In addition to marketing techniques informed by participant data, we incorporate recommendations from the Farmers Market Coalition's Anti-Racist Toolkit; thus addressing implicit bias commonly found in FM culture and communications and working to remove barriers that discourage a broad diversity of consumers and vendors. These efforts result in data-informed recommendations to farmer vendors and FMMs working together to create a welcoming shopping environment. Capitalizing on our team of experts from Penn State, Cornell, and the farmer and FMM communities, we extend the benefits of the project to additional audiences through presentations and publications, including a 6-week Direct Marketing Farmer Training Course and a 1-day NY-PA Direct Marketing Conference.
llm_summary: Cornell’s Agriculture Marketing Research Program is undertaking a project to increase sales of locally grown foods at farmers markets within specific regions of New York and Pennsylvania. This initiative will utilize analysis of Point-of-Sale (POS) data collected from farmers market vendors alongside Rapid Market Assessment (RMA) consumer surveys in three designated areas. The project’s goal is to identify practical marketing practices that can enhance access to and sales volume for locally produced agricultural commodities among farmers and consumers. Researchers will examine vendor and local demographic information to understand shopper and vendor dynamics and pinpoint opportunities for improvement within the farmers market environment. The research will compare individual and aggregate results to formulate recommendations for both farmer vendors and farmers market managers. These recommendations will be centered on creating a welcoming shopping environment and promoting the increased consumption of locally sourced foods. The anticipated outcomes include a better understanding of consumer behavior and actionable strategies for vendors to boost sales. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the local food system. Ultimately, the project seeks to improve market access and sales for locally grown agricultural products.

Published Project Description: The Central Wisconsin Farmers Market Collaborative (CWFMC) is a community-led initiative that has been assessing needs & building partnerships to address food equity & improve low income  access at Farmers Markets (FM).Central Wisconsin is predominantly rural; there are just over a dozen markets serving about 350,000 people in the five counties in our project area; spanning close to 5 thousand total square miles. These markets have some limits that this project will help address: few have a paid market manager; less than half redeem food assistance benefits; none offer consistent double-your-dollar incentives for benefit use. FM also lack the capacity to engage the community, grow their customer base, & support new or marginalized farmers. With many barriers to technology, including limited broadband internet access, only a small fraction of our market vendors utilize electronic/mobile payment services, especially among Amish/Mennonite, non-English speaking vendors, & farmers with limited income. Research clearly shows that Central Wisconsin farmers & FM need technical & educational support to: expand & diversify their customers & vendors; adopt emerging electronic & mobile sales technologies; improve outreach to & accessibility for food assistance recipients; develop business plans that leverage local partnerships; & implement strategic communication plans. The CWFMC, formed during the LFPP planning grant, is now poised to implement change
llm_summary: The Central Wisconsin Farmers Market Collaborative is undertaking a project to address critical needs and enhance access to farmers markets within Central Wisconsin, a region characterized by its expansive rural geography encompassing nearly 5,000 square miles across five counties and serving approximately 350,000 residents. This initiative aims to improve food equity and support farmers, consumers, and processors by expanding market capacity and fostering strategic partnerships. The project will focus on several key areas, including increasing the utilization of food assistance benefits at markets, implementing consistent double-your-dollar incentives, and facilitating the adoption of electronic and mobile payment services among vendors, particularly those with limited income or who speak languages other than English. Furthermore, the Collaborative seeks to bolster community engagement, develop robust business plans, and create effective communication strategies to support farmers and stimulate market growth. The project anticipates outcomes such as an increase in market vendor participation, expanded customer base engagement, and improved access to organic grains and livestock feed. Ultimately, the CWFMC intends to positively impact farmers and consumers in Central Wisconsin by creating and strengthening local food systems and improving market accessibility for all stakeholders.

Published Project Description: Farm Generations Cooperative will collaborate with each of our thirteen farmer member-owners to create a promotional plan for their farm's direct-to-consumer sales in the 2025 season, to be implemented in our cooperatively owned marketing platform, GrownBy. We will measure the effectiveness of each farm's promotional campaign using GrownBy sales and customer data, focusing on the return-on-investment realized from each distinct promotional campaign.
llm_summary: Farm Generations Cooperative will develop tailored promotional plans for its thirteen farmer member-owners to maximize direct-to-consumer sales within the 2025 growing season, leveraging the cooperative’s marketing platform, GrownBy. The core objective of this project is to refine marketing strategies for each farm, specifically focused on increasing sales volume and return on investment through the GrownBy platform. These promotional campaigns will be directly measured using sales data and customer information captured within GrownBy, allowing for a detailed assessment of the effectiveness of each farm’s approach. Anticipated outcomes include increased revenue streams for the participating farmers and enhanced market access for their products. The primary beneficiaries of this initiative will be the farmers themselves, alongside the consumers who purchase these farm-fresh goods. Furthermore, processors and other stakeholders involved in the distribution chain will also benefit from the expanded market reach. This project will result in improved sales figures for the farms and a strengthened position for the cooperative within the market. The success of this project will contribute to securing a larger volume of organic agricultural commodities for sale.

Published Project Description: Good Food Farmers Network (GFFN) is an online sales platform established to expand market access for small-scale and beginning farmers. GFFN collaborates with 25 producers and serves 275 households. This project will support a Member Engagement Campaign to increase annual revenue by 30%. This campaign will increase direct payments to participating producers by $115,000 annually and increase GFFN net revenue by $45,000 annually of which approximately $35,000 per year will be allocated for ongoing support of the part- time Member Engagement Coordinator position (initially established through this grant and matching funds) and $10,000 per year towards ongoing generation of print materials and other collateral. To achieve this 30% increase in annual revenue, this project has two key objectives: (1) to increase average transaction value by 15% or $12 per order, and (2) to increase average weekly member order rate by 15%, from 52% to 60% participation. To achieve these objectives, this grant will support developing and disseminating weekly online and social media content promoting available products and educating members on how to use available foods emphasizing quick and convenient meals; print materials reinforcing the online messaging; promotional merchandise; and events that increase member connection to GFFN farms and regional agriculture.
llm_summary: Good Food Farmers Network (GFFN) is undertaking a Member Engagement Campaign with the primary purpose of increasing annual revenue by 30%, which will result in an additional $115,000 in direct payments to participating farmers and a projected increase in GFFN net revenue of $45,000 annually. This project will specifically support the development and distribution of weekly online and social media content designed to promote available products and educate members on utilizing available foods, emphasizing quick and convenient meal options. Furthermore, the project will create print materials reinforcing the online messaging, produce promotional merchandise, and host events aimed at increasing member connections to GFFN farms and regional agriculture. The anticipated outcomes include a 15% rise in average transaction value, equating to $12 per order, and a 15% increase in the average weekly member order rate, rising from 52% to 60%. These changes are intended to benefit farmers by boosting their annual income and enhancing the operational capacity of GFFN. The project will allocate approximately $35,000 per year towards ongoing support of the part-time Member Engagement Coordinator position and $10,000 per year towards the generation of print materials and other supporting collateral. Ultimately, this initiative will benefit farmers, consumers, ranchers, and other stakeholders by expanding market access for locally produced agricultural commodities and fostering a stronger connection between producers and the individuals purchasing their goods. This project supports the development of new and expanded organic markets for commodities such as grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, and organic legumes.

Published Project Description:
The City of South Bend's Engagement and Economic Empowerment team hosts the Linden Avenue Farmers Market (LAFM), a seasonal farmers market and family-friendly entertainment venue that runs once per month from June through October. Now in its fourth year, LAFM continues to partner with local and regional small- to medium-scale agricultural producers, prepared food artisans, and food security partners to improve food systems in low-income/low-access neighborhoods that have been dis-invested throughout their history. In this proposal, the City will expand its support to activate local farmers by providing market access opportunities through the LAFM and its wraparound supports: vendors will have access to market equipment such as tents, tables, and electrical accessories. In addition, LAFM offers staff and volunteer assistance with pre-market engagement, and volunteer assistance with day-of logistics.

Promoting small-scale farmers markets while simultaneously addressing food security requires a comprehensive approach with innovative mechanisms for vendor recruitment, community outreach, and mission-driven programming; expanding vendor incentives and offerings will bolster the quality and quantity of regional farming and improve consumer access to healthy food systems.
llm_summary: The City of South Bend’s Engagement and Economic Empowerment team is undertaking a project to expand the Linden Avenue Farmers Market (LAFM), a seasonal market operating monthly from June through October, to bolster local agricultural production and enhance access to healthy food. This initiative focuses on providing market access opportunities for regional farmers, ranchers, and food processors, alongside support services including market equipment such as tents, tables, and electrical accessories, and staff/volunteer assistance with pre-market engagement and day-of logistics. The anticipated outcome of this project is an increase in the quantity and quality of locally produced agricultural commodities, specifically targeting organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops currently unavailable in organic form. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, food processors, and other stakeholders involved in the regional agricultural supply chain. The City of South Bend aims to improve consumer access to these products, contributing to a stronger local food system. By providing direct market access, the LAFM will facilitate the sale of agricultural goods and support the economic viability of regional producers, ultimately strengthening the supply of organic ingredients available to the community.

Published Project Description:
The Healthy By Design (HBD) coalition is dedicated to fostering resilient local food systems that promote community health and well-being. Through the USDA FMPP Turnkey Marketing and Promotion grant, we aim to increase vendor recruitment and expand customer reach using a targeted marketing campaign. The proposal aims to strengthen vendor capacity and participation through innovative retention-focused marketing tools that correct market attendance misconceptions and increase market visibility beyond the immediate neighborhood. The marketing campaign will involve identifying strategic marketing opportunities. Proposed partners will include a TBD-determined sub-awardee to support community-wide marketing efforts. This project supports the Healthy People 2030 objective to improve health by promoting healthy eating and making nutritious foods readily available.

The weekly market is held at South Park located in the South Side of Billings; a neighborhood that is a USDA defined food desert having lost its only grocery store in 2013. Potential, and existing, market vendors have expressed several barriers to regular participation, including limited customer base beyond the neighborhood, and lack of multiple anchor vendors to attract customers. Previous FMPP grants underscore a track record of impactful initiatives. By expanding market attendance and vendor participation, the project aims to enhance the economic and health outcomes of the broader community.
llm_summary: The Healthy By Design (HBD) coalition is undertaking a project to strengthen local food systems and promote community well-being, specifically through a targeted marketing campaign supported by a USDA FMPP Turnkey Marketing and Promotion grant. The primary goal of this initiative is to increase vendor recruitment and expand customer reach at the weekly market held in South Park, located in the South Side of Billings, a region recognized as a USDA-defined food desert due to the loss of its original grocery store in 2013. The project will focus on addressing barriers faced by existing and potential market vendors, including limited customer bases and a lack of anchor vendors, aiming to correct market attendance misconceptions and substantially elevate market visibility beyond the immediate neighborhood. This expansion seeks to bolster vendor capacity and participation, ultimately enhancing economic and health outcomes for the broader community, including farmers, ranchers, and processors involved in the local food supply chain. Anticipated outcomes include increased market attendance, greater vendor engagement, and a strengthened local food system. The project’s intended beneficiaries are the farmers and ranchers providing agricultural products, as well as the consumers seeking access to fresh food options. By increasing the availability of locally sourced goods, the project aims to positively impact the health and economic vitality of the Billings community. The HBD coalition recognizes the critical need to expand market paths for organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes and other rotational crops, and organic ingredients.

Published Project Description: Despite an increase in population and a need for easy access to fresh produce, Nevada remains far behind other regions of the United States in the production, adoption, and development of a local food industry. The City of Henderson is committed to creating a healthy, livable, and sustainable community as identified in the City's Henderson Strong Comprehensive Plan and 2024-2027 Strategic Plan. The City of Henderson's Premier Harvest Farmers Market Program aims to support the growth, coordination, and expansion of the City's existing Farmers Market Program. The purpose of this project is to increase access to healthy foods to populations in low income/low access census tracts, especially seniors, low income, and SNAP eligible populations. This project will seek out the development, implementation, and evaluation of a Farmers Market Feasibility Study to identify ways to promote and market existing and new farmers markets. Through a public-private partnership, the city will work with contracted farmers market operator(s) to enhance existing markets, increase the frequency the markets are offered, and expand to new locations. Along with these efforts, marketing materials and supplies will be purchased with the goal to boost foot traffic and awareness of the various markets, and healthy foods will be more accessible to a wider population of the city.
llm_summary: The City of Henderson is undertaking a project to increase access to fresh produce within the city, aligning with its commitment to creating a healthy, livable, and sustainable community as outlined in its strategic plans. This project focuses on the development, implementation, and evaluation of a Farmers Market Feasibility Study, designed to identify strategies for promoting and expanding existing and potential farmers markets throughout the region. As part of this initiative, the City will collaborate with contracted farmers market operators to enhance current market operations, potentially increasing the frequency of market offerings and exploring new locations to better serve the population. The project will involve the purchase of marketing materials and supplies aimed at boosting foot traffic and awareness of the available markets, making fresh food more accessible to a wider range of consumers and supporting local farmers. The anticipated outcome is to improve access to healthy food options for populations in low-income/low-access census tracts, with a particular focus on supporting seniors, low-income individuals, and those utilizing SNAP benefits. These efforts will benefit stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of agricultural products. Ultimately, this project intends to strengthen local food systems and provide greater access to fresh produce for the community.

Published Project Description: Through the following initiatives, Portland Farmers Market aims to: 1) Increase accessibility and awareness of farmers markets as direct-to-consumer sales opportunities for historically under-served farmers and ranchers, 2) Provide trainings to enhance vendors’ success in diverse marketplaces, and 3) Increase the number of vendors at Lents International and King Farmers Markets.  Vendor Recruitment: We will implement a new digital recruitment strategy, host prospective vendor info sessions, simplify and translate application & informational materials to improve access for vendors with limited English proficiency, and collaborate with organizations serving new farmers/ ranchers to present workshops on developing a farmers market enterprise.  Vendor Trainings & Peer-to-Peer Workshops: Partnering with OFMA and expert instructors, we will present a training series on enhancing vendor success and customer service in diverse marketplaces.  We will also convene Peer-to-Peer Workshops where vendors share knowledge and discuss common challenges in a panel-style format.  New Vendor Incubation: Incubator booths at Lents International and King Farmers Markets will enable new farmers to experience selling at market and learn from experts, in collaboration with Outgrowing Hunger and Headwaters Incubator Farm.  These initiatives will engage 248 current and 80 prospective vendors (duplicated) in trainings & workshops, and 24 unique vendors in new direct-to-consumer sales at farmers markets.
llm_summary: Portland Farmers Market aims to expand access to farmers markets as direct-to-consumer sales opportunities for farmers and ranchers, providing resources to enhance vendor success within various marketplaces, and increasing the number of vendors at the Lents International and King Farmers Markets. This project will facilitate the establishment of incubator booths at these markets, enabling new farmers to gain experience in direct sales and learn from expert collaboration with Outgrowing Hunger and Headwaters Incubator Farm. The anticipated outcome includes the engagement of 248 current and 80 prospective vendors, resulting in 24 unique vendors participating in direct-to-consumer sales. Specifically, Portland Farmers Market intends to support farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders in expanding their market reach and increasing the availability of domestically produced agricultural products. The project will focus on building capacity within the agricultural sector, promoting the production and distribution of organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops. By creating these opportunities, Portland Farmers Market seeks to improve the flow of agricultural commodities from production to consumption, supporting the success of agricultural businesses and the overall health of the local food system. Ultimately, this project will benefit farmers, ranchers, and consumers alike by fostering a more robust and accessible market for locally sourced agricultural products.

Published Project Description:
Food For All! increases locally grown produce sales at two existing
farmers markets, and tests two new markets for economic sustainability,
by using digital and print media. “Farmers Forks” hires farmers to give
cooking demonstrations and teach dishes to make with their crops. Twice
annual focus groups gather input on materials, strategies and
programming.
Deliverables include quarterly print campaigns in Edible South Florida
Magazine, ongoing banners and social media posts by Edible, monthly
print ads in The Biscayne Times, ongoing promotion on Yelp, a weekly
produced e-newsletter to over 3500 people, 3 social media posts and
stories weekly to over 10,000 people, 3 mailings of postcards to 10,000
people in market vicinity and targeted neighborhoods, and 2 annual
Freebee vehicle wraps running for 2 months, including postcard delivery to
all riders.
Outcomes expected: 10% increase in sales of produce by farms at existing
markets. At two new markets, at least four farms will find new
opportunities, with 25% sales growth in year two. 30 consumers will
engage per “Farmers Forks” event, 75% reporting learning new recipes
and 50% will try a local ingredient.
Collaborators include media Edible South Florida Magazine, Freebee, and
Biscayne Times. Site locations are Legion Park, Vizcaya Museum &
Gardens Trust, and Tropical Audubon Society. Beneficiaries are farms
with an increase in direct sales: Tiny, French, Paradise, Regener8,
Samsara, Under the Vine, Intergro, LNB and others.
llm_summary: Food For All! aims to increase locally grown produce sales at two existing farmers markets and test two new markets for economic sustainability utilizing digital and print media. This project will execute a comprehensive marketing strategy encompassing quarterly print campaigns in Edible South Florida Magazine, ongoing banners and social media posts by Edible, monthly print ads in The Biscayne Times, ongoing promotion on Yelp, a weekly produced e-newsletter to over 3500 people, and three social media posts and stories weekly to over 10,000 people. Furthermore, the initiative includes three mailings of postcards to 10,000 people in market vicinity and targeted neighborhoods, alongside two annual Freebee vehicle wraps running for two months, including postcard delivery to all riders. The anticipated outcomes include a 10% increase in sales of produce by farms at existing markets, with at least four farms finding new opportunities at the two new markets achieving 25% sales growth in year two.  Approximately 30 consumers will engage per “Farmers Forks” event, with 75% reporting learning new recipes and 50% indicating they will try a local ingredient. The primary beneficiaries of this project are the farmers – Tiny, French, Paradise, Regener8, Samsara, Under the Vine, Intergro, LNB, and others – alongside consumers and stakeholders involved in the markets. The project seeks to bolster the reach and sales of locally grown produce, creating new avenues for market access for participating farms and enhancing the availability of fresh agricultural products for the community.  The anticipated results will significantly benefit farmers by increasing direct sales and provide consumers with more opportunities to access and purchase locally sourced produce.

Published Project Description:
Farm to School Frederick is dedicated to enhancing marketing and promotional endeavors for five Farmers Markets situated in low-income and low-access areas across Frederick County. Despite these markets having a strong foundation, there's a pressing need to increase access to and availability of locally produced agricultural products to families of color and those facing challenges in accessing nutritious foods, especially fresh fruits and vegetables.

The project includes a comprehensive needs assessment, the development of a dynamic marketing strategy and the creation of diverse promotional materials to attract a wide-ranging customer base. Collaboration plays a central role, with Farm to School Frederick already fostering robust partnerships with farmers, the Office of Agriculture, community organizations, and Frederick County Public Schools. Leveraging its established position as a trusted community partner, the impact of the initiatives will be amplified.

Farmer Market Managers and a marketing firm will provide guidance and produce professional content. The project will actively engage communities through interviews, focus groups, and surveys to gather insights for improving market accessibility and increasing farmer sales. Data collection and analysis will evaluate the campaign's impact on attendance, revenue, and sales, ultimately aiming to enhance the visibility and prosperity of Farmers Markets while fostering a more inclusive local food system.
llm_summary: Farm to School Frederick is undertaking a vital project to enhance marketing and promotional efforts for five Farmers Markets located in low-income and low-access areas throughout Frederick County. The primary purpose of this initiative is to increase access to locally produced agricultural products for consumers, farmers, and processors, specifically targeting families and those facing challenges in obtaining nutritious foods, particularly fresh fruits and vegetables. This project will involve the development of a dynamic marketing strategy and the creation of a range of promotional materials designed to attract a broad customer base to the markets. Collaboration with existing partners, including farmers, the Office of Agriculture, community organizations, and Frederick County Public Schools, will be central to the project’s success, leveraging Farm to School Frederick’s established position as a trusted community resource. Data collection and analysis will be employed to evaluate the campaign’s impact on attendance and sales, with the goal of improving market visibility and fostering the prosperity of these markets. The anticipated outcomes include increased revenue for participating farmers and greater access to fresh agricultural products for the communities served. Ultimately, this project seeks to strengthen the local food system and ensure greater availability of regional agricultural commodities.

Published Project Description: The Farmer Forward Marketing and Promotions Project seeks to address critical challenges faced by small-scale agricultural producers in Clark County, Washington by developing and implementing a strategic marketing and promotions plan. Project deliverables include 1) a Brand and Positioning Strategy Document to refine VFM's overall promotion of local farms, 2) signage for the Farmers Market and Clark County farm booths to elevate the markets visibility and highlight information about growers such as distance from market and growing practices, 3) a Farm Finder Website Tool that provides detailed farmer information and helps consumers navigate and inform purchase decisions, and 4) improved social media promotions through enhanced photography and a film series captured through farm visits and grower interviews.
llm_summary: The Farmer Forward Marketing and Promotions Project seeks to significantly enhance the operational capabilities of small-scale agricultural producers in Clark County, Washington, by implementing a comprehensive strategic marketing and promotions plan designed to address critical market access challenges. This project will deliver four key components: a detailed Brand and Positioning Strategy Document to refine the promotional efforts of local farms, eye-catching signage for the Farmers Market and Clark County farm booths to markedly increase market visibility and communicate grower information, including distances from the market and specific growing practices, a user-friendly Farm Finder Website Tool enabling consumers to easily navigate and inform purchase decisions based on detailed farmer information, and enhanced social media promotions through professional photography and a compelling film series created via on-farm visits and grower interviews. The anticipated outcome of this initiative is a strengthened market presence for Clark County’s agricultural producers, leading to increased sales and improved relationships with consumers. Specifically, farmers, ranchers, and processors within the county will benefit from increased market opportunities. The project will support consumers in their search for locally sourced agricultural products. Ultimately, the project aims to create a more robust and accessible market for agricultural commodities within Clark County, supporting the economic viability of local farming operations and fostering direct connections between producers and those seeking high-quality food products.

Published Project Description: Growing Hope will support the viability of local farmers and food businesses through heightened awareness and visibility of the Ypsilanti Farmers Markets, coinciding with relocating to a vibrant downtown location in 2025. To meet this objective, we will execute a dynamic marketing plan. Deliverables include a comprehensive marketing strategy and tailored promotional materials to emphasize the market's new location and local food options.  Expected outcomes include increased attendance, sales, utilization of food assistance, and heightened awareness about the market's relocation and offerings. Additionally, transitioning the farmers market to a downtown location will expand the space for vendors by 50%, increasing the number of participating vendors, particularly among marginalized groups.  This project will benefit farmers, food businesses, Ypsilanti residents, and the downtown Ypsilanti business district. Each party participates by fostering community engagement and economic growth while prioritizing access to fresh, local, culturally relevant food. Our key partner, Taste the Local Difference, will play a crucial role by leveraging their expertise in local food marketing to maximize the project's impact and reach during the relocation process. Our strategic collaborations and community engagements will ensure that the project simultaneously boosts market visibility, ensures a seamless transition, promotes local food systems, and addresses food access challenges.
llm_summary: Growing Hope’s project aims to bolster the viability of local farmers and food businesses through heightened awareness and visibility of the Ypsilanti Farmers Markets, coinciding with a relocation to a vibrant downtown location in 2025. This initiative will execute a dynamic marketing plan, resulting in the creation of a comprehensive strategy and tailored promotional materials that emphasize the market’s new location and the variety of local food options available. The anticipated outcomes include increased attendance at the market, enhanced sales figures, greater utilization of food assistance programs, and heightened awareness regarding the market’s transition and offerings. Specifically, the project will expand the market’s physical space by 50%, allowing for an increase in the number of participating vendors, particularly among farmers and food businesses. These expanded operations will benefit farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders by providing increased market access for their products. The project intends to strengthen the local food system while addressing the need for additional market paths for organic grains and livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes and other rotational crops, and organic ingredients. The primary beneficiaries of this project include the farmers and food businesses themselves, as well as Ypsilanti residents seeking access to fresh, local food options. Strong collaborations with Taste the Local Difference will ensure a seamless market transition and maximize the project’s impact, supporting the growth of the market and the overall food system.

Published Project Description: The Franklin County Farmers Market (FCFM) has been an active presence and sometimes the only source of fresh food in downtown Frankfort, KY, for over 20 years. Through the successful implementation of a 2017 FMPP project, the market launched an online ordering platform, deliveries to workplaces, a sliding-scale CSA-style market, and expanded food access programs and community engagement. FCFM successfully continued and expanded these programs after grant funding ended. As a result, market sales increased from $217,000 in 2017 to over $600,000 in 2023, and producer participation doubled from 31 in 2017 to 65 in 2023. Now, the market is being relocated to make way for new development. FCFM is partnering with the City of Frankfort to identify a new downtown location and build a new pavilion that offers expanded opportunities for continued success. Through this project, FCFM will collaborate with the Kentucky Center for Agriculture and Rural Development and a range of community partners to develop and implement a marketing plan to increase community awareness of and engagement with the market and ensure a successful transition to a new site. The market also aims to increase producer sales by 10%, develop and expand the online sales program, and partner with the Friends of the Market to expand fresh food access programs to ensure that FCFM continues to provide a vibrant and reliable sales opportunity for local farmers and a source of fresh food for the community.
llm_summary: The Franklin County Farmers Market is undertaking a comprehensive project to establish a new, expanded market presence in downtown Frankfort, Kentucky, following a relocation necessitated by new development. This project involves securing a suitable new location and constructing a pavilion designed to enhance the market’s capacity and offerings. Anticipated outcomes include a 10% increase in sales generated by participating farmers, the development and expansion of an online sales program, and the continued operation of a vibrant market that serves as a reliable sales opportunity for local producers. The Franklin County Farmers Market aims to bolster the existing market’s success and expand its reach to benefit farmers, ranchers, and processors within the region. Furthermore, the project seeks to broaden access to fresh food for the community, and the market’s success will directly support stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of agricultural commodities. The project will ensure the continuation of the market’s role as a central hub for local food, and its expanded operations will contribute to the economic vitality of Frankfort. This market’s long-term stability will benefit the entire community, providing access to locally sourced food products.

Published Project Description: NCFW will develop, design, implement, and evaluate a marketing plan to support local direct product-to- consumer markets to increase access to and availability of locally and regionally produced agricultural products. This plan will focus on how each of our producer-centered programs can effectively engage their appropriate audience, expand their audience to historically under-served populations through language and accessibility improvements, and increase partnership engagement to develop a stronger network for cross- promotion.  Project deliverables include a marketing plan with audience-specific organizational branding, collaborative marketing tools, cohesive messaging strategies and marketing guidelines for product development. Design and purchase of digital and printed marketing materials will include a content calendar tool and plan, email marketing plan, print materials, and Spanish-language materials. Evaluation of marketing and promotion activities will include collection and synthesis of internal and external data via forms, surveys, and conversations with focus audiences to inform on-going work.  Expected outcomes include a 15% increase in local producer-to-consumer market engagement, access points, education, access to new operational methods, and producer participation and sales.  Intended beneficiaries are NCFW producers, consumers, community members, and partners - including Astoria Sunday Market and Astoria Co-op.
llm_summary: NCFW will develop and implement a comprehensive marketing plan focused on boosting engagement within local direct-to-consumer agricultural markets, ultimately increasing access to regionally produced goods. This project will encompass the creation of audience-specific branding, collaborative marketing tools, and cohesive messaging strategies, alongside the design and purchase of digital and printed marketing materials, including a content calendar tool and plan, email marketing plan, and Spanish-language materials. The anticipated outcomes include a 15% increase in participation and sales among NCFW producers, alongside expanded access points for consumers and stakeholders. Specifically, the project aims to strengthen connections between farmers, ranchers, processors, and retailers, creating a more robust network for cross-promotion and market development. The primary beneficiaries of this initiative include NCFW producers, consumers seeking fresh agricultural products, and key partners such as the Astoria Sunday Market and Astoria Co-op. This project will also ensure access to new operational methods for producers. Through the development of targeted marketing materials and strategic partnerships, NCFW intends to cultivate a stronger market presence for locally sourced agricultural products, ultimately supporting the increased availability of regionally produced goods for all stakeholders involved.

Published Project Description: The project aims to enhance awareness of the Camarillo Farmer's Market and promote equitable access to its offerings for our Spanish-speaking and Filipino communities. Our strategy involves implementing a loyalty program, advertising in newspapers, amplifying social media presence, hosting interactive workshops, and distributing awareness-raising postcards to nearby residents. We anticipate that these efforts will lead to a more diverse audience and increased attendance, benefiting both attendees and vendors alike. Key partners for this initiative include our vendors and the City of Camarillo.
llm_summary: The Camarillo Farmer’s Market project aims to elevate awareness and expand access to its offerings for the Spanish-speaking and Filipino communities within Camarillo. This initiative will be achieved through a multi-faceted approach, including the implementation of a loyalty program designed to encourage repeat visits, strategic advertising campaigns in local newspapers to reach a broad consumer base, a significantly amplified social media presence to connect directly with potential attendees, and the hosting of interactive workshops focused on showcasing the market’s products. Furthermore, the project will involve the distribution of awareness-raising postcards to nearby residents, facilitating increased engagement with the market. Anticipated outcomes include a broadened audience base and heightened attendance, directly benefiting both the farmers who supply the market and the consumers who purchase its products. The project will prioritize the availability of a wider selection of organic agricultural commodities, seeking to support farmers, ranchers, and processors. By expanding market access, the project seeks to improve the distribution channels for organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops. This expanded market will provide greater opportunities for these stakeholders to connect with consumers seeking fresh, locally-sourced agricultural products. The overall goal is to enhance the reach and impact of the Camarillo Farmer’s Market, supporting its continued growth and contributing to a more robust local agricultural economy.

Published Project Description: “Find Fresh Erie County” will address food insecurity and promote awareness of fresh food sources by facilitating access to fresh produce for underserved communities located in areas of concentrated poverty with limited access to fresh locally or regionally grown food in Erie County, NY
llm_summary: “Find Fresh Erie County” is a project designed to address food insecurity and promote awareness of fresh food sources within Erie County, NY. This initiative will facilitate access to fresh produce for communities experiencing concentrated poverty and limited access to locally or regionally grown food. The project anticipates increasing the availability of fresh produce to farmers, ranchers, and other stakeholders who currently face challenges in accessing markets for their goods. The anticipated outcome is a strengthened local food system, providing consumers with greater access to fresh food options. Specifically, the project focuses on supporting the production, aggregation, and distribution of fresh produce, aiming to improve the supply chain for farmers and ranchers. The project will support the development of market pathways for fresh food within Erie County, ultimately benefiting the communities experiencing limited access to this vital resource. The project intends to increase the overall supply of fresh food available to consumers in these areas, contributing to improved nutrition and a more robust local food system.

Published Project Description: Montavilla Farmers Market (MFM) in Portland, Oregon provides a year-round, vibrant marketplace, hosting an average of 55 vendors and serving 2,000 customers per week. MFM is the largest year-round farmers market serving Southeast Portland, currently operating twice a month during the winter season (January–April).  Our winter season has the greatest opportunity for growth: customer counts and sales are slow, physical space is available for additional vendors, and winter vegetables remain under-appreciated. With the expertise of marketing and communications professionals, MFM will assess our community’s needs, create and implement a customized winter season marketing plan, and evaluate the effectiveness of our work.  A marketing plan will increase customer counts by educating, reminding, and inspiring our community. Communications will include promoting farmer stories focusing on winter food production, the sustainability and economic benefits of shopping at farmers markets, and the unique winter produce available. Implementation of a professional plan will result in our abundant summer shoppers attending our market during the winter months (summer sees on average 156% more shoppers), increasing direct producer-to-consumer sales.  This project will excite our community to support local farmers year-round. The winter farmers market season will thrive, extending an essential fresh food access point for consumers and increasing sales opportunities for small producers.
llm_summary: Montavilla Farmers Market (MFM) seeks to significantly expand its reach and impact during the winter season, with the primary purpose of increasing customer counts and sales by implementing a targeted marketing plan. This project will focus on enhancing the market’s ability to attract more shoppers, particularly during the traditionally slower winter months, and will achieve this through strategic communications that highlight the value of purchasing local produce. Specifically, MFM will develop and execute a comprehensive marketing strategy designed to educate, remind, and inspire the community to support local farmers and access the unique winter vegetables available. The anticipated outcome is a substantial increase in shopper traffic, aiming to replicate the substantial summer shopper volume – approximately 156% higher – during the winter season, thereby boosting direct sales between producers and consumers. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers, ranchers, and processors who rely on market access for their products, and the consumers who benefit from access to fresh, locally grown agricultural commodities. Furthermore, the expanded winter market will provide a vital access point for consumers seeking fresh food options. The Montavilla Farmers Market intends to cultivate greater demand for locally sourced agricultural products, directly supporting the economic viability of small producers and strengthening the local food system.

Published Project Description: This project builds capacity for Sustainable Solano to engage in effective marketing strategies reaching both new and existing market segments in Solano County to support local/regional farmers. Sustainable Solano will partner with UC Davis to develop, test and revise a comprehensive marketing plan, with a special focus on engaging consumer groups with underdeveloped preferences for and limited access to locally grown/produced foods. This builds on existing work to increase consumer awareness around local food, including a proposed “5 by ‘35” campaign to get 5% of food dollars spent on Solano County goods by 2035 and supporting initiatives to sustain and support agriculture in the county. Project activities include literature review; development research; engaging a local marketing agency as advisor; outreach to project beneficiaries and diverse community segments; conducting focus groups and lab-in-the-field experiments that test marketing messages. Additional outcomes and beneficiaries are increased market access and revenue opportunities for small and medium-sized Solano farmers and food producers; increased awareness of healthy, local food choices across diverse populations and retail environments; increased resilience of the local food system; increased capacity of Sustainable Solano to reach diverse audiences; and meaningful learning opportunities for UC Davis students.
llm_summary: Sustainable Solano will develop a comprehensive marketing plan to support local/regional farmers within Solano County, with the primary purpose of increasing market access and revenue opportunities for farmers and food producers. This project will involve a collaborative effort with UC Davis to create and refine this plan, specifically focusing on engaging consumer groups who have limited preferences for and access to locally grown/produced foods. The project activities encompass a literature review, research development, and the engagement of a local marketing agency as an advisor, alongside extensive outreach to project beneficiaries and a broad range of community segments. Key components include conducting focus groups and lab-in-the-field experiments to rigorously test marketing messages. Anticipated outcomes include increased market access and revenue opportunities for farmers and food producers, alongside heightened awareness of healthy food choices across retail environments. Furthermore, the project aims to bolster the resilience of the local food system. The primary beneficiaries of this project are farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders involved in the production and distribution of agricultural commodities. Ultimately, Sustainable Solano intends to significantly increase the availability and demand for locally produced goods, contributing to a strengthened local food system and enhanced economic opportunities for agricultural businesses within Solano County.

Published Project Description: The Hudson Valley Market Vendor Training and Support project will support 150 small Hudson Valley businesses by providing workshops, one-on-one marketing support, mentorships, and a resource library. The project aims to develop a strong sense of community among vendors, increase vendor sales and overall success, attract new vendors to our market, welcome new customers to our markets, and grow our local economy.
llm_summary: The Hudson Valley Market Vendor Support project is designed to bolster 150 small businesses within the Hudson Valley region by providing targeted support to enhance their sales and overall success. This initiative will focus on cultivating a strong sense of community among market vendors, attracting new customers to the markets, and ultimately contributing to the growth of the local economy. The project will provide direct assistance to farmers, ranchers, and processors, aiming to increase the availability of organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops currently lacking organic forms.
