By facilitating connections and offering resources, the project anticipates increased sales volume for participating businesses and a greater consumer base for locally sourced organic products. The primary beneficiaries of this effort include the small business owners, agricultural producers, and the consumers who seek access to fresh, organic goods. This project intends to strengthen local market dynamics and promote the growth of the organic agricultural sector within the Hudson Valley community.

Published Project Description: Capital Roots' Food Access Programs support new market opportunities for Upstate NY farm operations by cultivating retail spaces in the Region's disadvantaged neighborhoods.
llm_summary: Capital Roots’ Food Access Programs are designed to create new retail spaces within disadvantaged neighborhoods throughout Upstate New York, directly supporting farm operations and expanding market opportunities for agricultural commodities. This initiative focuses on establishing connections between regional farmers and consumers seeking organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops – items currently unavailable in organic form. The anticipated outcome of this project is an increased availability of domestically produced organic agricultural products, thereby benefiting farmers, ranchers, and processors who are involved in the production and distribution of these commodities. Specifically, Capital Roots aims to build retail spaces strategically located within these neighborhoods, facilitating direct access for consumers to purchase these organic products. The primary beneficiaries of this project include farmers seeking expanded market channels and processors who require organic ingredients to fulfill their operations. Furthermore, the project intends to strengthen the overall supply chain for organic agricultural goods, ultimately increasing the volume of domestically produced organic commodities reaching the market. Capital Roots’ efforts contribute to creating more viable pathways for agricultural businesses and ensuring a consistent supply of organic ingredients for the region’s food system.

Published Project Description: Rurally located and beginning producers, farmers markets and on-farm agritourism opportunities are abundant in Western Montana, but regional strategic marketing and promotion plans and resources that drive both local residents and tourists from over-visited more densely populated cities and towns to more rural farm, ranch and farmers market locations are lacking. This project includes two marketing and promotion campaigns that connect rural and beginning farmers and ranchers across five Western MT Counties to individual consumers, tourists and wholesale buyers located in more densely populated hub locations. This project includes activities in all five Turnkey Marketing Objectives and works to increase producer engagement and promotion within a diverse array of market opportunities centered on both individual consumers and wholesale buyers of local food.  Local Food & Farm Adventure Passports, Guides and Maps will be used as the foundational components of planning regionally specific marketing campaigns that are fun, interactive and breathe new life into experiencing Montana's local agriculture in the Flathead, Missoula and Bitterroot Valleys. The Partners on the Plate component brings together wholesale buyers and producers to forge new connections that result in increased market location opportunities and helps producers market their farm/ranch offerings in a way that maximizes networking time and quality.
llm_summary: This project aims to enhance regional marketing and promotion efforts for beginning farmers and ranchers across five Western Montana counties, connecting them with consumers, tourists, and wholesale buyers located in more densely populated areas. The core of this initiative involves the development and implementation of two marketing and promotion campaigns, utilizing fun and interactive components such as Local Food & Farm Adventure Passports, Guides, and Maps to revitalize the experience of Montana’s local agriculture within the Flathead, Missoula, and Bitterroot Valleys. Furthermore, a “Partners on the Plate” component will be established to facilitate direct connections between wholesale buyers and producers, generating increased opportunities for market locations and optimizing networking time for producers. Anticipated outcomes include increased engagement from farmers and ranchers seeking to expand their reach and promote their farm/ranch offerings. The primary beneficiaries of this project are farmers, ranchers, processors, and other stakeholders within the five targeted Western Montana counties. By facilitating stronger connections between producers and markets, this project will contribute to the growth of local food systems and the increased availability of Montana agricultural products. The project’s success will be measured by the expansion of market locations and the volume of sales generated through these new connections, ultimately supporting the economic viability of local agricultural operations.

Published Project Description: This project seeks to reinvigorate numerous local food outlets that have struggled to be consistent in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic and related economic impacts. We will create and implement a marketing plan for our four outdoor summer farmers’ markets which will include a number of targeted digital and print marketing efforts.
llm_summary: AMS seeks to revitalize local food outlets impacted by recent economic challenges, focusing on implementing a comprehensive marketing plan for four outdoor summer farmers’ markets. This project will establish targeted digital and print marketing efforts designed to increase the visibility and appeal of these markets to consumers and stakeholders. The anticipated outcome of this initiative is a sustained increase in the volume of organic agricultural commodities sold through these markets, benefiting farmers, ranchers, and processors involved in the production and distribution of these goods. Specifically, AMS will concentrate on promoting the availability of organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops—items currently limited in organic form within the local market. Through these marketing activities, AMS expects to bolster market access for producers of these commodities, ultimately supporting the growth and stability of the local organic agricultural sector and ensuring a broader range of organic products are accessible to consumers. This project will directly contribute to the increased demand for domestically produced organic agricultural products, addressing the need for additional market pathways for these goods.

Organizaton: Cornell Cooperative Extension of Nassau County
Published Project Description: The goal of CCE Nassau’s Eat Local - Shop Local Promotion Program is to spread awareness of the benefits eating and shopping locally-grown and sourced foods has on individuals, local businesses, and communities, and will serve to support the promotion of the CCE Nassau Farmers Market, as well as other avenues for Long Islanders to access farm fresh and local food and goods.
llm_summary: CCE Nassau’s Eat Local - Shop Local Promotion Program aims to increase awareness of the advantages associated with consuming and purchasing locally grown and sourced foods, directly supporting the CCE Nassau Farmers Market and other avenues for Long Islanders to access fresh, local food and goods. This initiative will focus on facilitating the acquisition of organic grains, livestock feed, organic dairy, organic fibers, organic legumes, and other rotational crops, effectively expanding market channels for these commodities. The anticipated outcome of this program is a strengthened local food system that benefits farmers, processors, and stakeholders throughout Long Island by improving access to locally produced organic agricultural products. Specifically, the program intends to bolster the availability of these commodities, thereby enhancing the capacity of local farmers and ranchers to meet consumer demand. The primary beneficiaries of this promotion include the farmers and ranchers who supply these goods, as well as the consumers who seek access to fresh, locally-sourced food options. Ultimately, the project seeks to create a more robust and accessible local food system, promoting the consumption of organic agricultural products and supporting the growth of the CCE Nassau Farmers Market and related distribution networks.
